question: What is stated about selection of chairs/directors?
answer:
According to Article 9.15 of the Collective Agreement:

1. The term of office for Chairs/Directors shall normally be for three (3) years, renewable by Department/School selection per Article 9.15 – Selection of Chairs/Directors (Source: Article 9.20.1).
2. If a strong consensus emerges for the selection of one candidate at step 4 of the procedure, the Selection Committee may proceed directly to step 8 of the procedure (Source: Article 9.15.14).
3. If at least two Members object to the abbreviated selection process, the Committee shall follow the full procedure (Source: Article 9.15.14).
4. The Chair/Director shall be a tenured or probationary Member of faculty (Source: Article 9.15.12).
5. Any outside appointment for a Chair/Director shall be made in accordance with Article 5.20 – Appointment and Renewal (Source: Articles 9.15.12 and 9.15.13).

Additionally, Article 9.20 states:

1. Should Chairs/Directors not be able to carry out their duties for four (4) months or less, they shall make provision for the take-over of their duties in consultation with the Department/School and Dean/University Librarian (Source: Article 9.20.2).
2. If the absence is for a period longer than four (4) months, the Chairs/Directors shall relinquish her/his title and a new Chair/Director shall be selected according to the procedures set out in Article 9.15 – Selection of Chairs/Directors (Source: Article 9.20.3).

question: What is stated about personnel files?
answer:
According to Article 21 of the Collective Agreement 2015-2018, there are several key points stated about personnel files:

1. Official personnel files of a member shall be kept by the President and are the property of the Employer (p. 42).
2. Members have the right to examine all of their personnel files upon making prior arrangements to do so (Article 21.02).
3. Material in the files that is to be held confidential according to the provisions of this Agreement will be removed from the files prior to inspection by the member, and an inventory of this material will be provided to the member (Article 21.02).
4. The Employer agrees not to use any unofficial personnel information for any official purposes, including disciplinary measures (p. 42).
5. There are two types of files: active files and archival files. Active files contain only information allowed under Article 21, while archival files contain material that has been banned for use in subsequent proceedings but is required for other matters (Article 18.01).

Additionally, according to Article 5.70 of the Collective Agreement:

6. Members have the right to examine all of their personnel files during normal business hours after notice in writing, and an inventory of confidential material will be provided to the member (Article 5.70.2).
7. Members may request a copy of their personnel file, excluding confidential material, which will be provided within five working days at no charge (Article 5.70.3).
8. No anonymous material concerning any Member shall be kept by the Employer for inclusion in the Member's personnel file (Article 5.70.4).
9. Members have the right to have their files supplemented or corrected, and may request the removal of false, irrelevant, or unsubstantiated material from their personnel file (Article 5.70.5).

answer:

question: What does the agreement say about arbitration procedure?
answer:
According to Article 11.15 of the Collective Agreement (pages 201-246), here is what the agreement says about arbitration procedure:

1. Failing settlement and/or timely response under the grievance procedure, any grievance may be submitted to arbitration (11.15.1(a)).
2. A written request for arbitration must be received within 30 working days after the decision of the Vice President, Academic or the Union President under Step 2 – Formal Grievance Procedure (11.15.1(a)). If no request is made, the grievance shall be deemed to have been abandoned.
3. When a Party requests arbitration, it must make such request in writing and appoint a nominee within 30 working days (11.15.1(b)).
4. The other Party must also appoint its nominee within 15 working days of receiving the request for arbitration (11.15.1(b)). If this Party fails to do so, the Minister of Labour for Ontario shall have the power to make such appointment.
5. The two nominees shall attempt to agree upon a chairperson of the Arbitration Board (11.15.1(b)).
6. The decision of the Arbitrator will be final and binding upon the Parties hereto and the Member(s) concerned, except as provided by law (36.05).
7. Each Party will share equally the fees and expenses of the Arbitrator (36.06).
8. Time limits set out in the Grievance and Arbitration Procedures are mandatory, and failure to comply strictly with such time limits shall result in the grievance being deemed to have been abandoned, unless otherwise agreed by the Parties (36.07).

question: What are the rules concerning sabbatical leaves?
answer:
According to Article 22.07 of the Collective Agreement, here are the rules concerning sabbatical leaves:

* A sabbatical leave is for a period of 12 months, commencing on July 1, or for 6 months commencing on July 1 or January 1 [Source: Collective Agreement, page not specified (assuming it's Article 22.07)].
* No portion of the academic year in which a sabbatical leave is taken shall count toward the years of eligibility entitlement [Source: Collective Agreement, page not specified (assuming it's Article 22.07)].
* A sabbatical leave includes the appropriate vacation entitlement proportional to the length of the leave [Source: Collective Agreement, page not specified (assuming it's Article 22.07)].

Additionally, according to other articles in the Collective Agreement:

* When a Member takes a sabbatical leave after three years, all accumulated years of eligibility are exhausted except as otherwise provided for by this Collective Agreement [Source: Collective Agreement, page not specified (assuming it's Article 5.20)].
* Members with tenure can be granted a sabbatical after three years, but only if they have met the eligibility criteria [Source: Collective Agreement, page not specified (assuming it's Article 5.20)].

Finally, according to Article 12.20:

* Immediately following the completion of a sabbatical leave, the member is required to return to the University for a period equal to the length of the leave taken, or to satisfy some other arrangement that is mutually acceptable to the member and the Employer [Source: Collective Agreement, page not specified (assuming it's Article 12.20)].

Please note that I assumed the source document name as "Collective Agreement" without specifying the page number for each claim, as the context provided does not include the page numbers.

question: What does the collective agreement provide regarding physical education facilities?
answer:
According to Article 4.56 (page 98) of the Collective Agreement 2002-2005, all full-time Members, their spouses and dependants are eligible for free Physical Education Centre membership subject to the payment of an annual service fee and lockerette rental fee as established by the Division of Physical Education.

question: What is stated about sabbatical leave?
answer:
According to Article 22.07 in the collective agreement, a sabbatical leave can last for either:

* 12 months, commencing on July 1 (page 123)
* 6 months, commencing on July 1 or January 1 (page 123)

Additionally, no portion of the academic year in which a sabbatical leave is taken shall count toward the years of eligibility entitlement pursuant to Article 22.02.

A sabbatical leave includes the accumulation of vacation entitlement proportional to the length of the leave (Article 12.12, page 123).

Furthermore, a member on sabbatical leave shall continue to be covered by the University's group benefit plans, and the Employer shall continue its normal contributions toward the premium costs for such plans (Article 12.13, page 123).

question: How is employer's retirement addressed in the collective agreement?
answer:
According to Article 8.45.4, Employer contributions to the Retirement Plan shall be at least the amount required to fund current service costs and any unfunded liabilities and Solvency liabilities, or reduced by 7.5%, whichever is greater, in accordance with the Pension Benefits Act and regulations thereunder based upon actuarial valuations for the Retirement Plan that the Employer files with the Financial Services Commission of Ontario. Additionally, Article 2.55.1 states that notices required to be given under the provisions of this Collective Agreement shall be in writing and shall be sufficient either if addressed to the appropriate recipient and sent by campus mail or Canada Post, or if delivered to the appropriate recipient personally with a signed receipt required. This implies that the Employer must also follow similar notice procedures for retirement-related matters.

It's worth noting that Article 16 of the Collective Agreement 2011-14 provides details on Special Voluntary Early Retirement, including benefits and pension contributions during this period. (Source: Collective Agreement 2011-14, page 212)

Overall, the collective agreement outlines specific requirements and procedures for Employer contributions to the Retirement Plan, as well as notice procedures related to retirement matters.

question: According to the agreement, what applies to selection of chairs/directors?
answer:
According to Article 9.15 - Selection of Chairs/Directors, a normal term of office for Chairs/Directors is three (3) years, renewable by Department/School selection per Article 9.15 (Source: Collective Agreement, Article 9.20.1).

In case the Chair/Director cannot carry out their duties for four (4) months or less, they shall make provision for the take-over of their duties in consultation with the Department/School and Dean/University Librarian (Source: Collective Agreement, Article 9.20.2). If the absence is for a period longer than four months, the Chair/Director shall relinquish her/his title and a new Chair/Director shall be selected according to the procedures set out in Article 9.15 - Selection of Chairs/Directors (Source: Collective Agreement, Article 9.20.3).

Additionally, Article 9.25 outlines specific entitlements for Chairs/Directors, including a six (6) credit teaching load reduction and an annual stipend based on the number of full-time teaching/librarian Members in the Department/School and other full-time equivalent employees reporting to the Chair/Director (Source: Collective Agreement, Articles 9.25.1-2).

question: What is stated about loan reimbursement?

According to Article 31 - MOVING EXPENSES, Collective Agreement 2012-2016 (page 45), moving expenses paid to a new Member constitute a loan made by the University. The loan will be retired when the Member has completed three (3) years of continuous service with the University.

Additionally, if the beneficiary leaves the University before completing three (3) years of continuous service for personal or disciplinary reasons, they must reimburse the University for a pro-rated portion of the loan. This is stated in Article 31 - MOVING EXPENSES, Collective Agreement 2012-2016 (page 45).

Furthermore, this condition is consistent with other collective agreements that mention moving expenses as a loan:

* Article 4.55 - MOVING EXPENSES, Collective Agreement 2002-2005 (pages 96-97)
* A.09 MOVING EXPENSES, Collective Agreement 2015-2018 (page 57)

In all these documents, it is stated that moving expenses paid to a new Member will constitute a loan made by the University, and the conditions for loan repayment are similar.

question: What is stated about academic workload?
answer:
According to Article 5.40 of the collective agreement, the academic workload of a full-time member during the academic year includes:

* Teaching/professional librarianship/archives management, including the supervision of graduate and undergraduate students (40%); [Source: Collective Agreement, Article 5.40.2(a)]

* University governance, administrative duties, and other contributions to the University (20%) [Source: Collective Agreement, Article 5.40.2(c)]

Additionally, the normal guideline for the distribution of workload among these three main components is 40% teaching/professional librarianship/archives management, 40% scholarly activity, and 20% university governance, administrative duties, and other contributions to the University. [Source: Collective Agreement, Article 5.40.2(c)]

question: What does the collective agreement provide regarding disciplinary measures?
answer:
According to the collective agreement, disciplinary measures must be just and reasonable (Source: Collective Agreement, page not specified). The "cause" for disciplinary measures includes:

* Serious unprofessional behaviour (5.75.2(a))
* Failure to comply with any of the provisions of this Collective Agreement, minor technical violations excepted (5.75.2(b))

The only formal "Disciplinary Measures" that may be taken by the Employer against a Member are:

* A letter of reprimand, specifying the grounds and adding this reprimand to the personnel file (5.75.3(a))
 
Additionally, there is also another section mentioning:
When an alleged breach of discipline is made against a member, the parties shall attempt to resolve the matter through a discussion between the Dean/University Librarian, the member, and their union representative (Source: Collective Agreement, page not specified).

question: How is study leaves addressed in the collective agreement?
answer:
According to Article 7.30 of the Collective Agreement, Study Leaves are addressed as follows:

1. Eligibility: A study leave may be granted to a tenured, probationary or Master Lecturer Member (page 34 of LUFA-H Collective Agreement 2016-2020) after two years of full-time service.
2. Purpose: The purpose of the study leave is to upgrade academic qualifications, normally through the attainment of a higher degree or some other equivalent acceptable to the University and the Department/School (Article 7.30 - STUDY LEAVES).
3. Maximum length: The maximum length of leaves to be granted during a Member's academic career shall normally not exceed two years (Article 7.30 - STUDY LEAVES).
4. Application procedure: Applications for study leave shall be made by September 30 in consultation with the Department/School through the Chair/Director and the appropriate Dean/University Librarian to the Vice-President, Academic and Provost (Article 7.30.2(a)).
5. Decision-making process: The Vice-President, Academic and Provost shall verify the status of the application in relation to the relevant University policies and the financial implications of the leave, and make a decision, a copy of which shall be sent to the Member (Article 7.30.2(b)).
6. Salary: A Member on study leave shall receive 30% of the Member's salary to a maximum of $40,000 (LUFA-H Collective Agreement 2016-2020, page 34).

question: How is laurentian university research addressed in the collective agreement?
answer:
Laurentian University's research activities are addressed in Articles 6.10-6.45 of the Collective Agreement 2017-2020.

According to Article 6.15, the Office of Research Services (ORS) shall provide resources to assist all Members in preparing grant applications, with the goal of promoting research activities and creativity at Laurentian University, both nationally and internationally.

The ORS is also responsible for communicating the composition and terms of reference of the selection committee for internally or externally-funded grant applications on its website. The selection committee includes Faculty Members elected by Senate, unless doing so would prevent the application from proceeding.

Additionally, Article 6.20 outlines that all new full-time Members with probationary or tenured appointments shall receive a minimum Start-up Grant of eight thousand dollars ($8,000) to attract and retain faculty Members.

Article 6.25 establishes the Laurentian University Research Fund (LURF), which provides research support through an open competition among Members. The fund is valued at $160,000 per year for each year of the Collective Agreement, with an additional $20,000 per year for retired Members, Sessional Members, and Master Lecturers to support research activities and attendance at academic and professional conferences.

The LURF Committee, consisting of eight full-time Members from various faculties, evaluates proposals submitted to the Office of Research Services once a year.

question: How does the agreement define or describe languages?
answer:
According to Article 1.15 (page not specified) and Article 2.04 (both references):

Both the English and French versions of the Collective Agreement shall be official and definitive versions. (Article 1.15.1, page not specified)

This means that both languages are recognized as equally valid and authoritative versions of the agreement.

Additionally, according to Article 2.04 (page not specified) which is identical to Article 1.15.1:

Both parties may use either the English or the French version in any proceedings arising out of the collective agreement...

This further emphasizes that both languages are accepted as official languages for communication and negotiations under the Collective Agreement.

It's worth noting that I couldn't find a specific page number for Article 1.15.1, but it is likely to be on the same page as the rest of Article 1.15.

This implies that the rights of both parties are defined within this Agreement.

question: How does the agreement define or describe appointment and renewal?
answer:

The agreement emphasizes that appointments shall be made only to specific ranks outlined in Article 5.20.5, which includes Lecturer, Assistant Professor, Associate Professor, Full Professor, and corresponding library ranks.

When considering appointment or renewal, it is essential to refer to the relevant articles of the collective agreement for detailed information and procedures.

question: What conditions apply to retirement?
answer:
According to Article 19 - Retirement and Resignation, page not specified but it seems that it is mentioned in different clauses:

* The possible retirement dates of a member and the provisions for early retirement under the University pension plan are governed by the terms of the plan to which the University belongs. (Source: Article 19 - Retirement and Resignation)
* All leaves to which the retiring member would be entitled must be terminated at the member’s retirement date. (Source: Article 19 - Retirement and Resignation)

However, for Special Voluntary Early Retirement specifically, there are additional conditions:

* The Member must be five (5) years or less from the attainment of her/his Normal Retirement Date.
* The Member must have completed at least fifteen (15) years of full-time service at Laurentian University as of the proposed date of commencement of Special Voluntary Early Retirement.

question: How does the agreement define or describe moving expenses?
answer:
According to Article 31 — MOVING EXPENSES in the Collective Agreement:

Moving expenses are defined as including:

* Moving, packing, crating, and unpacking of household goods and personal effects (32.02(a) LUFA-H Collective Agreement 2012-2016, page 45)
* Transfer of family by the most economical means of transportation (32.02(b) LUFA-H Collective Agreement 2012-2016, page 45)
* Reasonable living expenses while travelling to Sudbury (32.02(c) LUFA-H Collective Agreement 2012-2016, page 45)
* One advance visit for the purpose of securing suitable housing, which may be accompanied by a spouse (32.02(d) LUFA-H Collective Agreement 2012-2016, page 45)

Additionally, Article 8.55 in the 2011-14 Collective Agreement also lists similar expenses:

Moving expenses include:
* Moving, packing, crating and unpacking of household goods and personal effects
* Transfer of family by the most economical means of transportation
* Reasonable living expenses for the duration of the trip to the new location
* One (1) advance visit for the purpose of securing suitable housing. The newly appointed Members may be accompanied by their spouse in this instance.

Note: There are slight variations in the definition between different Collective Agreements, but they generally cover similar expenses.

question: What does the agreement say about sabbatical leave?
answer:
According to Article 12 of the Collective Agreement, the purpose of sabbatical leave is to "foster the pursuit of knowledge and serve the academic and scholarly objectives of the University by affording members a regular opportunity to devote their energies entirely to research and study" (Collective Agreement, p. not specified). The agreement also acknowledges that both parties have a joint responsibility to encourage the effective use of sabbatical leaves so as to strengthen the university in achieving its objectives (Article 12.01).

Additionally, Article 22.09 states that compensation for sabbatical leaves coincides with the Collective Agreement in place, and salary, benefits, and other provisions will be adjusted according to any new agreement between the Board and the Association.

It's worth noting that there is no specific information on how sabbatical leave is awarded or the process for applying for one. However, Article 12 suggests that the purpose of sabbatical leave is to allow members to focus on research and study, which implies that it may be available to members who need time to pursue academic objectives.

question: What are the rules concerning sabbatical leaves?
answer:
According to Article 22.07 of the Collective Agreement, the rules concerning sabbatical leaves are as follows:

* A sabbatical leave is for a period of either 12 months commencing on July 1 or 6 months commencing on either July 1 or January 1 (source: "Collective Agreement" page 22.07).
* No portion of the academic year in which a sabbatical leave is taken shall count toward the years of eligibility entitlement (source: same as above).
* A sabbatical leave includes the appropriate vacation entitlement proportional to the length of the leave (source: same as above).

Additionally, Article 5.20 provides further rules and guidelines for sabbatical leaves:

* When Members take a sabbatical leave after three years, all accumulated years of eligibility are exhausted except as otherwise provided for by this Collective Agreement (source: "SABBATICAL LEAVE" page 5.20.01).
* When the sabbatical leave is postponed, the Member shall receive one year's sabbatical credit for the year postponed so that their next sabbatical leave will occur according to their original sabbatical rotation (source: same as above).
* Sabbaticals after three years can be granted provided that Members have tenure when the leave is taken (source: "SABBATICAL LEAVE" page 5.20.01).

Finally, Article 12.20 states that immediately following the completion of a sabbatical leave, the Member is required to return to the University for a period equal to the length of the leave taken, or to satisfy some other arrangement that is mutually acceptable to the member and the Employer (source: "Collective Agreement" page 12.20).

question: What does the agreement say about removal from office of?
answer:
According to Article 9.30 - Removal From Office of Chairs/Directors, proceedings for the removal of a Chair/Director may be initiated by either:

* A written complaint to the Dean/University Librarian specifying the reasons for the complaint, signed by at least a majority of the full-time faculty of the Department/School (Clause 9.30.1(a)).
* A written complaint by the Dean/University Librarian to the Vice-President, Academic and Provost specifying the grounds for the complaint (Clause 9.30.1(b)).

In either case, if the Chair/Director is not requested to relinquish their office, procedures under Article 9.30.3(c) may be initiated.

Article 9.30.3 outlines three possible scenarios:

* If the Chair/Director does not voluntarily resign as Chair/Director:
	+ The Vice-President, Academic and Provost is empowered to suspend that individual as Chair/Director (Clause 9.30.3(a)).
	+ The Vice-President, Academic and Provost shall instruct the Dean/University Librarian to appoint an Acting-Chair/Director in consultation with the Department/School (Clause 9.30.3(b)).
	+ The President shall create an ad hoc committee to investigate the complaint and shall conduct its investigation in accordance with statutory requirements (Clause 9.30.3(c)).

Source: Collective Agreement 2011-14, Article 9.30 - Removal From Office of Chairs/Directors.

question: What conditions apply to patents?
answer:
According to ARTICLE 6.30 – PATENTS of the Collective Agreement, the following conditions apply to patents:

* Where an invention was made with the use of the Employer's funds, personnel or equipment, the Members shall sign an agreement with the University before an application for patent is filed (6.30.4).
* In such cases, the Employer shall assign all rights, title and interest in the invention to the Members, subject to the University and the Members sharing equally in the "net proceeds" as used in this Article (6.30.4).

Note: The "net proceeds" is defined as the net profits derived from licensing or commercialisation of the patented product, equipment or process after deduction of all expenses incurred in patent searches, for obtained patent protection and for maintaining said protection in Canada and in other countries (6.30.4).

question: What does the collective agreement provide regarding physical and mental illness?
answer:
The collective agreement provides several provisions regarding physical and mental illness:

1. Cases involving non-culpable behaviour by a Member as a result of a physical or mental illness, confirmed by an independent physician agreed to by LUFA and the Employer, shall be treated separately from cases for disciplinary conduct (LUFA-H Collective Agreement 2016-2020, page 55).
2. Members who are unable to perform their duties due to physical or mental illness shall have leave granted and the case dealt with within the University's sickness and disability provisions set out in Article 7.55 – Physical and Mental Illness (Collective Agreement 2008-11, section 5.80.3).
3. If a Member refuses to comply with the requirements of the University's sickness and disability provisions, the President may proceed to lay dismissal charges (Collective Agreement 2008-11, section 5.80.3(c)).
4. Members on sickness or disability leave who consider they have recovered and are capable of undertaking normal academic activities shall present medical evidence from a medical practitioner to their Dean/University Librarian, and if agreed, shall be reinstated with full rights and benefits (Collective Agreement 2008-11, section 5.80.3(e)).
5. The Employer may subrogate to all rights of recovery of the Member to the extent that they have made payment to or on behalf of the Member (Article 7.55.1).
6. Members are eligible for sick leave up to a maximum of six months at salary otherwise receivable from the date of disability due to accident or illness, and illness of a duration of more than six months will be dealt with according to the provisions of the University's Long-Term Disability Plan (Article 7.55.1).

These provisions aim to support Members who are experiencing physical or mental health issues, while also ensuring that they fulfill their academic responsibilities when possible.

question: What is stated about personnel files?

* Members may request a copy of their personnel file excluding confidential material, which will be filled within five working days at no charge (Article 5.70.3).
* Anonymous material concerning any Member shall not be kept by the Employer for inclusion in the Member's personnel file (Article 5.70.4).

answer:

question: What does the agreement say about disciplinary measures?
answer:
The agreement mentions the process for handling allegations and investigations in Article 5.75.6 and another section with a similar number, but I'll provide information based on the first mentioned section.

According to Article 5.75.6, when an allegation is made against a Member (likely meaning a faculty member), they shall be given five working days' notice of the time and place of a meeting where possible or practicable. The Parties (the Member, their union representative, and the Employer) are expected to attempt to resolve the matter in a manner acceptable to all concerned.

It appears that specific details about disciplinary measures, such as penalties or consequences for the Member, are not explicitly outlined in this section. However, the process for handling allegations is described, including notice, review of particulars, opportunity to respond, and attempting to resolve the matter amicably.

answer:
According to Article 5.2 - Removal from Office (page not specified) and Article 9.30 – REMOVAL FROM OFFICE OF CHAIRS/DIRECTORS, proceedings for the removal of a Chairperson/Director may be initiated in two ways:

question: What are the rules concerning annual report for members?
answer:
According to the collective agreement, there are specific rules concerning annual reports for different types of members.

**Sessional Members (Article 4.35)**:
- Must submit a brief annual report in electronic and paper format to their Departments/Schools.

- At their discretion, Sessional Members may also include material related to scholarly or creativity activity, professional development, university governance, or other relevant activities.

**Full-time Members (Article 10.08)**:
- Must submit a written Annual Report on their activities for the preceding twelve months from May 1 to April 30.
- The report must cover all components of members' activities as described in Article 10, Academic Activity.
- The report is due by June 22 and should be submitted to the President with a copy to their department chairs.

**Members on Sabbatical or Study Leave (Articles 4.50.3 and 4.50.4)**:
- Must include in their annual report a full written account of their scholastic and professional activities and accomplishments as per the approved sabbatical plan during the leave.

Note: The decision to award an annual increment is governed by Article 8.20, which requires that members submit their reports on time for consideration by June 30.

question: How is committee apprehension addressed in the collective agreement?
answer:
According to Article 2.60 of the Collective Agreement 2017-2020, there are two specific instances where committees were established to address apprehension of bias:

1. APPENDIX D - LETTER OF UNDERSTANDING BETWEEN: THE LAURENTIAN UNIVERSITY FACULTY ASSOCIATION AND LAURENTIAN UNIVERSITY OF SUDBURY RE: JOINT COMMITTEE TO STUDY APPREHENSION OF BIAS (page 215). This letter establishes a committee of two representatives chosen by the Union and two representatives chosen by the Employer to provide guidelines for the applications of the concept of "apprehension of bias" in university decision-making and in the context of committees operating under this Collective Agreement. The committee shall be established by January 15, 2012 and make its report to the Parties by March 15, 2012.
2. APPENDIX J - LETTER OF UNDERSTANDING BETWEEN: THE LAURENTIAN UNIVERSITY FACULTY ASSOCIATION AND LAURENTIAN UNIVERSITY OF SUDBURY RE: JOINT COMMITTEE TO STUDY APPREHENSION OF BIAS (page 235). This letter also establishes a similar committee with the same purpose, to be established by January 15, 2009 and make its report to the Parties by March 15, 2009.

These letters of understanding demonstrate that both parties agreed to establish committees to address apprehension of bias in university decision-making.

question: What conditions apply to new hires?
answer:
According to Article 3.20 of the Thorneloe-LUFA Collective Agreement, the following conditions apply to new hires:

1. **Tenure-track positions:** New members appointed to a tenure-track position are eligible to receive:
	* A 3-credit course reduction from the normal workload of 15 credits in any year of their employment prior to the granting of tenure (Article 3.20.1).
	* A $4000 research grant, expendable prior to the granting of tenure. Applications for the research grant must meet the criteria set out for Professional Allowance (4.95.3) (Article 3.20.2).
2. **Childcare Assistance:** The University will provide information about childcare facilities in Sudbury and subsidies available for childcare expenses not later than the offer of employment (Article 3.20.3).
3. **Spousal Hires:**
	* When a candidate has been recommended by a Thorneloe Academic Unit for tenure-track (or probationary) or tenured position, and has a spouse or partner who may be qualified for an academic position:
		+ A Thorneloe Academic Unit appropriate to the discipline of the spouse or partner may recommend a 1-3 year term appointment without advertising under certain conditions (Article 3.20.4).
		+ The conditions include: 
			- Confirmation by the President that a position within the academic unit is available, in consultation with all department chairs.
			- Availability of an application file for viewing by all Members of the Thorneloe Academic Unit and arrangement of interviews and open meetings with the candidate and Members in the Unit.

question: What does the collective agreement provide regarding academic freedom?
answer:
According to the Collective Agreement 2017-2020 (page 2) and the Collective Agreement 2018-2021 (pages 1 and e), the relevant provisions regarding academic freedom are:

* Academic freedom is essential to the teaching and research activities of the University, and its pursuit is a fundamental objective of the institution. (Collective Agreement 2017-2020, page 2)
* Academic freedom allows members to search for truth, knowledge, and understanding; to express their opinions freely; and to teach, discuss, and criticize without restriction. (Collective Agreement 2018-2021, Article 0.02(a))
* However, academic freedom does not confer legal immunity, and members are still obligated to perform their duties and responsibilities satisfactorily. (Collective Agreement 2018-2021, page 1)
* Academic freedom also carries the responsibility to respect the rights of other members of the academic community to express their opinions. (Collective Agreement 2018-2021, Article e)

Overall, the collective agreement emphasizes the importance of academic freedom in the pursuit of truth and knowledge, while also acknowledging its limitations and responsibilities.

question: What are the rules concerning definitions?
answer:
According to Article 1.30 – Definitions, the following terms are defined:

* "Conseiller" (Counselor) is a member who was previously part of the bargaining unit, designated by the OLRB certificate dated April 9, 2020.
* "Crédits universitaires" (University credits) refer to the number of credits allocated to a course by the University Senate and indicated in the Laurentian University calendar.
* "Directeur" (Director) refers to the Director of an academic department, professional school, or library.
* "Doyen" (Dean) refers to the Dean of a faculty appointed in good standing or their delegate.
* "Employer or Council of Governors" means the Council of Governors of Laurentian University, or its delegate, according to the provisions of the Laurentian University Act (Sudbury).
* "Faculté" (Faculty) refers to any grouping identified as such by the University Senate with the approval of the Employer, according to the Laurentian University Act.
* "Famille immédiate" (Immediate family) includes a spouse, common-law partner, brother, sister, parent, child, or step-child by blood, adoption, marriage, or de facto relationship.
* "La Loi de l'Université Laurentienne de Sudbury" refers to the Laurentian University Act (Sudbury), that is, Chapter 151 of the Ontario Statutes of 1960, as amended by Chapter 154 of the 1961-1962 Statutes.
* "Les Centres" refer to the counseling services and the Centre for Indigenous Sharing and Learning.
* "Les crédits universitaires qui contribuent à l'ancienneté des Membres chargés de cours" (University credits contributing to the seniority of Sessional Members) include credits allocated to courses for which the name of the Sessional Member appears on official lists, bulletins, teaching evaluations, or appointment letters.
* "L'exercice professionnel" (Professional exercise), for librarians and archivists, refers to contributions to the selection, development, and implementation of strategic directions, priorities, policies, procedures, and standards for library and archives resources and services.
* "Membres associés du corps professoral" (Associate Members of the Professorial Staff) refer to individuals external to the University whose scholarly work or professional achievements warrant association with the University. Associate Members are appointed for a specified period with specific privileges and are responsible for their own research choices. They have no rank or voting rights on Department/School decisions.
* "Membres à temps plein nommés au poste de Maître de conférences" (Full-time Members appointed to the position of Professor) are responsible for first-cycle teaching, clinical education, or supervision of clinical internships, language instruction, skill improvement, mentorship, research assistance, or other relevant functions as specified by the Employer. In some cases, a Professor may teach upper-level courses or conduct scholarly work and has the right to participate in University governance and express themselves through voting at Department/School meetings.

question: What does the agreement say about pregnancy, parental and adoption?
answer:
According to Article 25.06 of the LUFA-H Collective Agreement 2012-2016 (page not specified), there are provisions related to pregnancy leave, parental leave, and adoption.

**Pregnancy Leave:**

* A Member may postpone or interrupt her pregnancy leave by the number of weeks the newborn child is hospitalized but it must be taken within the fifty-two (52) weeks from the date of the birth of the child. (Page not specified)
* The pregnancy leave of a Member who is not entitled to take parental leave shall end on the later of either the day that is seventeen (17) weeks after the pregnancy leave began or the day that is six (6) weeks after the birth, stillbirth or miscarriage.

**Parental Leave:**

* On the occasion of the adoption of a child coming into the care or custody of a parent for the first time, a Member who is a parent shall be entitled to a parental leave of up to thirty-seven (37) weeks. The parental leave must be commenced within the fifty-two (52) weeks from the date the child comes into care or custody of the parent for the first time.

**Adoption:**

* The agreement also allows for parental leave on the occasion of the adoption of a child, with up to thirty-seven (37) weeks available.

question: What are the rules concerning voluntary reduced workload?
answer:
The rules concerning voluntary reduced workload can be found in Article 7.35 - VOLUNTARY REDUCED WORKLOAD of the Collective Agreement.

**Eligibility**

* Any full-time Member of the Bargaining Unit who currently occupies a regular full-time position and has a minimum of two (2) years of continuous full-time service at the University may apply for a voluntary reduced workload (7.35.1).

**Application Process**

* The request must be made in writing to the Department/School and the Dean/University Librarian three (3) months in advance (7.35.1(b)).
* The Dean/University Librarian approves the request, with approval not being unreasonably withheld (7.35.1(c)).

**Duration of Voluntary Reduced Workload**

* The temporary reduction is effective for a twelve (12) month period (7.35.1(a)).
* The University may grant voluntary reduced workloads for periods longer than twelve (12) months and/or renewals of twelve (12) month reduction periods, subject to the Dean’s/University Librarian's approval (7.35.2).

**Benefits**

* Faculty Members on Voluntary Reduced Workload have the right to benefits and to contribute to the benefits plan of the University in accordance with the provisions of the Collective Agreement for sharing contributions (7.35.3).
* Members will be covered for periods of sick leave, long-term disability, pension plan, life insurance, and sabbatical leave entitlements as per the Collective Agreement (7.35.3(a-e)).

**Other Provisions**

* Members who use this option shall remain Members of the Bargaining Unit, notwithstanding the definition of Membership as defined in Article 2.15 – Recognition of the Bargaining Unit (7.35.4).
* Periods of reduced workload shall be pro-rated in accordance with the reduction in workload for the application of tenure and promotion policies (7.35.5).

Note: These rules may have changed since the Collective Agreement was signed, but these are the rules as they appear in the document provided.

question: What are the rules concerning faculty personnel files?
answer:
According to Article 21 of the Collective Agreement 2015-2018 (pages 42 of 59), there are specific rules concerning faculty personnel files:

* The official personnel files of a member shall be kept by the President and are the property of the Employer (Article 21.01).
* Members have the right to examine all their personnel files, upon making prior arrangements to do so (Article 21.02).
* Material in the files that is to be held confidential according to the provisions of this Agreement will be removed from the files prior to their inspection by the member.
* There are two types of files: active files and archival files. Active files shall contain only information allowed under Article 5, while archival files shall contain material banned for use in subsequent proceedings (Collective Agreement 2015-2018, page not specified).

Additionally, there are specific rules regarding confidential information:

* All letters or assessments solicited by the Faculty Personnel Committee and any summaries thereof shall be kept confidential and used only for the purposes for which they were solicited in any subsequent proceedings against that Member (Article 5.70.8).
* Student evaluations, in numerical or written form, shall not be admissible as evidence in any process involving a Member's tenure, promotion or dismissal if such evaluations are more than five years old (Article 5.70.9).

question: What does the collective agreement provide regarding beneficiary procedures?
answer:
According to Article 8.80 of the Collective Agreement 2017-2020, specifically sections 8.80.1 to 8.80.3, the following procedures are outlined for beneficiaries:

* The beneficiary is required to contact the Pension and Benefits Officer in the Personnel Office (section 8.80.1).
* If the University has not been contacted by the beneficiary within seven days, the University shall make every reasonable effort to contact the beneficiary (section 8.80.1).
* To request payment of life insurance proceeds, the beneficiary must provide certain documents to the insurance carrier, including a Statement required by the insurance carrier, Social Insurance Number, notice of the Employee's death in Obituary Notices, Death Certificate, and last insurance certificate issued to the faculty Member (section 8.80.2).
* If the Member dies prior to receiving a pension, the beneficiary must complete an "Application for Death Benefit", provide a Death Certificate, and a notarial copy of the Employee's "Last Will and Testament" (section 8.80.3).

It is also noted that all Members are expected to have a current "Last Will and Testament" (section 8.80.3), and if they do not, beneficiaries may need to settle disputes in court before receiving any funds from the Pension Plan.

Source: Collective Agreement 2017-2020, Article 8.80.

answer:
According to Article 2.02 of the LUFA-H Collective Agreement 2016-2020, page 4:

Academic freedom entails the obligation to base all research and teaching on a responsible search for truth and knowledge.

3. The acceptance of responsibility for one's own beliefs and utterances (LUFA-H Collective Agreement 2016-2020, page 4).

question: According to the agreement, what applies to academic workload?
answer:
According to the collective agreement, the following principles apply to academic workload:

1. The President must ensure that the annual academic workload is determined, distributed, and scheduled as equitably as possible (Source: 10.07 Annual Academic Workload (a), p.?).
2. The member's assigned annual academic workload must take into account the four domains of activity indicated in 10.01 and the Preamble regarding the academic freedom of individual members (Source: 10.07 Annual Academic Workload (a), p.?).
3. Factors such as the needs of the member's program, including student enrolments and the necessity of offering required courses, must be considered when determining workload (Source: 10.07 Annual Academic Workload (i), p.?).
4. The President will assign academic workload in a fair and equitable manner, including teaching/librarianship, scholarly activity, governance, and community service (Source: ARTICLE 12 — WORKLOAD, 12.01, p.?).
5. The Dean/University Librarian has the authority to limit the number of overload courses a Member may teach in any given academic year, or its equivalent in the Library (Source: 8.35.3, p.?).

* Sabbaticals after three years can be granted provided that:
	+ Members have tenure when the leave commences (Eligibility (a)).

Additionally, it is stated in Section 22.09 that Members on sabbatical leave who elect to remain on campus are not normally assigned any formal workload nor participate in any formal activities of the University other than those required by this Collective Agreement (page [insert page number]).

question: What does the collective agreement provide regarding discipline?
answer:
According to the collective agreement, the following are key points regarding discipline:

* Discipline must be "just and reasonable" (Source: Collective Agreement, page 1).
* The principle of progressive discipline is applied, except in egregious cases (Source: Collective Agreement, page 1).
* Just cause for disciplinary measures includes:
	+ Gross misconduct, including serious unprofessional behavior and/or misconduct that violates the personal safety of another Member or student (Source: Collective Agreement, 5.75.2(a)).
	+ Persistent failure to discharge academic responsibility (Source: Collective Agreement, 5.75.2(b)).
	+ Serious unprofessional behavior (Source: Collective Agreement, 5.75.2(a)).
	+ Failure to comply with any provisions of the collective agreement, except for minor technical violations (Source: Collective Agreement, 5.75.2(b)).
* The following are the only formal disciplinary measures that can be taken against a Member:
	+ A letter of reprimand, specifying the grounds and adding this reprimand to the personnel file (Sources: Collective Agreement, 5.75.3(a) and 5.75.5(a)).
	+ Suspension with pay, if and only if cited as a disciplinary measure by the Vice-President, Academic and Provost (Source: Collective Agreement, 5.75.5(b)).
* A Member has a fundamental right to know, in a timely manner, the nature of the allegations against them, and the right to respond to such allegations (Sources: Collective Agreement, 5.75.4 and 5.75.5).

Note: The collective agreement provides two different versions of sections 5.75.2-5.75.5. I have cited both sources where applicable.

(Source: Page not specified, but appears to be the general definitions section)
* Faculté (Faculty): "Faculté signifie tout regroupement identifié comme tel par le Sénat de l'Université avec l'approbation de l’Employeur, selon la Loi de l'Université Laurentienne de Sudbury." (Source: Page not specified, but appears to be the general definitions section)
* Famille immédiate (Immediate family): "Famille immédiate signifie un conjoint, une conjointe, un frère, une sœur, un parent, un fils ou une fille, par lien de sang, d’adoption, de mariage ou de relation de conjoint de fait." * Membres associés du corps professoral (Associate members of the faculty): "Les Membres associés du corps professoral signifient les personnes externes à l’Université dont les travaux d’érudition ou les réalisations professionnelles méritent d’être associés avec l’Université." (Source: Page not specified, but appears to be the general definitions section)
* Membres chargés de cours (Sessional instructors): "Les crédits universitaires qui contribuent à l'ancienneté des Membres chargés de cours sont les crédits accordés aux cours pour lesquels le nom du Membre chargé de cours figure sur la liste officielle des cours, les bulletins, les évaluations d'enseignement ou les lettres de nomination." question: How does the agreement define or describe political leaves?
answer:
According to Article 7.50 - POLITICAL LEAVES, the Employer recognizes that all Members of the Bargaining Unit are free to enter public life and to seek any political office (Source: Collective Agreement 2017-2020, page 8, Article 7.50.1).

Additionally, if Members wish to allow their names to stand either before a party convention or for actual nomination for an election, they must notify the Dean/University Librarian concerned within a reasonable time so that arrangements can be made to ensure that the resulting added workload can be properly performed by others (Source: Collective Agreement 2017-2020, page 8, Article 7.50.2).

The Employer may grant such a Member leave without pay for a period from the issuance of the writ up to and including election day (Source: Collective Agreement 2017-2020, page 8, Article 7.50.3).

question: What are the rules concerning redundancy committee?
answer:
The rules concerning the Redundancy Committee can be found in Article 10.10 and 11.10 of the Collective Agreement.

**Formation of the Redundancy Committee:**

* The Committee shall be formed as a result of the Employer's declaration (Article 10.10.5).
* The Union shall forward to the Vice-President, Academic and Provost the names of three Members who shall serve on the Redundancy Committee within ten (10) days of receipt of the notice (Article 10.10.5).

**Composition of the Redundancy Committee:**

* The Committee shall include:
	+ Three Members chosen by the Union (Article 10.10.6(a)).
	+ Three individuals named by the Employer (Article 10.10.6(b)).
	+ The Vice-President, Academic and Provost as non-voting Chair (Article 10.10.6(c)).

**Responsibilities of the Redundancy Committee:**

* Within sixty (60) days of its first meeting, the Redundancy Committee shall make its final report to the Employer (with a copy to the Union) (Article 11.10.7).
* The Committee's responsibility is to recommend who among the Members of the Department(s)/School(s) under consideration shall be affected by redundancy (Article 11.10.8).

**Steps in Considering Redundancy:**

* The Redundancy Committee shall consider the following steps in the following order:
	+ Non-renewal of limited term appointments within the Department/School.
	+ Non-renewal of two (2) year probationary contracts within the Department/School.
	+ Non-renewal of contracts of Members within the Department/School on three (3) year probationary contracts.
	+ Removal of a tenured Member from the Department/School (Article 11.10.9).

**Transfer Options:**

* If a redundant Member has tenure, or is on a three (3) year probationary contract, the Redundancy Committee shall include in its final recommendation to the Employer a list of administrative and academic areas to which the Members could be transferred, with or without a year's retraining (Article 11.10.10).

**Employer's Notification:**

* If the Employer approves a resolution to act on the Redundancy Committee's recommendation that a Member be declared redundant, then the Employer shall send the Member a written notice of its resolution (Article 11.10.11).

question: What does the collective agreement provide regarding retirement?
answer:
According to the collective agreement, there are several provisions related to retirement. However, I'll focus on the key points.

Firstly, Section 8.80.2 Life Insurance (b) mentions that a beneficiary must complete a Statement required by the insurance carrier and provide their Social Security number as part of requesting payment.

Regarding pension benefits for Members hired after September 24, 2017, who are age 55 or older upon retirement or resignation, it is stated in Section 5.90.5 that they will not have the option to commute the value of their pension benefit upon retirement or resignation. The Pension Plan will be amended accordingly.

In terms of participation in the Retirement Plan, Section 8.45.3 states that Members shall only participate in the Defined Benefit component of the Retirement Plan and Member contributions shall only be used for this purpose.

Lastly, there is no specific information on retirement age, but it's worth noting that the collective agreement mentions that a Member may also agree to some combination of normal workload assignment plus paid overload as appropriate (Section 8.40.5 Supervision), which could imply flexibility in work arrangements leading up to retirement.

Additionally, according to Article 24.03, The Arbitration Board shall not be authorized to make any decision inconsistent with the provisions of this Agreement, nor to alter, modify, add to, or amend any part of this Agreement. (Source: Collective Agreement 2018-2021, page 54)

Also, Article 36.05 states that the decision of the Arbitrator will be final and binding upon the Parties hereto and the Member(s) concerned except as provided by law. (Source: Collective Agreement 2018-2021, page 59)

answer:
According to Article 2.60 - Joint Consultative Committee for the Administration of the Collective Agreement (page number not specified), the agreement defines a Joint Consultative Committee as follows:

"The Parties agree to form a Joint Consultative Committee for the Administration of the Collective Agreement, composed of three (3) representatives of each Party..."

Additionally, the agreement describes the purpose and functions of the committee in Article 2.60.5, which states that the Committee shall attempt:

"a) To maintain and develop a spirit of cooperation and mutual respect between the Parties.
b) To facilitate better working relationships between the Employer and the Union and its Members.
c) To discuss, review, and make recommendations to the Parties on matters of concern to either Party."

The agreement also outlines the structure and procedures of the committee in Articles 2.60.4-9.

question: What are the rules concerning redundancy?
answer:

* The Employer agrees not to use any procedures other than those specified in this article to deal with redundancies (Source: "Collective Agreement" page ???).

question: What is stated about chair/coordinator?
answer:
According to Article 33 of the LUFA-H Collective Agreement, the following is stated about the Chair/Coordinator:

* They are elected to a three-year (3) term by a simple majority of the full-time Members of a department/program. (LUFA-H Collective Agreement 2016-2020, page 50 and 47)
* Their duties include:
	+ Ensuring that Members of the Department are informed of their duties and responsibilities in accordance with University Senate regulations, University regulations, and this Collective Agreement.
	+ Convening and presiding over meetings of the Department at regular intervals during the academic year.
	+ Consulting on budgetary recommendations with the President and/or Executive Director.
	+ Administering the annual budget for the Department.
	+ Ensuring that Members of the Department have an opportunity to share in the decision-making process, formulation of policies, and administrative tasks.
	+ Coordinating formal departmental/program reviews.
	+ Approving mark forms for courses offered in the department/program.
	+ Overseeing the development and revision of correspondence courses.
	+ Supervising student counselling on academic matters and assignment of programs of study within the Department.
	+ Administering space and equipment allocated to the Department.
	+ Presenting the academic programs of the Department for accreditation or approval by external bodies, as needed.
	+ Advising the President on the teaching roster, timetable, and office hours for the Department.
	+ Preparing a succinct annual report for submission to the President by June 30.
* Chairs/Coordinators are responsible for providing academic leadership to their department/program and representing the decisions and objectives of the department/program. (LUFA-H Collective Agreement 2016-2020, page 50)
* Department Chairs shall receive a 6 credit reduction in teaching or the value equivalent to 6-credits added to their salary for every year they are Chair, with their duties beginning on July 1. (LUFA-H Collective Agreement 2016-2020, page 50)

* The Member's performance over a three-year time period or since the award of the last merit increment, whichever is shorter, must be judged clearly above the level required for promotion to that rank (Article 8.25.5, page not specified).
* All merit increments received previously under the terms of prior Collective Agreements remain in force (Article 4.20.7, page not specified; Article 8.25.7, page not specified).

question: What does the collective agreement provide regarding academic workload?
answer:
The collective agreement provides that the President must ensure that the annual academic workload is determined, distributed, and scheduled as equitably as possible (10.07(a)). The assigned annual workload shall be communicated in reasonable detail, in writing, to the member by July 1 by the President (10.07(b)).

Additionally, teaching workloads are assigned by the President upon consideration of the recommendation of the Department Chair pursuant to Article 9.06(g) (10.07(c)). Any proposed changes to a member's teaching load will be raised with the member's department in a timely manner mindful of the demands such changes entail (10.07(d)).

The collective agreement also sets out specific standards for teaching workload, including that full-time faculty shall have a normal teaching load of 15 credits per academic year, which includes a minimum of 12 credits taught live (10.07(iv)). The President has the responsibility to ensure that over a period of two years, the full-time course equivalent (FCE) work load is equitably distributed and there are enough courses offered by the Department or programme so that, in the event of a cancellation, a full-time member is not prevented from meeting the standards set out above (10.07(v)).

question: How is health, safety and security addressed in the collective agreement?
answer:
According to Article 3.25 – HEALTH, SAFETY AND SECURITY of the Collective Agreement:

* The Employer recognizes a responsibility to provide an environment intended to protect the health, safety and security of employees as they carry out their responsibilities (page 22 of 243, Collective Agreement 2011-14).

* The Employer agrees to maintain a Joint Health and Safety Committee, which will independently consider matters concerning the health and safety of employees and students (page 22 of 243, Collective Agreement 2011-14).
* Members who have reason to believe that a work situation is likely to endanger them have the right to refuse unsafe work pursuant to and in accordance with the provisions of the Ontario Occupational Health and Safety Act (Article 3.25.3).

Additionally, Article 4.03 of the LUFA-H Collective Agreement 2016-2020 states:

* The Employer recognizes its responsibility to provide an environment intended to protect the health, safety and security of Members as they carry out their duties.
* The Employer will provide a copy of the annual report of the Health and Safety Committee to the Membership.

question: According to the agreement, what applies to study leaves?
answer:
According to Article 7.30 - STUDY LEAVES (page numbers not specified in the context), several things apply to study leaves:

* A leave for the purpose of upgrading academic qualifications shall be known as Study Leave.
* Such leave must be in the best interests of the University.
* The maximum length of leaves to be granted during a Member's academic career shall normally not exceed two (2) years.

Additionally, Article 7.30.1 Eligibility states that:

* A study leave may be granted to a tenured, probationary or Master Lecturer Member after two (2) years of full-time service.
* The leave will not be automatic and shall be granted only upon the approval by the Vice-President, Academic and Provost.

And Article 7.30.2 Application states that:

* Applications for study leave shall be made by September 30 in consultation with the Department/School through the Chair/Director and the appropriate Dean/University Librarian to the Vice-President, Academic and Provost.
* In submitting an application for study leave, the Members shall provide a well-considered plan indicating the value of the leave to their professional improvement and to the best interest of the University.

Source: Collective Agreement 2017-2020.

question: What conditions apply to sabbatical leave?
answer:
According to Article 7.25.2 of the Collective Agreement 2017-2020, eligibility for sabbatical leave is subject to the following conditions:

(a) Members must have been full-time faculty members of the University for the past six consecutive years, holding the rank of Full Professor/Librarian, Associate Professor/Librarian, and Assistant Professor/Librarian at the time of application. They must be tenured at the time their sabbatical leave begins.

(b) In exceptional circumstances, tenured Lecturers/General Librarians/Archivists with the requisite years at Laurentian are also eligible for sabbatical if they have the approval of the Dean/University Librarian to apply.

(c) Where the leave is to be used for upgrading, the University shall give special consideration to employment equity goals.

(d) Faculty Members' service for purposes of sabbatical leave eligibility shall be calculated from the date of their initial full-time appointment or from the date of their last sabbatical leave, whichever is later.

question: What are the rules concerning copyright?
answer:
The Laurentian University Faculty Association collective agreement has specific rules regarding copyright. 

**Section 15.01**, "ARTICLE 15 – COPYRIGHT", states that copyright applies to all original written, artistic, and recorded works (p. ?).

**Section 6.35.3** outlines the circumstances under which the university holds the first ownership of the copyright: when a member creates work for the university under a special contract, including distance education courses (p. ?).

However, **Section 15.02**, "Vested in Member", states that except where materials are commissioned by the employer or created within normal administrative and teaching duties, the copyright is retained by the members responsible for creating the material (p.?).

**Section 6.35.5** specifies that the master copy of any work whose copyright is vested in the university shall be the property of the university (p. ?).

**Section 6.35.10** allows authors to request revisions after three years of use, and at three-year intervals thereafter, with negotiation on costs and fees (p.?).

These sections provide a comprehensive overview of the rules concerning copyright under the collective agreement.

question: What does the collective agreement provide regarding appointment and renewal for sessional members?
answer:
The collective agreement provides that appointments of Sessional Lecturers are made by the Vice-President Academic and Provost or her/his designate on behalf of the Employer and on the recommendation of the Dean/University Librarian and the Department/School concerned (4.15.1). The appointment process includes:

* Sessional appointments and other extra-departmental assignments of courses shall be made from rosters of names of potential instructors maintained by the Departments/Schools responsible for the particular course (4.15.2).
* Sessional Members on the University roster shall be notified of the courses expected to be offered in their Department(s)/School(s) in all sessions of the upcoming year by April 15 (4.15.3).
* Sessional Members interested in teaching any of the available courses must send a letter of application to the Chair/Director of the Department/School by May 15, along with a current curriculum vitae, a current teaching dossier, and any relevant supporting documentation (4.15.4).

As for renewal, the collective agreement states that Sessional Members with Establishment and with highest seniority shall have first right of reappointment, subject to notice of those rights with respect to a particular term (4.15.17).

question: How does the agreement define or describe rights, responsibilities and duties?
answer:
According to Article 2.00 - RIGHTS, RESPONSIBILITIES AND DUTIES OF ACADEMICS (page not specified), the agreement defines or describes rights, responsibilities, and duties as follows:

	+ University Governance and Administrative Duties (Article 2.00)
	+ Outside Professional Activities
	+ Service to the Community
	+ Other Paid Activity

* Regular Stream Members: participate actively in items A), B), and C) (Teaching / Scholarly Activity / University Governance and Administrative Duties)
* Alternate Stream Members: participate actively in items A) and C) (Teaching / University Governance and Administrative Duties)

Overall, the agreement emphasizes that Members have both rights and responsibilities, and that these are derived from their positions as teachers/professional librarians and scholars within the University community.

question: What does the collective agreement provide regarding discipline?
answer:
According to Article 5.75 of the Collective Agreement, discipline is governed by the following provisions:

* Discipline must be just and reasonable (5.75.2).
* Just cause is defined as gross misconduct or persistent failure to discharge academic responsibility (5.75.2(a) and (b)).
* The Employer shall not impose discipline without compliance with principles of natural justice and due process, including giving the Member a timely opportunity to know the nature of the allegations against them and respond to such allegations (5.75.4).
* The Member has a fundamental right to know, in a timely manner, the nature of the allegations against him/her, and the right to respond to such allegations (5.75.4).

Regarding the forms of discipline that may be taken by the Employer, Article 5.75 provides:

* For full-time Members:
	+ A letter of reprimand
	+ Suspension with pay (if cited as a disciplinary measure)
	+ Suspension without pay
	+ Withholding of an annual increment
	+ Dismissal
* For sessional or part-time Members:
	+ A letter of reprimand
	+ Suspension with pay (if cited as a disciplinary measure)
	+ Suspension without pay (with a reduction in pay computed as 1/87 per day of suspension per three credit course, or as the average salary over the previous 4 weeks for Part-Time Clinicians)
	+ Removal of seniority and/or Establishment
	+ Dismissal for Part-time Clinicians

question: How is committee consist addressed in the collective agreement?
answer:
According to Article 9.30 and Article 2.55, there are multiple instances where a "committee" or similar group is referenced, but only one of them specifically addresses how committees are constituted.

A specific rule for committee composition is mentioned on page 13:

"The Committee shall consider the claim and, should at least three members agree with the claim, the subject Committee member shall not participate in discussions on, or vote on that application." (Source: Collective Agreement 2018-2021, Page 13)

This suggests that some committees consist of a minimum of three members, but it does not provide further information about the composition or appointment process for these committees.

Additionally, Article 9.30 mentions "a Committee" without specifying its size or composition, and Article 2.55 refers to "the Committee" in general terms without providing specific details about how its membership is constituted.

question: What are the rules concerning removal from office of?
answer:
According to Article 5.2 - Removal from Office, a Chairperson/Director may be removed from office by the Vice-President, Academic, who shall consider all serious complaints against them and take appropriate action, including the possibility of removal.

Additionally, in the event of a complaint initiated by the Dean/Director of the Library, the process for removal is as follows:

1. A written complaint to the Dean/Director of the Library specifying the reasons for the complaint, signed by at least a majority of the full-time faculty of the unit (Article 5.2 - Removal from Office, page 111).
2. The Dean/Director of the Library shall investigate the situation and offer their services to resolve the matter (Article 5.2 - Removal from Office, page 111).
3. If the attempt is unsuccessful, the Dean/Director of the Library will forward the written complaint together with their report to the Vice-President, Academic (Article 5.2 - Removal from Office, page 111).

Source: Collective Agreement 2002-2005, pages 106 and 111.

question: What is stated about study leaves?
answer:
A study leave with pay is granted to enable a Member to pursue a program of study of benefit to the Member and in order to meet specific needs of the University (Article 23.01, page not specified). Study leave periods may vary to a maximum of twelve (12) months and may be renewable without compensation. A study leave includes the appropriate vacation entitlement proportional to the length of the leave.

Additionally, all Members on study leave must obtain written approval in advance from the Dean/University Librarian for any paid activity before making such a commitment (Article 23.01, page not specified).

It is also stated that time spent on study leave does not count towards sabbatical credit (Article 13.01(c), Collective Agreement 2017-2020, page 1).

question: According to the agreement, what applies to faculty appointments?
answer:
According to Article 13 — Faculty Appointments in the LUFA-H Collective Agreement 2012-2016 (page 17), the following applies:

* The appointment process is a peer-review process.
* Input from Members of the same discipline as the contemplated appointment is important, but the Employer determines the faculty complement necessary to carry out its objectives and mission.
* Final decisions are the responsibility of the Board and President.

Additionally, in Article 5 — Appointments, there are several provisions that apply to faculty appointments:

* Priority shall be given to Canadian citizens, permanent residents, and persons on minister's permits where a number of candidates have been judged to be substantially equal in qualifications and appropriateness of academic specialisation (Collective Agreement 2002-2005, page 34).
* Relevant criteria for appointment shall include teaching/professional, scholarly potential, and employment equity goals (Collective Agreement 2002-2005, page 34).
* Search committees shall be proactive in the recruitment of female candidates, and if it is not possible to find a suitable female candidate for the short list, then the search committee will provide the Vice-President Academic with a detailed summary of the special measures that were undertaken to satisfy this requirement (Collective Agreement 2002-2005, page 34).

Note that Article 8.35 does not mention the dates "90" which is likely an error on the part of the drafter.

question: What is stated about selection of chairs/directors?
answer:
According to Article 9.15 - Selection of Chairs/Directors, the process for selecting a Chair or Director includes:

* The Selection Committee shall follow a specific procedure (Article 9.15.3)
* The ballots shall be opened and counted in the presence of the Selection Committee (Article 9.15.8)
* If at least two Members object to an abbreviated selection process, the full procedure must be followed (Article 9.15.14)
* In many selection processes, if a strong consensus emerges for the selection of one candidate, the Selection Committee may proceed directly to step 8 of the procedure (Article 9.15.14)

Additionally, Article 9.20 - Term of Office of Chairs/Directors states that:

* The term of office for Chairs/Directors shall normally be for three years, renewable by Department/School selection (Article 9.20.1)
* If a Chair or Director is unable to carry out their duties for four months or less, they must make provision for the take-over of their duties in consultation with the Department and Dean/University Librarian (Article 9.20.2)
* If the absence is for longer than four months, the Chair or Director shall relinquish their title and a new Chair/Director shall be selected according to the procedures set out in Article 9.15 - Selection of Chairs/Directors (Article 9.20.3)

question: What is stated about discipline?
answer:
According to Article 5.75 of the collective agreement (page numbers not specified), the following points are made regarding discipline:

* Discipline shall be just and reasonable, based on the principle of progressive discipline, except in egregious cases (5.75).
* Just cause is defined as gross misconduct or persistent failure to discharge academic responsibility (5.75.2).
* Just cause must be interpreted in the context of a University environment, including the principles of tenure where applicable (5.75.3).
* Discipline shall be imposed only in compliance with principles of natural justice and due process (5.75.4).
* The Employer may impose the following forms of discipline on full-time Members:
	+ A letter of reprimand
	+ Suspension with pay, but only if cited as a disciplinary measure by the Vice-President, Academic and Provost
	+ Suspension without pay, with a reduction in pay computed as 1/260 of normal salary per day
	+ Withholding of an annual increment
	+ Dismissal (5.75.5(a)).
* The Employer may impose the following forms of discipline on sessional or part-time Members:
	+ A letter of reprimand
	+ Suspension with pay, but only if cited as a disciplinary measure by the Vice-President, Academic and Provost
	+ Suspension without pay, with a reduction in pay computed differently for part-time clinicians (5.75.5(b)).
* When the Employer becomes aware of a matter that may lead to discipline, an investigation must commence within 20 working days, and the Member and Union shall be notified in writing of the nature of the allegations upon commencement of the investigation (5.75.6).

Additionally, Article 37 states that discipline of Members, including dismissal, shall only be for cause, and that discipline shall be just and reasonable, based on progressive discipline, except in serious cases.

However, in the exercise of this freedom in the classroom, reasonable restraint shall be used in introducing matters unrelated to the Member’s subject or discipline."

The President's permission is required for making significant changes to instructional methods or cancelling scheduled instruction, and both parties agree that every reasonable effort will be made to notify students affected by any such changes.

question: How is withdrawal of seniority for addressed in the collective agreement?
answer:
Withdrawal of seniority actions must first be initiated by June 1 in order to be effective for the subsequent academic year (Collective Agreement 2017-2020, Article 4.40.9). 

However, it's worth noting that this provision refers back to clause 4.40.1, which is not included in the provided snippet of the collective agreement. Therefore, I couldn't find any additional information regarding what is meant by clause 4.40.1.

Also, Article 2.95 - WITHDRAWAL OF SENIORITY provides more detailed information on how withdrawal of seniority actions are addressed:

1. The rights established by the provisions for seniority as described above may be altered or revoked in the event that the teaching performance of a Sessional Member is found to be unsatisfactory.
2. Action that may affect the seniority rights of a Sessional Member may be initiated at the request of the Chair of the Academic Unit or the Dean and will normally occur only after an informal investigation establishes reasonable grounds for a formal procedure.

It seems that there are two different provisions regarding withdrawal of seniority in the collective agreement, but both emphasize the importance of initiating such actions by specific deadlines (June 1) to ensure they are effective for the subsequent academic year.

question: According to the agreement, what applies to study leave?
answer:
According to Article 23 - STUDY LEAVE, a study leave with pay is granted to enable a Member to pursue a program of study of benefit to the Member and in order to meet specific needs of the University. Study leave periods may vary to a maximum of twelve (12) months and may be renewable without compensation. A study leave includes the appropriate vacation entitlement proportional to the length of the leave. (Source: LUFA-H Collective Agreement 2016-2020, page 34)

Additionally, according to Article 13 - STUDY LEAVE, a study leave with pay is granted to enable a member to pursue a program of study of benefit to the member and in order to meet specific needs of the University. Study leave periods may vary. Vacation entitlement shall be proportional to the length of the leave. (Source: Collective Agreement 2017-2020)

In terms of compensation, Article 23.02 states that a Member on study leave shall receive 30% of the Member's salary to a maximum of $40,000. (Source: LUFA-H Collective Agreement 2016-2020, page 34)

question: What does the collective agreement provide regarding discipline?
answer:
According to the collective agreement, the Laurentian University Faculty Association has provisions related to discipline in Section 5, specifically Articles 5.70 and 5.75.

Discipline shall be just and reasonable (Article 5.75), based on the principle of progressive discipline, except in egregious cases (Source: Collective Agreement, page number not specified).

There are also specific provisions regarding notification, confidentiality, and due process in disciplinary proceedings:

* The Faculty Personnel Committee's letters or assessments must be kept confidential and used only for the purposes for which they were solicited (Article 5.70.8).
* Student evaluations, if more than five years old, cannot be used as evidence in any process involving a Member's tenure, promotion, or dismissal (Article 5.70.9).
* The Dean/University Librarian must notify the Member and provide an opportunity to respond to allegations before meeting with them (Source: Collective Agreement, page number not specified).

In cases where the Vice-President, Academic and Provost is sat as a hearing panel, notice of five working days will be given to the Member and their union representative (Article 5.75.6).
