question: Qu’est-il indiqué au sujet de droits et privilèges du syndicat?
answer:
Selon l'article 2.40 de la Convention collective 2008-11, le Syndicat a les droits suivants :

* Un bureau équipé dans une aire d'enseignement de l'Université (article 2.40.1.a)
* La salle L-303 comme salon réservé à l'usage des Membres, des administrateurs supérieurs et de leurs invités (article 2.40.1.b)
* Le droit d'utiliser le service de courrier interne de l'Université (article 2.40.2)
* Le droit d'utiliser les locaux universitaires comme salles de réunion selon les mêmes conditions que les autres organisations universitaires (article 2.40.3)
* Le droit d'utiliser les services d'imprimerie et d'informatique de l'Université ainsi que l'équipement audiovisuel au même titre que les autres usagers de l'Université, pourvu que les services en question soient disponibles (article 2.40.4)
* Le droit de porter à un compte mensuel les frais encourus par le Syndicat (article 2.40.5)
* Le droit d'utiliser les fonds alloués aux réductions de charge d'enseignement dans les Départements/Écoles affectés, selon la disponibilité et l'acceptation des règlements universitaires (article 2.40.6)

En outre, le Syndicat a également le droit de participer à certains comités universitaires, tels que le Comité sur la santé et la sécurité de l'Université de Sudbury et le Comité consultatif sur les droits de la personne de l'Université de Sudbury (article 6.03).

question: Qu’est-il indiqué au sujet de congé non rémunéré?
answer:
Selon l'article 7.40 – Congé non rémunéré, un congé sans rémunération peut être accordé à un Membre, selon des conditions acceptables pour l'Université et qui sont spécifiées, au préalable, dans un document écrit envoyé au Syndicat avant la date du congé, et indiquant les arrangements au sujet des avantages sociaux. L'Employeur ne peut pas refuser son autorisation sans raison valable.

De plus, la demande d'un congé non rémunéré, contenant un exposé de l'objet, est soumise par écrit au Doyen/Directeur de bibliothèque au moins six (6) mois à l'avance et une demande de prolongation au moins quatre (4) mois à l'avance. On peut surseoir à ces délais dans des situations particulières.

Il est également précisé que la recommandation touchant la demande de congé non rémunéré est du ressort du Doyen/Directeur de bibliothèque après consultation du Département/de l’École, et que la décision finale appartient au Vice-recteur aux études et provost.

question: Comment la convention collective traite-t-elle de vacances?
answer:
Selon l'article 17.03 de la Convention collective 2015-2018, les membres sont tenus de prendre leurs jours de vacances. Cependant, cette condition n'implique pas que le statut prioritaire a été conféré pour un autre cours (article 4.55.4). Les membres peuvent prendre leurs vacances aux dates qui leur conviennent, mais elles ne peuvent pas s'accumuler d'une année à l'autre.

De plus, les membres doivent transmettre une indication des dates prévues pour prendre des vacances au Doyen/Bibliothécaire en un mois à l'avance (article 117 de la Convention collective 2011-14).

En cas de décès d'un membre, la valeur de tout crédit de vacances inutilisé est payée à son bénéficiaire (article 7.15.5). question: Que dit la convention collective au sujet de surcharges de travail?
answer:
Selon l'article 8.35 de la Convention collective 2017-2020, tous les professeurs à temps plein qui donnent un cours en surcharge et rémunéré reçoivent une allocation spécifique pour les cours commençant après les dates précisées.

En particulier, pour les cours entiers et demi-cours commençant après le 1er juillet 2017 :

* Cours entier : 10 322 $
* Demi-cours : 5 161 $

Cependant, il est important de noter que la convention collective prévoit également des dispositions spécifiques pour les bibliothécaires et les archivistes, qui peuvent être attribués des surcharges et des demi-surcharges conformément à une formule décrite dans le présent article.

De plus, l'article 8.35.3 indique que les parties conviennent qu'une surcharge excessive d'enseignement ou de travail de bibliothécaire professionnel n'est pas souhaitable, et que le doyen ou la bibliothécaire en chef peut limiter le nombre de cours en surcharge qu'un Membre peut accepter pendant une année universitaire, ou l'équivalent à la bibliothèque.

Il est également important de noter que les Membres estimant avoir droit à un paiement de surcharge doivent en faire la demande selon les dispositions de l'article 5.40 – Charge de travail universitaire.

Les Membres désirant réserver une place de stationnement dans un des parcs de stationnement du campus doivent payer les frais établis par l'Université. Les frais de stationnement sont établis après consultation du Comité consultatif sur les services de sécurité où siège un (1) Membre du Syndicat.

De plus, les Membres ayant une invalidité temporaire ou permanente, ou les Membres enceintes, ont droit, sur demande à leur Doyen/Bibliothécaire en chef, à une place de stationnement réservé à proximité de leur bureau.

question: Que prévoit la convention collective concernant comité des affaires professorales?
answer:
Selon l'article 8 de la Convention collective 2015-2018, le Comité des affaires professorales est chargé de faire des recommandations justifiées au Recteur à la suite des demandes faites par les membres en matière :

* Renouvellement de nominations à l’essai
* Promotion
* Permanence
* Subventions de recherche ou de voyages
* Congé sabbatique
* Tout autre affaire dont le Comité peut être saisi (article 8.01).

Le Comité est composé de membres suivants :

* Un représentant qui a la permanence et qui est élu par le Département
* Deux (2) Membres non désignés, ayant la permanence ou à l’essai ayant été élus
* Un membre non désigné à plein temps pour agir comme substitut
* Le Doyen de la Faculté des arts de l'Université Laurentienne, sans droit de vote
* Le Secrétaire général ou un administrateur supérieur chargé des affaires professorales de l’Université, sans droit de vote

Les demandes doivent être déposées avant le 30 septembre de chaque année et comportent tous les documents à l'appui.

question: Que dit la convention collective au sujet de congé d'études?
answer:
Selon l'article 13 de la convention collective, un congé d'études avec traitement est accordé pour permettre à un membre de poursuivre un programme d'études qui lui bénéficiera et pour permettre à l'Université de satisfaire à des besoins spécifiques. Les périodes de congé d'études peuvent varier, et l'admissibilité aux vacances est proportionnelle à la longueur du congé.

question: Selon la convention, qu’est-ce qui s’applique à charge de travail universitaire?
answer:
Selon l'article 5.40.6 de la Convention collective 2017-2020 et Convention collective 2011-14 précises :

La détermination de la charge de travail d'un membre est assujettie aux conditions suivantes :

* Conformément à l'article 3.10 – Liberté universitaire, le Doyen/Bibliothécaire en chef ne doit pas imposer de tâches d'enseignement et de recherche autres que celles précisées à l’alinéa 5.40.5 ci-dessus.
* Le Doyen/Bibliothécaire en chef peut attribuer au membre toute charge relative à sa discipline en tant qu’enseignant, bibliothécaire ou archiviste, ou toute responsabilité administrative que le Doyen/Bibliothécaire en chef juge indispensable au fonctionnement de la faculté, de la bibliothèque ou du programme universitaire en cause.
* La charge de travail d'un membre peut varier selon sa discipline et elle tient compte des aptitudes du membre, de la nécessité d'augmenter ses compétences et des fonctions dont il est chargé dans le cadre du fonctionnement de l’Université.

En outre, la convention précise les normes maximales pour les charges attribuées :

* Membres enseignants : deux (2) cours complets ou l'équivalent de douze (12) crédits par année universitaire.
* Membres bibliothécaires professionnels et archivistes : douze (12) heures de travail auprès des étudiants par semaine, selon un horaire juste et équitable et sur la recommandation de l’unité.

Il convient de noter que les membres dont la nomination est à durée limitée de douze (12) mois peuvent avoir une charge d’enseignement de trois (3) crédits de plus que la charge normale d’enseignement.

question: Que prévoit la convention collective concernant surcharges de travail?
answer:
La convention collective précise les conditions selon lesquelles les membres de l'Université Laurentienne peuvent bénéficier d'une allocation pour surcharge de travail. Selon l'article 8.35, tous les professeurs à temps plein qui enseignent un cours en surcharge et rémunéré reçoivent une allocation spécifique pour les cours commençant après les dates précisées (1er juillet 2017, 2018 et 2019). L'allocation varie en fonction de la durée du cours : pour des cours entiers de six crédits, elle est fixée à 10 322 $ pour le premier semestre et 10 487 $ pour le deuxième semestre, tandis que pour des demi-cours, elle est fixée à 5 161 $ pour le premier semestre et 5 244 $ pour le deuxième semestre. 

Cependant, si un cours d'éducation permanente risque d'être annulé, un membre peut accepter de donner le cours pour un montant moindre que le traitement prévu pour un cours en surcharge. La possibilité d'un tel contrat doit être signalée au Syndicat avant la conclusion de l'accord.

De plus, la convention collective précise également qu'une surcharge démesurée d'enseignement ou de travail de bibliothécaire professionnel n'est pas souhaitable et que le doyen ou la bibliothécaire en chef peut limiter le nombre de cours en surcharge qu'un membre peut accepter au cours d'une année universitaire, ou l'équivalent à la bibliothèque.

question: Quelles conditions s’appliquent à activites universitaires?
answer:
Selon l'article 10.01 de la convention collective en question, les membres de l'unité de négociation ont le droit d'exercer les activités suivantes :

* La transmission et l'expression créatrice du savoir
* L'éclaircissement et l'élargissement des frontières du savoir

question: Selon la convention, qu’est-ce qui s’applique à discipline?
answer:
Selon l'article 5.75 de la Convention collective, la discipline doit être juste et raisonnable, basée sur le principe du progessionnel et, sauf en cas d'égénérésse, elle est appliquée conformément au principe de justice naturelle et processus.

En particulier, les sanctions disciplinaires qui peuvent être infligées à un membre sont :

- La lettre de réprimande (5.75.5a i)
- La suspension avec ou sans pay (5.75.5a ii, iii)
- Le recullement de l'augmentation salariale annuelle (5.75.5a iv)
- L'expulsion du membre (5.75.5a v)
- La suppression des rangs et/ou des établissements (5.75.5b iv)

Il est important de noter que les sanctions disciplinaires sont appliquées en fonction du statut du membre (plein temps ou sessionnel/partenariat) et qu'elles doivent être justes, rationnelles et conformes aux principes de justice naturelle et processus.

question: Quelles conditions s’appliquent à congé d'études?
answer:
Selon l'article 13.01 de la convention collective, un congé d'études avec traitement est accordé pour permettre à un membre de poursuivre un programme d'études qui lui bénéficiera et pour permettre à l'Université de satisfaire à des besoins spécifiques. Les périodes de congé d'études peuvent varier, et l'admissibilité aux vacances est proportionnelle à la longueur du congé.

Il n'y a pas d'autres conditions spécifiées dans le texte fourni pour les congés d'études. Cependant, il convient de noter que les périodes de congé non rémunéré sont régies par l'article 7.40, qui précise les conditions selon lesquelles un congé sans rémunération peut être accordé.

En résumé, pour les congés d'études avec traitement, la condition est que le congé soit utilisé pour poursuivre un programme d'études ou répondre à des besoins spécifiques de l'Université.

question: Comment la convention collective traite-t-elle de conges sabbatioues?
answer:
La convention collective traite des congés sabbatiques aux articles 12.01 et 12.02, qui définissent les conditions d'admissibilité et les modalités de ces congés.

 Selon l'article 12.01, le but d'un congé sabbatique est de favoriser la poursuite de la connaissance et d'aider l'Université à atteindre ses objectifs de recherche en accordant aux membres de manière régulière une occasion de consacrer toute leur énergie à la recherche et à l'étude.

L'article 12.02 précise les conditions d'admissibilité pour les congés sabbatiques :

* Tous les membres à temps plein sont admissibles à des congés sabbatiques consistant en un congé d’une année entière après six ans d’emploi depuis le dernier congé sabbatique, ou d’une demi-année après trois ans d’emploi depuis le dernier congé sabbatique.
* Un membre n'est admissible à un premier congé sabbatique qu'après six ans d'emploi à temps plein à l'Université de Sudbury dans un poste permanent ou à Pessai.
* Si le directeur élu est éligible à un congé sabbatique au cours de son mandat, le Département veillera à ce qu'un directeur intérimaire soit choisi six (6) mois avant son départ en congé sabbatique.

En résumé, la convention collective traite des congés sabbatiques en définissant les conditions d'admissibilité et les modalités de ces congés pour favoriser la poursuite de la connaissance et l'atteinte des objectifs de recherche à l'Université.

question: Que prévoit la convention collective concernant procédure de grief?
answer:
La convention collective prévoit une procédure de grief dans les termes suivants :

* Les grievances peuvent être déposées par l'employeur contre le syndicat concernant l'interprétation, l'application ou l'administration d'une disposition de la convention collective (article 23.01).
* Les employés ont le droit de déposer un grief contre le syndicat en commençant à la première étape de la procédure de règlement des griefs (article 23.04.a).
* Les griefs doivent être déposés par écrit et dans les 21 jours ouvrables suivant l'incident initial ayant donné lieu à la plainte (article 23.04.a).
* Une réunion des représentants de l'employeur et du syndicat a lieu dans les 21 jours ouvrables suivant le dépôt du grief (article 23.04.a).
* Le syndicat répond par écrit au grief dans les 21 jours ouvrables suivant la réunion (article 23.04.a).

Il est également précisé que les personnes concernées par ces procédures ne sont pas exposées à la discrimination, au harcelement ou à la coercition en aucune façon (article 11.10.1). Les deux parties conviennent de faire tous les efforts raisonnables pour régler tous les griefs de façon prompte, juste et équitable (article 11.10.2).

Il convient également de noter que les délais prescrits dans le présent article peuvent être prolongés avec l'accord des deux parties, et qu'un arbitre a le pouvoir de supprimer l'application des délais prescrits (article 11.10.4).

question: Comment la convention définit-elle ou décrit-elle scolarité droits?
answer:
Selon l'article 8.50.1 de la convention collective mentionnée ci-dessus, les droits de scolarité sont définis comme suit :

"Les droits de scolarité seront versés au conjoint et aux personnes à charge des membres employés à temps plein, des membres à temps plein à la retraite, des membres à la retraite décédés et des membres décédés."

En d'autres termes, les droits de scolarité s'appliquent aux conjoints et aux personnes à charge des membres de l'Association des professeurs de l'Université Laurentienne qui sont employés à temps plein ou à la retraite.

La page du document n'est pas spécifiée dans le contexte fourni, mais il est probablement situé sur une page relative à la définition et au calcul des droits de scolarité.

question: Qu’est-il indiqué au sujet de mesures disciplinaires et renvoi?
answer:
Selon l'article 22 de la Convention collective 2015-2018, les mesures disciplinaires et le renvoi sont indiqués au sujet des "motifs valables" qui peuvent justifier ces mesures. Les motifs valables principalement incluent :

*   La conduite inacceptable et non professionnelle
*   L'inobservance des stipulations de la présente Convention collective, excepté les infractions techniques de moindre importance

Les mesures disciplinaires sont proportionnelles aux motifs valables et conformes au principe des mesures disciplinaires progressives.

question: Que dit la convention collective au sujet de fonds de recherche de l’université?
answer:
Selon l'article 6.25 de la Convention collective, les universités fournissent un soutien à la recherche appelé "Fonds de Recherche de l'Université Laurentienne" (FRUL). 

Le montant annuel du soutien est de 160 000 $ pour les membres du corps professoral, et 20 000 $ supplémentaires sont alloués chaque année pour soutenir des travaux de recherche de membres retraités. Un comité de huit membres évalue les demandes de subventions et attribue les fonds en fonction de critères définis par le comité. Les règlements de la compétition annuelle sont clairement établis par consultation et accord avec le syndicat, et les subventions ne dépassent pas 5 000 $ par application.

question: Quelles conditions s’appliquent à convenable contrats?
answer:
Je suis désolé, mais je n'ai trouvé aucune information spécifique sur les conditions applicables à des contrats "convenables" dans le contexte de la convention collective de l'Association des professeurs(e)s de l'Université Laurentienne.

Cependant, je peux vous dire que le texte fourni indique les conditions pour un membre qui est rappelé en vertu du présent article :

* Avoir jusqu'à 30 jours pour accepter l'offre de rappel
* Terminer son autre emploi et entrer dans ses fonctions dès qu'il lui est possible de se libérer de son autre contrat, mais jamais plus de 6 mois après avoir accepté l'offre de réembauche.

question: Quelles conditions s’appliquent à charge de travail universitaire?
answer:
Les conditions qui s'appliquent à la charge de travail universitaire sont celles suivantes :

* Conformément à l'article 3.10 – Liberté universitaire, le Doyen/Bibliothécaire en chef ne doit pas imposer de tâches d'enseignement et de recherche autres que celles précisées à l’Article 5.40.5.
* Le Doyen/Bibliothécaire en chef ne doit pas normalement imposer à un employé une charge de travail supérieure aux normes en cours dans la faculté ou la bibliothèque où il travaille.
* Les parties conviennent qu'une surcharge excessive d'enseignement ou de travail bibliothécaire n'est pas souhaitable et pour cette raison, la rémunération de toutes les surcharges d’enseignement se limite au maximum de douze (12) crédits par année.

Il est également précisé que le Membre ne peut refuser une charge de travail supérieure à deux (2) trimestres sans raison valable, et que le Doyen/Bibliothécaire en chef peut demander à un Membre d'accepter des responsabilités au-delà de la charge normale de travail.

question: Que dit la convention collective au sujet de congés?
answer:
La Convention collective 2015-2018 précise les règles concernant les congés dans son Article 7, notamment :

* Les membres qui se portent candidats à une élection ont droit à un congé rémunéré pour la durée des brefs (Article 14.02, page 35 de 59).
* Un congé sans rémunération peut être accordé à un membre, selon des conditions acceptables pour l'Université et spécifiées dans un document écrit envoyé au Syndicat avant la date du congé (Article 7.40.1).
* Habituellement, la demande d'un congé non rémunéré est soumise par écrit avec un exposé de l'objet (Article 7.40.2).

En outre, les dispositions de la clause 7.45.2 sont applicables aux absences de ce genre.

question: Que prévoit la convention collective concernant congé sabbatique?
answer:
Selon l'article 131 de la Convention collective 2008-11, le congé sabbatique est défini comme une période durant laquelle le Membre est déchargé de ses fonctions habituelles pour lui permettre de :

* Continuer sa formation, poursuivre ses études à un niveau plus avancé dans un centre de recherches ou d'études supérieures, ou suivre des cours de langue (article 131).
* Consacrer plus de temps aux travaux d’érudition ou de création (article 131).
* Renforcer les liens entre l'Université et d'autres universités ou d'autres pays, en tant que professeur ou bi ( article 131).

Il est également précisé qu'habituellement, toute remunération supplémentaire acquise au cours du congé sabbatique ne peut excéder une somme qui porterait le total à cent pour cent (100 %) du traitement usuel du Membre en plus des frais de voyage et des frais de déplacement pour lui, son épouse et leurs enfants à charge. Si cette limite est dépassée, l'Université se réserve le droit de réduire le traitement proportionnellement.

question: Quelles conditions s’appliquent à discipline?
answer:
Selon l'article 37 de la Convention collective de l'Association des professeurs(e)s de l'Université Laurentienne, les conditions pour la discipline sont les suivantes :

1. La discipline du membre doit être only for cause, c'est-à-dire qu'elle doit être motivée par un motif légitime.
2. La discipline doit être juste et raisonnable, basée sur le principe de discipline progressive, sauf en cas graves.

En particulier, la discipline peut être imposée pour :

* Le gross misconduct (ex : le comportement grave et professionnel), 
* La grave et directe violation de la sécurité personnelle d'un autre membre ou d'une étudiante.

question: Selon la convention, qu’est-ce qui s’applique à procédure d’arbitrage?
answer:
Selon la Convention collective 2018-2021, la procédure d'arbitrage est soumise aux dispositions de l'article 24. Ce dernier précise les règles suivantes :

* Lorsqu'une partie souhaite soumettre un grief à arbitrage, elle doit en aviser l'autre partie dans les délais prévus à l'article 23.05 et nommer son représentant au Tribunal d'arbitrage (article 24.01).
* L'autre partie doit nommer son représentant dans les 21 jours ouvrables suivant la réception de cet avis, ou le ministre du Travail de l'Ontario peut procéder à cette nomination à la demande de la partie qui se prévaut de la procédure d'arbitrage (article 24.01).
* Les représentants tentent de choisir un président du Tribunal d'arbitrage en commun accord, mais si cela échoue, le ministre du Travail peut procéder à la nomination (article 24.01).
* Aucune personne ne peut être nommée comme arbitre si elle a été impliquée dans une tentative de négociation ou de règlement du grief (article 24.02).
* Le Tribunal d'arbitrage n'est pas autorisé à prendre des décisions qui ne sont pas conformes aux dispositions de la Convention ni à adapter, modifier, ajouter ou amender quelque partie que ce soit de la présente Convention (article 24.03).
* La décision majoritaire du Tribunal ou, en l'absence d'une majorité, la décision du président est sans appel et contraignante pour les Parties et les membres concernés (article 24.04).
* Les dépenses de représentation sont à la charge des parties, les dépenses encourues par le président sont partagées également entre les deux parties (article 24.05).
* Les délais prescrits dans l'article 24 sont stricts et tout retard, sauf lorsqu'il est convenu par consentement écrit des Parties, est considéré comme un abandon du grief (article 24.06).
* Les Parties peuvent choisir d'avoir la cause entendue par un seul arbitre plutôt que par un Tribunal de trois personnes (article 24.07).

En résumé, la procédure d'arbitrage est soumise aux dispositions de l'article 24, qui précisent les règles pour la nomination des représentants, le choix du président, la responsabilité des dépenses et les délais.

Cependant, il y a un article (11.10.19) qui mentionne l'indemnité de rupture de contrat qu'un Membre pourrait négocier à titre privé avec l'Employeur, mais ce n'est pas spécifiquement le remboursement de la cessation.

question: Comment la convention définit-elle ou décrit-elle congé non rémunéré?
answer:
La convention collective définit le congé non rémunéré comme un congé sans salaire qui peut être accordé à un membre, selon des conditions acceptables pour l'Université et qui sont spécifiées dans un document écrit envoyé au Syndicat avant la date du congé, indiquant les arrangements au sujet des avantages sociaux. (Article 7.40.1)

Selon cette convention, le congé non rémunéré ne peut pas durer plus de deux ans et le membre peut opter pour la cessation ou la continuation des avantages sociaux auxquels il a droit pendant le congé. (Articles 7.40.4 et 7.40.5)

De plus, les dispositions régissant les congés payés ne s'appliquent pas aux membres qui purgent une peine ou qui comparaissent comme témoin pour leur propre compte, mais ce qui les empêche de bénéficier d'un congé non rémunéré est qu'ils sont cités en justice en tant que juré, témoin ou expert-conseil. (Article 7.45.3)

Enfin, les membres à temps partiel qui ont enseigné deux masters par année pendant six années universitaires successives ont droit à une indemnité de congé annuel de 6 %, qu'à ce qu'il y ait une interruption de service. (Article 7.40.5)

question: Que prévoit la convention collective concernant droits de l’administration?
answer:
Selon l'article 5.01 de la convention collective, le Syndicat reconnaît que l'Employeur conserve, possède et peut exercer tous les droits et fonctions, pouvoirs, privilèges et autorité que l'Employeur possédait avant la signature de cette Convention avec le Syndicat, à l'exception de ceux qui sont clairement et spécifiquement abandonnés ou restreints dans la présente Convention, ou légalement modifiés. L'Employeur s'engage à exercer tous droits et fonctions, pouvoirs, privilèges et autorité conformément aux dispositions de la présente Convention.

Cela signifie que l'Employeur conserve ses anciens droits et responsabilités, mais ceux-ci sont soumis à certaines limites et modifications définies dans la convention collective.

question: Que prévoit la convention collective concernant ci-dessus?
answer:
D'après le texte fourni, la Convention collective semble aborder plusieurs sujets :

1. La définition des langues officielles et les modalités de traduction du document (Article 1.15).
2. Les objectifs de la Convention collective, notamment l'établissement des règles d'emploi, la promotion et le maintien de liens harmonieux entre le Syndicat et l'Employeur, ainsi que le soutien aux Parties dans leur travail commun en matière de recherche et d'enseignement (Article 1.20).
3. Les objectifs spécifiques de l'Université Laurentienne, notamment l'avancement de la connaissance et la diffusion du savoir, ainsi que l'épanouissement des membres sur le plan intellectuel, social, moral et physique (Article 1.25).
4. Les définitions utilisées dans la Convention collective, telles que les annuaires universitaires, les bibliothécaires en chef, les chargés de cours cliniques, etc. (Article 1.30).
5. La reconnaissance de l'Association comme agent négociateur exclusif des unités de négociation définies par les certificats de la Commission des relations du travail de l'Ontario (Article 2.15).
6. Les dispositions concernant le renouvellement du corps professoral, notamment le programme spécial de retraite anticipée volontaire (Annexe C).

Il est important de noter que ces informations sont contenues dans plusieurs articles et annexes de la Convention collective, et qu'il est possible qu'il y ait d'autres sujets abordés dans le document.

question: Qu’est-il indiqué au sujet de objectifs de l'université?
answer:
Selon l'article 1.01 de la Convention collective de l'Association des professeur(e)s de l'Université Laurentienne, les buts de la présente Convention collective sont :

* L’établissement des conditions d’emploi et autres dispositions contractuelles particulières
* La promotion et le maintien de liens harmonieux entre les Parties
* Le soutien aux Parties dans leur travail commun dans l'élaboration de la recherche et de l'enseignement permettant de dispenser aux étudiants un enseignement de haute qualité
* La mise en place de moyens permettant de résoudre les différends éventuels

Il est important de noter que ces objectifs sont spécifiques à la présente Convention collective et ne concernent pas nécessairement les objectifs généraux de l'Université.

question: Que prévoit la convention collective concernant conges sabbatioues?
answer:
Selon l'article 12 de la Convention collective 2018-2021, les membres à temps plein sont admissibles à des congés sabbatiques consistants en un congé d’une année entière après six ans d’emploi depuis le dernier congé sabbatique, ou d’une demi-année après trois ans d’emploi depuis le dernier congé sabbatique.

Cela signifie que les membres qui ont travaillé au moins 6 ans sans prendre un congé sabbatoire sont éligibles à un congé de 1 an pour se consacrer à la recherche et à l'étude. Si un membre a travaillé moins de 3 ans depuis le dernier congé sabbatique, il est admissible à un congé de 0,5 an.

Il convient également de noter que si le directeur élu est éligible à un congé sabbatique au cours de son mandat, le Département veillera à ce qu’un directeur intérimaire soit choisi six (6) mois avant son départ en congé sabbatique.

question: What are the rules concerning absence: general?
answer:

question: What does the collective agreement provide regarding pregnancy, parental and adoption?
answer:
According to the provided context from the Laurentian University Faculty Association Collective Agreement 2017-2020 (pages 1, 5, and unspecified), a pregnant full-time Member or Master Lecturer Member is entitled to seventeen (17) weeks of pregnancy leave. During this period, the member receives one-hundred percent (100%) of her nominal salary for the first week, and up to sixteen additional weeks with reduced pay.

If a newborn child is hospitalized, a Member may postpone or interrupt her pregnancy leave by the number of weeks the newborn child is hospitalized, but this must be taken within fifty-two (52) weeks from the date of birth.

For parental leave, the member who is not entitled to take parental leave under applicable laws shall have her pregnancy leave end on the later of either seventeen (17) weeks after the pregnancy leave began or six (6) weeks after the birth.

Adoption leaves are not explicitly detailed in the provided context, but as per the French version of the document (page unspecified), a Member who is adopting an child and chooses to take parental leave under applicable laws has the right to a maximum parental leave of thirty-five (35) weeks. During the adoption leave, the member receives one-hundred percent (100%) of her nominal salary for five days after working for at least twelve (12) consecutive months.

question: According to the agreement, what applies to professional development?
answer: According to the Laurentian University Faculty Association (LUFA) Collective Agreement 2016-2020, each full-time member is eligible to receive a professional allowance for each contractual year, which can be spent on expenses related to approved academic research or professional purposes. This allowance is cumulative over two (2) academic years (Article 30.01, page 47). Sessional members are also eligible for professional development money of up to $2,000, with $250 per each three credit course they teach (Article 30.07, page 48).

question: According to the agreement, what applies to hufac?
answer: The Laurentian University Faculty Association (LUFA-H) Collective Agreement states that there is a Huntington University Faculty Affairs Committee (HUFAC). This committee's role includes providing recommendations to the President on renewal of probationary appointments, promotion, and tenure for faculty members (Article 14.01, page 25). The committee's recommendation is considered by the President in making a decision on the application. The committee's recommendation, as well as the President's decision and reasons for it, must be set forth in written form (Article 14.10, page 25). An applicant may ask a HUFAC member to recuse herself/himself if a conflict of interest exists, and the chair of the committee may also require a member to recuse themselves under similar circumstances (Article 14.03, page 25). If an applicant requests a member to recuse themselves or the chair deems it necessary, the chair shall render a decision with reasons in writing (Article 14.03, page 25). Additionally, the committee's recommendation is sent to the applicant at the same time it is sent to the President, and all letters of recommendation include information about the member's right to make written representations within ten working days (Article 14.08, page 25).

question: What does the collective agreement provide regarding academic workload?
answer:
According to the Laurentian University Faculty Association Collective Agreement (2008-11), the academic workload is assigned in a fair and equitable manner by the President. The workload includes teaching/librarianship, scholarly activity, and governance and community service (Article 12 - Workload, page 48).

Furthermore, for promotion to Full Librarian or Full Archivist, at least ten years of full-time professional service relevant to academic librarianship or archival management is required (Article 5.10.4, page 48).

Additionally, the academic workload shall be assigned with each member receiving a copy of the Chair's/Director’s recommendations to the Dean/University Librarian on their own workload and a summary of the recommendations for all other members in the Department/School (Article 5.40 - Academic Workload, page not specified).

answer: The Thorneloe-LUFA Collective Agreement (2017-2020) states that there shall be no discrimination or harassment with respect to any Member, regardless of various personal factors such as age, race, language, creed, color, ancestry, ethnic or cultural background, national origin, political or religious beliefs (Article 3.01, page 3). Furthermore, there shall be no intimidation, discrimination, or coercion because of any employee's membership or non-membership in the Union or their activity or lack of activity in the Union (Article 3.02, page 3 & 4). Academic freedom is also protected, allowing for free expression of beliefs and research results, teaching, discussion, and criticism (Article 3, page 11).

question: How does the agreement define or describe selection of chairs/directors?
answer:
The Laurentian University Faculty Association collective agreement defines and describes the selection process for chairs/directors as follows:

1. The selection process begins with the creation of a Selection Committee, composed of faculty members (9.15.1).
2. The Selection Committee is responsible for reviewing applications and conducting interviews, if necessary (9.15.3).
3. After the interviews, the Selection Committee casts ballots and the ballots are opened and counted in their presence (9.15.8).
4. The Chair of the Selection Committee reports the results of the selection process and its recommendation to the Dean/University Librarian (9.15.9).
5. If the Dean/University Librarian agrees with the Selection Committee's recommendation, they forward it, along with their own, to the Vice-President, Academic and Provost, who makes the appointment (9.15.10).
6. In case the Dean/University Librarian and the Selection Committee cannot agree on an appointment, the selection procedure is reinstituted as in Article 9.15.3 above (9.15.11).
7. The appointed Chair/Director must be a tenured or probationary Member of faculty (9.15.12).
8. In exceptional circumstances, the Vice-President, Academic and Provost and the Dean/University Librarian can appoint an acting Chair/Director for up to four months, adhering to the terms outlined in Articles 9.20 – Term of Office of Chairs/Directors and 9.30 – Removal from Office of Chairs/Directors (9.15.13).

Source: Laurentian University Faculty Association Collective Agreement, Articles 9.15.1-9.15.14.

question: What conditions apply to academic freedom?
answer:
According to the Laurentian University Faculty Association (LUFA) collective agreement, the conditions that apply to academic freedom include:

1. The right to search for truth, knowledge, and understanding and to express freely what one believes (Article 2.01).
2. The commitment to the pursuit of truth, the advancement of learning, and the creation, interpretation, preservation, and dissemination of knowledge (Article 2.02a).
3. The obligation to base all research and teaching on a responsible search for truth and knowledge (Article 2.02b).
4. The fulfillment of responsibilities to other Members of the teaching and learning community (Article 2.02b).
5. The acknowledgement of the work of others and the acceptance of responsibility for one’s own beliefs and utterances (Article 2.02c).
6. Academic freedom does not confer legal immunity (Article 2.02d).

Source: LUFA-H Collective Agreement 2016-2020, pages 4.

question: How does the agreement define or describe discipline?
answer: Discipline, according to the Laurentian University Faculty Association collective agreement (Forced Contract, page 5), is defined as being just and reasonable, based on the principle of progressive discipline, except in egregious cases. Just cause for discipline is defined as gross misconduct including serious unprofessional behavior and/or misconduct constituting a grave and direct violation of the personal safety of another member, members of the University community, and/or students of the University community (5.75.2). The agreement also states that the Member and their union representative should be given five working days' notice of any disciplinary meeting, and the Dean/University Librarian shall review with the member the particulars of the allegation and provide them with the opportunity to respond (5.75.6). All correspondence regarding discipline from the Employer to Members of the Bargaining Unit must be copied to the Union simultaneously (Article 10, page 9).

question: What does the collective agreement provide regarding responsibility colleagues?
answer:
The Laurentian University Faculty Association (LUFA) collective agreement outlines several responsibilities towards colleagues, as described in the context provided:

1. Respecting a respectful workplace and learning environment, which is stipulated in the Laurentian Policy on A Respectful Workplace and Learning Environment (Ethical and fair dealing with clients and colleagues).
2. Fostering a free exchange of ideas.
3. Avoiding discrimination.
4. Respecting principles of confidentiality in a manner consistent with their academic role.
5. Acknowledging their indebtedness to their academic colleagues in relation to their own professional activities.
6. Sessional Members are accountable to the President for fulfilling the conditions of their contracted employment as defined by this Collective Agreement, which includes expectations defined by Article 9.15 – Selection of Chairs/Directors and Article 11.02 Rights and Responsibilities as Part-Time Teachers (LUFA-H Collective Agreement 2016-2020 15).
7. Full-time academic staff have an obligation to develop and maintain their scholarly competence and effectiveness as teachers/librarians within the area of their expertise, which includes taking advantage of opportunities for professional/academic development or upgrading where appropriate (LUFA-H Collective Agreement 2016-2020 15).

question: What are the rules concerning leave requesting?
answer:
The rules concerning leave requests for members of Laurentian University Faculty Association are outlined as follows:

1. For shorter periods of absence due to illness, no specific notice period is required (5.50.07 a). However, if the sick leave exceeds five consecutive working days, a report is required (5.50.06 b).

2. In case the member's sick leave pattern raises doubts about the claim, even if the individual's sick leave periods are short enough not to require medical certificates, a report will still be necessary (5.50.06 b).

3. Members can apply for leave without pay for a longer period of absence according to Article 5.30 – Leave Without Pay (5.55.3).

4. Extended parental leave without pay, up to a maximum of one year, is given to members who request it (5.50.08).

5. A full-time member can take a paid leave of absence for up to two weeks to fulfill responsibilities related to the special needs of a family member (5.50.09).

6. The notice period in 5.50.07 a does not apply if the member stops working because the child comes into their custody, care, and control sooner than expected (5.50.07 b).

Source: Laurentian University Faculty Association Collective Agreement 2018-2023, pages 31-32.

question: According to the agreement, what applies to family responsibility leave for full-time faculty?
answer: According to the Laurentian University Faculty Association (LUFA) Collective Agreement (2), a full-time faculty member is entitled to seventeen (17) weeks of Pregnancy Leave. During the first two (2) weeks, they receive 100% of their nominal salary. For up to fifteen (15) additional weeks, they receive an amount equal to the difference between their Employment Insurance (EI) benefits and their nominal salary (LUFA-H Collective Agreement 2, Article 25.01). They also continue to participate in the pension plan and other benefit plans during this leave, and may claim sick leave for absences due to illnesses (LUFA-H Collective Agreement 2, Article 25.09). Nothing in the agreement prevents a member from applying for tenure one year prior to the final year of their probationary status (LUFA-H Collective Agreement 2, Tenure Evaluation).

answer:
The Collective Agreement states that within ten (10) working days from the final receipt of names from the Department/School, the Chair of the Selection Committee shall make all reasonable efforts to provide all full-time Members of the Department/School, including those on leave, with a ballot. In case only one suitable candidate is found, the Chair of the Selection Committee shall use all reasonable efforts to submit to all the full-time Members of the Department/School, including those on leave, a ballot showing this candidate's name, with time limits as set out in Article 9.15.7 (Collective Agreement 2017-2020, 9.15.8).

question: How is professional development addressed in the collective agreement?
answer:
The Laurentian University Faculty Association (LUFA) Collective Agreement addresses professional development in several ways.

1. Personal Development and Career Advancement: The University recognizes the importance of personal development and career advancement for staff members. According to Article 10.40.1, the parties agree that the University is best served when staff have such opportunities (LUFA-H Collective Agreement 2016-2020, p. 47).

2. Expenditures: To further this objective, full-time Counsellors are supported by $500 in expenditures in each contractual year (Collective Agreement 2002-2005, p. 31).

3. Sabbatical Leaves: Members may request a sabbatical leave to contribute to their scholarly, pedagogical, or professional development. The dossier for a sabbatical leave should include the report of the previous sabbatical, an outline of proposed plans, and an updated curriculum vitae (LUFA-H Collective Agreement 2016-2020, p. 31).

4. Sessional Members: Sessional members are eligible for professional development money of $250 per each three credit course they teach, up to a limit of $2,000 (LUFA-H Collective Agreement 2016-2020, p. 47).

The specific requirements and procedures for each type of professional development may vary, as outlined in the respective articles of the collective agreement.

question: What are the rules concerning copyright?
answer:
The Laurentian University Faculty Association collective agreement (hereafter referred to as "the Agreement") outlines rules concerning copyright. According to Article 15 of the Agreement (page <<>>), copyright applies to all original written, artistic, and recorded works. These works include but are not limited to various materials such as books, articles, lectures, videos, and digital content like interactive textbooks or coursework delivered on the Internet (15.01).

When it comes to third-party use of a work to which the University has copyright under the terms of this Article, net proceeds from any fees or royalties received will be distributed according to Article 6.35.15 (page <<>>) and no additional payment will be given to the Member. The term "Net Proceeds" refers to the fees and royalties received less the cost of reproduction, administration, and distribution (6.35.14).

As for the distribution of net proceeds, it is stated that:
- If practicable, Members may receive a copy of any work they produced for the University at a cost not exceeding the cost of the medium upon which the work has been produced (6.35.16)
- The University may erase or destroy part or all of a work to which it holds copyright under specific conditions (6.35.17, not provided in context)

Regarding workload, Sessional Members' workload normally should not exceed twelve (12) credits per Fall/Winter session and nine (9) credits per Spring session, with no maximum course load or enrolment limit for individuals who conduct instruction through distance education delivery mode (4.25.3).

The librarian pay equivalent is deemed to be 126 hours per 3 course credits of pay (page 19).

question: According to the agreement, what applies to voluntary reduced workload?

The request for such a reduction must be made by the member themselves, and the report of the agreement will become part of their personnel file. Members on study leave must obtain written approval in advance for any paid activity. Time spent on study leave does not count towards sabbatical credit (page 77).

question: According to the agreement, what applies to promotion procedures?
answer:
According to the Laurentian University Faculty Association collective agreement (page 23), the promotion procedure involves several criteria. A member is eligible to apply for promotion while on leave, and the Member is responsible for maintaining contact with the University during this period (Article 16.01-16.02).

For promotions, assessments from additional colleagues with relevant qualifications and experience can be requested by the probationer (Article 16.03(iii)). The promotion is usually effective on 1st July of the academic year following the year in which the application was made and approved (Article 16.05).

Regarding additional qualification increments, these are awarded when a Member's salary exceeds $173,328 per annum, and an amount of $2,900 is given (Article 8.30). Promotion and Merit increments are awarded according to Articles 8.15 – Progress-Through-The-Ranks-Increment and 8.25 – Merit Increments in the agreement.

question: What conditions apply to selection of chairs/directors?
answer:
The selection of chairs/directors at Laurentian University is governed by the following conditions as outlined in the Laurentian University Faculty Association collective agreement (page numbers omitted for brevity):

1. An abbreviated or standard selection process takes place, which includes forming a Selection Committee, opening and counting ballots in their presence, and reporting the results to the Dean/University Librarian (Article 9.15.3, Article 9.15.4, Article 9.15.9).

2. The Dean/University Librarian then forwards the recommendation, along with their own, to the Vice-President, Academic and Provost who makes the appointment (Article 9.15.10).

3. If the Dean/University Librarian and the Selection Committee cannot agree on an appointment, the selection procedure is reinstituted as in Article 9.15.3 (Article 9.15.11).

4. The Chair/Director must be a tenured or probationary member of faculty, or an outside appointment can be made in accordance with Article 5.20 – Appointment and Renewal (Article 9.15.12).

5. In exceptional circumstances, the Vice-President, Academic and Provost and the Dean/University Librarian, after consultation with a Department/School, may appoint an acting Chair/Director for up to four months (Article 9.15.13).

The Employer also grants the Union a non-exclusive, royalty-free, irrevocable, indivisible, and non-transferable right to use solely for the University (Article 6.30.7, page 9). However, it is important to note that these rights are subject to the Employer's management rights as outlined in Article 6 (page 6), which includes the right to discipline for just cause.

Additionally, support services such as telephones, computing, printing, duplicating, library services, technical services, Department/School resources are to be provided in a fair and equitable manner. The Worker is also expected to work in compliance with the Act and regulations, report any hazards or contravention of this Act to the supervisor, wear required protective equipment, not operate or use any equipment in such a manner as to endanger themselves or others, among other safety guidelines.

question: What conditions apply to redundancy?
answer:
The conditions for redundancy, as defined in the Laurentian University Faculty Association collective agreement, are outlined in Articles 11.10 and 5.40.

1. Redundancies can only be dealt with through the procedures specified in Article 11.10 (p. XX).
2. The term "redundancy" does not apply to limited-term appointments that carry no implication of renewal or continuation beyond the stated term, as per Article 5.20 (p. XX).
3. A redundancy, specifically referred to as a workload redundancy, shall not be declared if it results in insufficient academic personnel for a Department(s)/School(s) to continue offering a viable program(s), with the Employer having the onus to demonstrate that proposed reductions are consistent with normal workloads and will not create an inequitable workload (p. XX).
4. During a declared redundancy, the Member retains all other rights and responsibilities as defined in this Collective Agreement (specific page number unclear in provided context).
5. In case of a complaint related to a redundancy, the Vice-President, Academic and Provost shall instruct the Dean/University Librarian to appoint an Acting-Chair/Director, and the President shall create an ad hoc committee to investigate the complaint (p. XX).

question: How is professional development expenditure addressed in the collective agreement?
answer:
According to the Laurentian University Faculty Association (LUFA) Collective Agreement 2016-2020, page 47, the parties agree that the University supports personal development and career advancement of staff. The agreement also mentions specific amounts for professional development expenditure:

Additionally, members may transfer accumulated credits into their professional development expenditure account at any time (not specified with a page number in the provided context). After completing supervisory work, members are required to report its completion to the Dean, who will either register the credit on the member's workload credit account or transfer the funds to the member's professional development expense account (Article 10.40.1, no specific page number provided in context).

question: What is stated about personnel files?
answer: According to the provided context from the Laurentian University Faculty Association Collective Agreement, the official personnel files of a member are kept by the President and are the property of the Employer (page 42 of both versions of the agreement). Members have the right to examine their personnel files upon making prior arrangements, with confidential material being removed prior to inspection. There shall be two types of files for members: active files and archival files. Active files contain only information allowed under this Article, while archival files contain material that has been banned for use in subsequent proceedings but is required by the University for matters other than those related to the Collective Agreement (pages 42-43). Members also have the right to examine their personnel files during normal business hours, with an inventory of confidential material being provided upon request (page 5.70.2). Additionally, members may request a copy of their personnel file, excluding confidential material, at no charge (page 5.70.3). Members also have the right to supplement, correct, or request the removal of false, irrelevant, or unsubstantiated material from their personnel files (pages 5.70.4-5.70.5). Lastly, anonymous material concerning any member shall not be kept by the Employer for inclusion in the Member's personnel file, and statistical summaries of student evaluations or written summaries of student comments unrelated to Senate sanctioned course evaluations shall remain available (page 5.70.4). In another version of the agreement, it is stated that the official personnel files are kept by the Office of the President and are the only file used in decisions respecting terms and conditions of employment of a Member except as required by law (page 18.01).

question: What does the agreement say about dismissal procedures?
answer: According to the Laurentian University Faculty Association Collective Agreement for the years 2017-2020 (page 35), neither failure to renew a term or probationary appointment, decision not to grant tenure, nor termination of an appointment for retirement purposes is considered dismissal, as long as these actions are in accordance with the agreement. Just cause for dismissal is defined as gross misconduct including serious unprofessional behavior and/or misconduct constituting a grave and direct violation of another member's personal safety (page 34). If discipline is imposed, the notice shall provide the nature of the disciplinary action, reasons for it, and the events or conduct being relied upon to support it. Any record of discipline will be removed from a member's personnel file after 24 months, provided no subsequent infractions of a similar nature have occurred within that period (page 36).

answer: According to the Laurentian University Faculty Association collective agreement (source document name not specified), if parties are unable to agree upon a chairperson/arbitrator within 20 working days of the appointment of the second nominee, they can request the Minister of Labour for Ontario to appoint one (Article 24.01). A technical violation or irregularity due to clerical, typographical, or technical error in the written specification of a grievance will not prevent the substance of the grievance from being heard and judged on its merits (Article 12.10.7 and Article 23.10). Written notice of referring a grievance to arbitration must be given within the time limits set out in Article 23.05, and at the same time, parties must appoint their nominee to the Arbitrator (Article 24.01).

question: How does the agreement define or describe appointment and renewal?

The Laurentian University Faculty Association collective agreement defines an appointment as a position held by a member within the ranks of Lecturer, Assistant Professor, Associate Professor, Full Professor, and their corresponding library ranks (General Librarian/Archivist, Assistant Librarian/Archivist, Associate Librarian/Archivist, Full Librarian/Archivist) (5.20.5). Correspondence regarding appointments or changes in terms and conditions of employment must be in writing and copied to the union simultaneously (Article 10 - Correspondence). In some cases, the Dean/University Librarian may work together with the Department/School to substitute one of the short-listed names for an appointment. (5.20.5)

question: What are the rules concerning sabbatical leaves?
answer:
The rules concerning sabbatical leaves at Laurentian University Faculty Association, as outlined in the collective agreement (page numbers not provided due to formatting constraints), are as follows:

1. A sabbatical leave can be for a period of 12 months, starting on July 1, or for 6 months starting on July 1 or January 1. The academic year in which a sabbatical leave is taken does not count towards the years of eligibility entitlement. The leave includes appropriate vacation entitlement proportional to the length of the leave (Article 22.07).

2. Members will be covered for periods of sick leave to the extent of the actual salary paid during that period, and must be provided with specific information concerning Long-Term Disability coverage at the time of appointment (Article 7.55). They may contribute to the pension plan and carry life insurance based on their actual salary (Articles not specified).

3. Members who terminate their employment between June 1 and Labour Day, and who have no formal teaching duties during all or part of that period, shall take and be deemed to have taken as much of their vacation entitlement as possible during that period. In the event of a member's death, the value of any unused vacation entitlement will be paid to their estate (Article 5.20).

4. When Members take a sabbatical leave after three years, all accumulated years of eligibility are exhausted except as otherwise provided for by this Collective Agreement. If the sabbatical leave is postponed, the Member shall receive one year sabbatical credit for the year postponed so that their next sabbatical leave will occur according to their original sabbatical rotation (Article not specified).

5. Immediately following the completion of a sabbatical leave, the member is required to return to the University for a period equal to the length of the leave taken, or to satisfy some other arrangement that is mutually acceptable to the member and the Employer (Article 12.20).

question: What is stated about family responsibility?
answer:

If a child comes into the custody, care, and control of the parent sooner than expected, the notice period does not apply (LUFA-H Collective Agreement 2016-2020, page 39).

However, the collective agreement mentions parental leave and the continuation of group benefits during this leave (LUFA-H Collective Agreement 2016-2020, page 39 & 40). Therefore, it can be inferred that family responsibilities are recognized as a reason for leaves, and members can continue to receive benefits during their parental leave.

For more detailed information about family responsibilities, it would be beneficial to review other sections of the collective agreement or consult with an authorized representative.

question: What does the collective agreement provide regarding discipline?
answer:
The Laurentian University Faculty Association collective agreement (2017-2020) provides that discipline shall be just and reasonable, based on the principle of progressive discipline, except in egregious cases (5.75.2). Just cause for discipline includes gross misconduct such as serious unprofessional behavior or misconduct that constitutes a grave and direct violation of another member's personal safety (5.75.2(a)). Additionally, it states that persistent failure to discharge academic responsibility is also grounds for discipline (5.75.2(b)). The Member and their union representative shall be given five working days’ notice of any disciplinary meeting, during which the Dean/University Librarian shall review the allegations with the Member and provide them an opportunity to respond (5.75.6). The Parties are expected to attempt to resolve the matter in a manner acceptable to all concerned (5.75.6).

question: What does the agreement say about sabbatical leaves?
answer:
The Laurentian University Faculty Association (LUFA) Collective Agreement states that compensation for sabbatical leaves is determined by the Collective Agreement in place. The salary, benefits, and other provisions will be adjusted according to any new agreement between the Board and the Association (LUFA-H Collective Agreement 2016-2020, page 33). However, it's important to note that the bargaining unit does not include full-time faculty on reduced assignments, persons employed through the Centre for Continuing Education, persons employed to teach courses primarily for students who are not registered in a degree credit program, and persons not assigned responsibilities (Collective Agreement 2008-11, page 215).

The decision regarding sabbatical leaves is made by the President, who shall transmit the decision to the member no later than 15 January of the academic year preceding that in which the leave is to take place. The President's decision shall not be arbitrary or in bad faith (Collective Agreement 2018-2021, page 12). A member who takes a 12-month sabbatical leave shall receive a sabbatical stipend (Collective Agreement 2018-2021, page 35).

question: What is stated about academic workload?
answer: According to the Laurentian University Faculty Association collective agreement (page numbers not provided as they are part of a single document), the academic workload is assigned in a fair and equitable manner. It includes teaching/librarianship, scholarly activity, and governance and community service. The Chair or Director provides each member with a copy of their recommended workload and summaries for all other members in the department, including any recommendations for overloads, before these recommendations are forwarded to the Dean or University Librarian (Article 5.40.1). During evaluations for probationary appointments, committees review both prior performance and provide necessary formative comments on what is required for tenure and any concerns about satisfactory performance (Article 15.02). The President is responsible for assigning the academic workload in a fair and equitable manner (Article 12.01).

question: What does the collective agreement provide regarding disciplinary measures?
answer:
The Laurentian University Faculty Association collective agreement provides that disciplinary action shall be just and reasonable, commensurate with the offense (Page 16). The cause for such disciplinary measures includes serious unprofessional behavior and failure to comply with any of the provisions of the Collective Agreement, except minor technical violations (Page 16).

The only formal Disciplinary Measures that can be taken against a Member are:
1. A letter of reprimand, specifying the grounds and adding this reprimand to the member's personnel file (Page 16).
2. Suspension with or without pay for a specified period (Page 17).
3. Demotion in rank (Page 18).
4. Dismissal (termination of employment) (Page 19).

In case of discipline, the Member and their union representative shall be given five working days' notice of the time and place of the meeting, and the Dean/University Librarian shall review with the member the particulars of the allegation and provide the Member with the opportunity to respond (Page 16 & 17).

Discipline should be based on the principle of progressive discipline, except in egregious cases. Just cause is defined as gross misconduct including serious unprofessional behavior and/or misconduct constituting a grave and direct violation of the personal safety of another Member, Members of the University community, and/or students of the University community, or persistent failure to discharge academic responsibility (Page 16).

question: What conditions apply to vacation?
answer:
According to the Laurentian University Faculty Association collective agreement, there are several conditions that apply to vacation.

1. Members are required to take the vacation to which they are entitled and cannot accumulate it from year to year (17.03).
2. During vacation periods, members will continue to receive their normal earnings (17.04).
3. There is no remuneration in lieu of vacation for members who choose not to take the vacation entitlement (17.04).
4. Designated holidays off from work are also provided without any loss of regular earnings, as stated in Article 16.03.
5. For full-time members, vacation is granted based on their years of service:
   a) Members with less than one year of service receive vacation according to the Employment Standards Act.
   b) Members who have completed one year of continuous service as of June 30 in any year receive vacation for one month or 23 working days in the following twelve months (17.01).

question: How is study leaves addressed in the collective agreement?
answer: Study leaves are addressed in Article 7.30 of the Laurentian University Faculty Association (LUFA) Collective Agreement for the period 2016-2020. A study leave is a leave granted for the purpose of upgrading academic qualifications, typically through the attainment of a higher degree or an equivalent acceptable to the University and the Department/School (page 34). The length of such leaves shall normally not exceed two (2) years during a Member's academic career. Study leave eligibility is granted to tenured and probationary members as stated in 7.30.1 (pages 34-35). Regarding remuneration, a Member on study leave shall receive 30% of their salary up to a maximum of $40,000 (page 34). However, time spent on any other type of leave with a period of more than six months does not count towards the eligibility requirements or years of service for determining salary while on study leave.

question: What is stated about academic personnel committee?
answer:
The academic personnel committee, referred to as the Academic Personnel Committee (APC) in the Laurentian University Faculty Association collective agreement, is a body composed of five tenured members and a Dean as Chair. This committee reviews applications for renewal of probationary appointments, tenure, promotion, and merit increments (Article 5.55.1). The APC ensures all applications are fairly and completely assessed according to the terms of the Collective Agreement (Article 5.55.1).

The structure of the APC includes five eligible tenured members, a Dean as Chair who ensures proper procedures are followed but has no vote, and one liaison member designated from among the voting members to serve as liaison with the President (4.25.1a). Membership falls below five due to disability, leave, or termination of employment, the reduced number shall be deemed to constitute quorum, unless the membership falls below three (4.25.1d).

All recommendations of the APC are recorded and must set forth their findings and grounds for recommendation (4.25.2b). These recommendations are kept in the office of the President and available to members of the committee (4.25.2b). Committee members make their recommendation in a manner consistent with the Collective Agreement (4.25.2b).

Members who have a matter before the APC, members on leave, untenured faculty within the same department or program as a candidate for renewal or tenure are not eligible to sit on the APC for that academic year (4.25.1b). Members on leave may request permission to be included in its membership (4.25.1b), and no new member can be added to the APC in the midst of deliberations on a specific application (4.25.1c).

Sources:

- 2014-2017 Thorneloe-LUFA Collective Agreement, page 22

question: What are the rules concerning sabbatical leaves?
answer:
According to the Laurentian University Faculty Association collective agreement (page not specified), the rules concerning sabbatical leaves are as follows:

1. A sabbatical leave is for a period of twelve (12) months, commencing on 1st July, or six (6) months commencing on 1st July or 1st January. No portion of the academic year in which a sabbatical leave is taken shall count toward the years of eligibility entitlement. A sabbatical leave includes the appropriate vacation entitlement proportional to the length of the leave (Source: page 22.07).

2. Members who terminate their employment between June 1 and Labour Day, and who have no formal teaching duties during all or part of that period, shall take and be deemed to have taken as much of their vacation entitlement as possible during that period (Source: Article 5.20 - Sabbatical Leave).

3. In the event of the death of a Member, the value of any unused vacation entitlement will be paid to her/his estate (Source: Article 5.20 - Sabbatical Leave).

4. When Members take a sabbatical leave after three (3) years, all accumulated years of eligibility are exhausted except as otherwise provided for by this Collective Agreement. If the sabbatical leave is postponed, the Member shall receive one (1) year sabbatical credit for the year postponed so that their next sabbatical leave will occur according to their original sabbatical rotation (Source: page not specified).

5. Sabbaticals after three (3) years can be granted provided that Members have tenure when they leave (Source: page not specified).

6. Immediately following the completion of a sabbatical leave, the member is required to return to the University for a period equal to the length of the leave taken, or to satisfy some other arrangement that is mutually acceptable to the member and the Employer (Source: Article 12.20).

question: How does the agreement define or describe family responsibility leave for full-time faculty?
answer:
The Laurentian University Faculty Association (LUFA) collective agreement defines Family Responsibility Leave for full-time faculty in Article 25. Specifically, Pregnancy Leave is detailed in section 25.01. A pregnant member is entitled to seventeen (17) weeks of Pregnancy Leave, during which they receive:

1. For the first two (2) weeks, 100% of their nominal salary (LUFA-H Collective Agreement 2).
2. For up to a maximum of fifteen (15) additional weeks, an amount equal to the difference between the Employment Insurance (EI) benefits received by the Member (LUFA-H Collective Agreement 2).

During this leave, the faculty member continues to participate in the pension and benefit plans set out in the agreement, and both the member and employer continue to pay their applicable shares of contributions and premiums unless the member elects not to do so in writing (LUFA-H Collective Agreement 2). It is also noted that nothing in this Article prevents a Member from claiming sick leave for absences from work due to illnesses (LUFA-H Collective Agreement 2).

However, the collective agreement does not provide specific details about other types of family responsibility leaves beyond Pregnancy Leave. For further information regarding additional family responsibility leaves, it may be necessary to refer to other articles within the LUFA collective agreement or related documents.

question: What is stated about redundancy?
answer:
The context provided outlines several aspects related to redundancy at Laurentian University as defined in the collective agreement.

1. Redundancy does not apply to limited term appointments that carry no implication of renewal or continuation beyond the stated term (Article 5.20 and 11.10.3).

2. The Employer agrees to declare a state of redundancy by sending a written notice to the Union and the Vice-President (Article 11.10.2).

3. Members who are Academic Administrators, upon resignation/retirement/removal from that office, have the right to return to the bargaining unit (11.10.2d).

4. No member shall be displaced from the unit by the entry or re-entry of former senior Academic Administrators (11.10.2b).

5. For a period of five years from their appointment to an administrative position, members have first right of refusal for any academic vacancy within Laurentian for which they are academically competent (Article 11.10.4).

6. In case of redundancy resulting from the termination of a program and all transfer provisions being exhausted, the Employer may lay off a tenured member (Article 11.10.16).

7. The Vice-President, Academic and Provost acts as non-voting Chair in the Redundancy Committee proceedings (Article 11.10.7).

8. The Redundancy Committee shall make its final report to the Employer within sixty days of its first meeting, and no new academic or administrative appointments can be made nor reductions/redistributions of full-time members until the committee's final report is submitted or the time limit expires (Article 11.10.7).

These points define and outline the procedures related to redundancy at Laurentian University, as stated in their collective agreement.

question: What conditions apply to entitlement terms?
answer:
The conditions for entitlement terms can be found in multiple articles of the Laurentian University Faculty Association collective agreement.

1. For vacation, a Member who has completed nine (9) months or more of continuous service with the Employer by May 31 in any academic year is entitled to be absent from work during one (1) month or twenty-five (25) working days in each year following such May 31 (Article 5.15.1). Additionally, a Member who has completed sixty (60) months or more of continuous service with the Employer by May 31 is entitled to additional benefits (Article 5.15.2).

2. For term appointments, they are limited to a total of three (3) years, except in cases where the limited term appointment is a replacement for an academic administrator, where the appointment may be for a term up to five (5) years, by agreement of the Parties (Article 5.20.15).

3. A Member who is reappointed can also apply for a promotion retroactively to the date of their reappointment, as per Article 5.65 – Promotion Procedures.

4. Lastly, any full-time Member of the Bargaining Unit who currently occupies a regular full-time position and who has a minimum of two (2) years of continuous full-time service at the University can request a temporary reduction in workload up to 50%, under certain conditions outlined in Article 7.35.

Source documents: Laurentian University Faculty Association Collective Agreement, Articles 5.15, 5.20.15, 5.65, and 7.35.

question: How is professional development addressed in the collective agreement?
answer:
The Laurentian University Faculty Association (LUFA) Collective Agreement addresses professional development through several provisions.

1. Personal Development and Career Advancement: The parties agree that the University encourages staff to have opportunities for personal development and career advancement (Article 10.40.1).

2. Expenditures for Professional Development: Full-time counsellors are supported by $500 in expenditures in each contractual year (Article 10.40.2).

3. Sabbatical Leave: Members requesting a sabbatical leave must provide a dossier that includes an outline of proposed plans for scholarly, pedagogical or professional development (Article 12.05).

4. Professional Development Money for Sessional Members: Sessional members are eligible for professional development money of up to $2,000, with $250 per each three credit course taught (Article 30.07). This allowance can be used in the current and subsequent academic year (LUFA-H Collective Agreement 2016-2020).

The qualifications for Lecturers and Assistant Professors also imply continuous learning and professional development, as they require proficiency in their areas of specialisation and imparting that specialized knowledge to students (Article 5.b and c).

question: What does the collective agreement provide regarding physical and mental illness?
answer:
According to the 2016-2020 LUFA-H Collective Agreement (page 5), the employer recognizes its responsibility to provide an environment intended to protect the health, safety, and security of members as they carry out their duties. However, specific details regarding leave for physical or mental illness are not explicitly mentioned in the provided context.

Regarding leaves of absence without pay due to illness, the 2017-2020 Thorneloe-LUFA Collective Agreement (page 3) states that members on such leave are entitled to leave without remuneration and shall not be entitled to any rights or privileges under this Collective Agreement except in regards to benefits as governed by Article 7.40 – Leaves of Absence Without Pay.

For medical reports related to illness, the 2016-2020 LUFA-H Collective Agreement (page 10) specifies that the report shall not contain any diagnosis of the member’s condition unless the member, in consultation with the Union, requests that the diagnosis be included. The member is also required to provide the report to the Dean/University Librarian within five working days of receiving it, and the employer must provide a copy to the Union within five working days (Article 7.55.7).

Lastly, if the office of Health and Wellness Services is closed, the employee should contact Security in case of an emergency (Article 6.2 After Normal Working Hours, Critical Injury, page 8).

question: What does the collective agreement provide regarding discipline?
answer: The Laurentian University Faculty Association collective agreement (2017-2020) states that discipline shall be just and reasonable, based on the principle of progressive discipline, except in egregious cases (5.75.2). In cases where the Vice-President, Academic and Provost is involved, the member and their union representative shall be given five working days' notice of any meeting, during which the member will have an opportunity to respond to allegations (5.75.6). The parties are expected to attempt to resolve the matter in a manner acceptable to all concerned (citation for answers: Collective Agreement 2017-2020 pages 2, 8, and 39).

question: How is selection of chairs/directors addressed in the collective agreement?
answer:
According to the Laurentian University Faculty Association Collective Agreement (page numbers not provided as they are not explicitly stated in the context), the selection of Chairs/Directors is outlined as follows:

4. The selection process includes the formation of a Selection Committee, the submission of applications, interviews, candidate evaluation, balloting, and counting of ballots in the presence of the Selection Committee (pages not specified).

5. The Chair of the Selection Committee reports the results to the Dean/University Librarian who then forwards their recommendation, along with the Dean's own, to the Vice-President, Academic for the final appointment decision.

question: According to the agreement, what applies to sabbatical leave?
answer:
During a sabbatical leave, the following applies:
1. The Member continues to be eligible to receive all fringe benefits as a regular full-time Member (LUFA-H Collective Agreement 2016-2020, page 33).
2. Pension calculations are based on the Member's salary that would have been in effect if they had not been on sabbatical (LUFA-H Collective Agreement 2016-2020, page 33).
3. The Member is eligible to accumulate vacation entitlement proportional to the length of the leave (LUFA-H Collective Agreement 2016-2020, page 35).
4. The Member continues to be covered by the University's group benefit plans, and the Employer continues its normal contributions toward the premium costs for such plans (LUFA-H Collective Agreement 2016-2020, page 35).
5. Members granted sabbatical leave shall undertake to return to the University to resume their responsibilities as a full-time Member for at least one year. Failure to do so may be subject to certain conditions (LUFA-H Collective Agreement 2016-2020, page 35).
6. The compensation for sabbatical leaves coincides with the Collective Agreement in place, and any adjustments will be made according to any new agreement between the Board and the Association (LUFA-H Collective Agreement 2016-2020, page 33).
