answer:
Les règles concernant le mécanisme d'évaluation en vue d'une promotion (promotion désignée par l'article 5.65) sont les suivantes :

1. Pour les professeurs et les bibliothécaires, la période probatoire est de trois ans pour les rangs de chargé(e) d'enseignement, bibliothécaire général, professeur adjoint et bibliothécaire adjoint (article 5.20.22).
2. Les nominations à l'essai d'un an sont faites pour les postes de membre du Comité du corps professoral, de la faculté et du Comité des bibliothécaires et archivistes professionnels (article 5.55) et commencent par le 1er mars de chaque année. La période d'évaluation en vue de la permanence commence le 30 septembre de la même année pour ceux qui ont été nommés au poste.
3. Dans toutes les nominations initiales menant à la permanence, les membres sont informés dans leur lettre de nomination du Vice-recteur (article non spécifié).
4. L'évaluation en vue d'une promotion se fait selon le mécanisme défini par l'article 5.65 :
   a) Pour les professeurs, la promotion est possible de chargé(e) d'enseignement à professeur adjoint, de professeur adjoint à professeur agrégé et de professeur agrégé à professeur titulaire.
   b) Pour les bibliothécaires et les archivistes, la promotion est possible du rang de bibliothécaire/archiviste général au rang de bibliothécaire/archiviste adjoint.

question: Que prévoit la convention collective concernant conges sabbatioues?
answer:
La Convention collective de l'Association des professeurs de l'Université Laurentienne prévoit que le congé sabbatique est une période durant laquelle un membre est déchargé de ses fonctions habituelles pour :

answer:

* Die Universität als Gemeinschaft von Gelehrten benötigt die Verfügbarkeit ihrer Mitglieder auf einer regelmäßigen und dauerhaften Basis, um sicherzustellen, dass die Aktivitäten der Universität geplante und ungeplante in einem ordnungsgemäßen Weise durchgeführt werden können (7.20.1).
* Jede Abwesenheit sollte normalerweise nicht mit den zugewiesenen bzw. geplanten Aktivitäten und dem harmonischen Funktionieren des Departments/Schulverbands kollidieren (7.20.2).

question: Welche Bedingungen gelten für Gehaltsstufen bei Zusatzqualifikationen?
answer:
Laut Artikel 8.30 der Collective Agreement werden Gehaltserhöhungen für Zusatzqualifikationen wie folgt gewährt:

* Die Erhöhung wird auf Basis des Artikels 8.30 - Augmentation pour qualifications supplémentaires vergeben.
* Es ist kein bestimmtes Höchstgehalt angegeben.

Die genauen Bedingungen sind jedoch von den Einzelheiten in Artikel 8.10.2, 8.10.3 und 8.10.4 abhängig, insbesondere die Fälle, in denen eine Erhöhung aufgrund des Gehalts pro Jahr nicht gewährt wird.

Artikel 8.30 lautet wie folgt:

* Die Erhöhung für Zusatzqualifikationen wird basierend auf Artikel 8.30 - Augmentation pour qualifications supplémentaires vergeben.
* Es ist kein bestimmtes Höchstgehalt angegeben.

Es gibt jedoch Bedingungen, wenn das Gehalt pro Jahr ein bestimmtes Niveau erreicht:

* Wenn das Gehalt eines Mitglieds bei allen Rängen mehr als 150.859 $ pro Jahr beträgt, wird keine solche Erhöhung gewährt.
* Bei anderen Rängen gilt für Gehälter über 136.295 $ pro Jahr eine Reduktion der Erhöhung auf 50 % ihrer Wertigkeit.

Es ist jedoch wichtig zu beachten, dass diese Bedingungen spezifisch für die Jahre 2012-2014 gelten und möglicherweise nicht auf das aktuelle Jahr anwendbar sind.

question: Was gilt laut Vereinbarung für die berufliche Weiterbildung?
answer:
Laut der Vereinbarung gilt folgendes:

Sessionelle Mitglieder sind für Gelder zur beruflichen Weiterbildung von 250 Dollar pro jeder drei Kredit-Veranstaltung bis zu einer Obergrenze von 2.000 Dollar pro Jahr berechtigt (ARTICLE 30 - PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT, LUFA-H Collective Agreement 2016-2020, Seite 47).

 Vollzeit-Mitglieder sind hingegen für die berufliche Weiterbildung nur für jedes Vertragsjahr berechtigt und erhalten eine Zulage in Höhe von einer nicht bestimmten Summe (ARTICLE 30 - PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT, LUFA-H Collective Agreement 2016-2020, Seite 47).

 Es wird erwähnt, dass diese Zulage für Ausgaben im Zusammenhang mit genehmigten akademischen Forschungen oder beruflichen Zwecken verwendet werden soll und kumulativ über zwei akademische Jahre gilt (ARTICLE 30 - PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT, LUFA-H Collective Agreement 2016-2020, Seite 47).

Diplomierte Dozenten werden automatisch zu Assistenzprofessoren befördert. Die Beförderung tritt jedoch erst am ersten Tag des Monats in Kraft, nachdem die Universität einen Abschlusszeugnis oder eine Bestätigung von der Universität erhalten hat, an der der Doktortitel erworben wurde, dass alle Bedingungen für den Doktorgrad erfüllt sind (ARTICLE 16.05, LUFA-H Collective Agreement 2016-2020).

 Die relevanten Texte in deutscher Übersetzung laut Artikel 30:

Jedes Vollzeit-Mitglied hat Anspruch auf eine berufliche Zulage pro Vertragsjahr für Ausgaben im Zusammenhang mit genehmigten akademischen Forschungen oder beruflichen Zwecken. Diese Zulage gilt kumulativ über zwei (2) akademische Jahre.

 Die Übersetzung von Artikel 16.05:

Es wird davon ausgegangen, dass es keine explizite Erwähnung in der Vereinbarung gibt, die eine Beförderung wirksam macht, es sei denn, dies ist an anderer Stelle im Vertrag festgelegt. In jedem Fall gilt für Dozenten, die einen Doktortitel erworben haben, eine automatische Beförderung zum Assistenzprofessor. Die Beförderung tritt in Kraft mit dem ersten Tag des Monats, nachdem der Universität ein Abschlusszeugnis oder eine Bestätigung von der Universität vorliegt, an der der Doktortitel erworben wurde, dass alle Bedingungen für den Doktorgrad erfüllt sind.

question: Welche Regelungen gelten für den Rücktritt/die Kündigung?
answer:
Laut dem Collective Agreement (2002-2005, Seite 144) und dem APPENDIX D "Letter of Understanding" zwischen der Laurentian University Faculty Association und der Laurentian University of Sudbury (datiert vom 24. Juni 1999) gelten die folgenden Regelungen für den Rücktritt/Die Kündigung:

* Ein Mitglied, das in einem administrativen Amt tätig ist, hat für eine Periode von fünf Jahren Anspruch auf Erstberufung in jedem akademischen vakanten Posten innerhalb der Laurentian University, sofern es vom Vice-President, Academic and Provost als akademisch qualifiziert gilt (11.10.16).
* Bei einer Redundanz infolge der Beendigung eines Programms (Artikel 11.10.3 (a)) und nach Erschöpfung aller Überführungsregelungen kann der Arbeitgeber ein beamtetes Mitglied entlassen, vorausgesetzt, das Mitglied ist mindestens 45 Jahre alt, hat die Beamtenschaft und die Summe aus Anstellungszeitpunkt bis zur Beamtstellung plus Alter beträgt 55 (11.10.16).
* Die Kosten im Zusammenhang mit einer Schiedsverhandlung infolge einer Entlassung werden gemäß Artikel 11.15 - Schiedsverfahren verteilt.
* Gruppen oder Einzelpersonen, die für eine Redundanz ausgewählt wurden, haben das Recht, ihre Auswahl zu beanstanden (gemäß Artikel 12.10 - Beanstandungsverfahren) aufgrund von Voreingenommenheit, Verfahrensfehler, diskriminierender Anwendung der Auswahlkriterien oder in schlechtem Glauben.
* Beamtete Mitglieder, die das Angebot einer Überführung ablehnen, müssen dies innerhalb von 30 Tagen nach Erhalt des Angebots beanstanden. Wenn das Schiedsgericht entscheidet, dass der Widerspruch berechtigt ist, behalten die Mitglieder ihre ursprüngliche Position bei (11.10.17).
* Vollzeitmitglieder, deren Arbeitsverhältnis durch Insolvenzverfahren beendet wird (Gerichtsakte CV-21-656040-00CL), haben das Recht auf Wiedereinstellung in die Laurentian University und werden in den Bedingungen, Verfahren und Zeiträumen gemäß Artikel 11.10.18(b) berücksichtigt.

Hinweis: Die obigen Zitate sind wörtliche Übersetzungen der entsprechenden Abschnitte des Collective Agreement und des "Letter of Understanding".

question: Was gilt laut Vereinbarung für hufac?
answer:
Laut der Vereinbarung ist die Mitgliedschaft in HUFAC (Huntington University Faculty Affairs Committee) wie folgt geregelt:

Die Vorsitzende von HUFAC wird vom Präsidenten der Universität bestellt (14.02 a) und soll nicht Mitglied der Laurentian University Faculty Association sein.

Das Gremium besteht aus fünf (5) beaufsichtigten Huntington-Mitgliedern, wobei die Vorsitzende außer Acht gelassen wird (14.02 b)). Wenn es an Huntington-Mitgliedern mangelt, werden solche mit Zustimmung der Joint Labour Management Committee aus den beaufsichteten Mitgliedern der federierten Universitäten oder - wenn diese nicht verfügbar sind - von Laurentian Humanities and Social Sciences ausgewählt (14.02 b) i). Dabei darf kein non-Huntington-Mitglied aus dem gleichen akademischen Einrichtung stammen.

In bestimmten Fällen können spezifische Ausnahmen gewährt werden:

* Bei der Bewertung eines Bibliothekars kann ein Mitglied aus den beaufsichtigten Bibliothekaren von Laurentian University hinzugezogen werden (14.02 b) ii).
* Wenn ein Mitglied aus Gerontologie evaluiert wird, kann dieses Mitglied verlangen, dass einer der fünf Mitglieder ein beaufsichtigtes Mitglied aus dem Fachbereich Gesundheit ist (14.02 b iii). Dieses Verlangen darf nicht unvernünftig abgelehnt werden.
* Wenn ein Mitglied aus Communication Studies oder Religious Studies evaluiert wird, kann dieses Mitglied verlangen, dass einer der fünf Mitglieder ein beaufsichtigtes Mitglied aus dem Fachbereich Arts ist (14.02 b iv). Dieses Verlangen darf nicht unvernünftig abgelehnt werden.

Die Empfehlung des Gremiums wird sowohl an den Präsidenten als auch an den Antragsteller weitergeleitet (14.08). In der Empfehlung ist anzugeben, dass der Mitglied schriftliche Vorstellungen an den Präsidenten innerhalb von zehn Arbeitstagen nach dem Datum, an dem HUFAC die Empfehlung an den Präsidenten weitergeleitet hat, machen kann.

question: Wie definiert oder beschreibt die Vereinbarung Abwesenheit im Allgemeinen?
answer:
Die Vereinbarung definisiert Abwesenheit im Allgemeinen in Artikel 7.20 als folgt:

"ARTICLE 7.20 – ABSENCE - GENERAL (deutsch: ARTIKEL 7.20 – ABSENCES - GÉNÉRALITÉS)
7.20.1 L'Université, en tant que communauté de savants, doit compter sur la disponibilité de ses Membres sur une base régulière et continue pour que toutes les activités universitaires, qu'elles soient prévues au calendrier ou non, puissent se poursuivre de façon bien ordonnée. (deutsch: Die Universität als Gemeinschaft der Gelehrten muss sich auf die Verfügbarkeit ihrer Mitglieder auf einer regelmäßigen und kontinuierlichen Basis verlassen, damit alle universitären Aktivitäten, sei es im Lehrplan oder nicht, in einem ordnungsgemäßen Rahmen durchgeführt werden können.)

7.20.2 Les absences ne doivent normalement porter atteinte ni aux fonctions attribuées ni aux activités prévues dans l'horaire ni au fonctionnement harmonieux du Département/de l’École. (deutsch: Abwesenheiten dürfen normalerweise weder die zugewiesenen Aufgaben noch die im Stundenplan vorgesehenen Aktivitäten noch das harmonische Funktionieren des Departments/Schule beeinträchtigen.)

7.20.3 Any absence from campus affecting teaching/professional librarian duties shall be subject to the approval of the Department Chair. (deutsch: Jede Abwesenheit vom Campus, die sich auf Lehr- bzw. Bibliotheksdiensttätigkeiten auswirkt, bedarf der Zustimmung des Departementsleiters.)"

question: Was wird über den Urlaub gesagt?
answer:
Entschuldigung, ich habe mich geirrt. Da der Kontext in Englisch ist und Sie auf die Antwort in Deutsch bestehen, werde ich dies tun. Allerdings müssen wir uns auf das Thema "LEAVES" beschränken.

Gemäß Artikel 7.10 - RECOGNIZED AND OTHER HOLIDAYS im Kollektivvertrag steht folgendes:

Die anerkannten Feiertage und die Tage, an denen Bundes- oder Provinzbehörden allgemein Feiertage erklärt haben, sind als Feiertage anerkannt. Die Mitglieder erhalten daher bezahlten Urlaub auf:

(a) Family Day, Good Friday, Ostersonntag, Victoria Day, Canada Day, August-Civic-Holiday, Labour Day, Thanksgiving Day, Weihnachtenstag, Boxing Day und Neujahr.

(b) Und auf andere Feiertage, die der Arbeitgeber erklärt, einschließlich des cu (es wird jedoch nicht klar, was "cu" bedeutet).

Es ist wichtig zu beachten, dass Artikel 7.10 nur die anerkannten Feiertage auflistet und nicht explizit darüber spricht, wie mit dem Urlaub umgegangen wird.

Zusätzlich gibt es Artikel 17.04 im Kollektivvertrag, der besagt: "Les membres continuent de recevoir leur traitement habituel pendant les périodes de vacances, mais aucune rémunération ne remplace les vacances au cas où un membre choisit de ne pas prendre les vacances auxquelles il a droit." (Die Mitglieder erhalten ihren normalen Gehalt während der Urlaubszeit, aber keine Entschädigung ersetzt die Urlaubstage, wenn ein Mitglied nicht die an sich stehenden Urlaubstage nimmt.)

Daher lautet meine Antwort:

Gemäß dem Kollektivvertrag (kein spezifisches Dokument und Seitenzahl angegeben) erhalten Mitglieder bezahlten Urlaub auf bestimmten Feiertagen. Es gibt jedoch keine explizite Regelung darüber, wie mit dem Urlaub umgegangen wird.

Ich hoffe, dies hilft!

question: Was sieht der Tarifvertrag bezüglich des akademischen Arbeitspensums vor?
answer:
Der Tarifvertrag regelt das akademische Arbeitspensum in Artikel 5.40. Danach soll das akademische Arbeitspensum in einer fairen und gerechten Weise zugewiesen werden (§ 5.40.1).

Das Arbeitspensum eines Vollzeitmitglieds umfasst:

* Lehre/Professionelle Bibliothekarität/Archivleitung, einschließlich der Überwachung von Master- und Bachelor-Studierenden (a)
* Wissenschaftliche Aktivitäten, einschließlich Verpflichtungen gegenüber externen Förderstellen (b)
* Universitätsverwaltung, administrative Aufgaben und andere Beiträge an die Universität (c)

Die normalmäßige Verteilung des Arbeitspensums unter den drei Hauptkomponenten lautet: 40% Lehre/Professionelle Bibliothekarität/Archivleitung, einschließlich der Überwachung von Master- und Bachelor-Studierenden; 40% wissenschaftliche Aktivitäten, einschließlich Verpflichtungen gegenüber externen Förderstellen; und 20% Universitätsverwaltung, administrative Aufgaben und andere Beiträge an die Universität (§ 5.40.2).

Die Zuweisung des Arbeitspensums soll bis spätestens April 1 schriftlich mitgeteilt werden. Der Dekan/Direktor der Fakultät/School hat das Recht, die schriftliche Beratung des Departments/School zu verlangen (§ 5.40.3).

question: Was wird über die Vergütungssätze für befristete Lehrbeauftragte gesagt?
answer:
Nach Artikel 4.55.2 der Kollektivvertragsvereinbarung (S.20) können befristete Lehrbeauftragte das Angebot annehmen, einen Kurs unter dem Überlastzuschuss zu lehren, vorausgesetzt, dass die Zahlung gleichmäßig verteilt wird und basiert auf der Anzahl der am Kursbeginn eingeschriebenen Studenten.

Nach Artikel 4.55.3 der Kollektivvertragsvereinbarung (S.20) erhalten befristete Lehrbeauftragte, die für ein bestimmtes Kursangebot an der Universität etabliert sind (gemäß Artikel 4.15), das gleiche Gehalt für jedes weitere Kursangebot, das sie lehren. Es wird jedoch betont, dass diese Zahlung nicht automatisch zu einer etablierten Beauftragung für dieses bestimmte Kursangebot führt.

Nach der Tabelle in Abschnitt 16.05 der Kollektivvertragsvereinbarung (S.20) wird das Gehalt für befristete Lehrbeauftragte wie folgt berechnet:

* Für Sessional Lecturers ohne Seniorität oder Etablierung: $6941 + 4% in Lieu von Urlaub + 4% in Lieu von Vorteilen = $7497
* Für Sessional Lecturers mit Seniorität, Etablierung und Pensionisten: $7288 + 6% in Lieu von Urlaub + 4% in Lieu von Vorteilen = $8017

Es wird jedoch festgestellt, dass befristete Lehrbeauftragte auch Anspruch auf die Zuweisung von Studienhilfskräften und/oder Korrektoren zu einem Niveau haben, das mit der Zuweisung solcher Unterstützung an vollzeitige Mitglieder vereinbar ist.

In Abschnitt 4.55.4 wird besagt, dass für Sessional Lecturers, die "lehrenswerte" Kurse in der Schule für Bildung oder "didaktische" Kurse in der École des sciences de l'éducation unterrichten, eine Vergütung von bis zu $693 pro Unterrichtsstunde gewährt wird.

question: Was wird über Ernennung und Verlängerung gesagt?
answer:
Nach dem Artikel 11.02 Rangs de nomination (Ränge der Ernennung) sagt es sich, dass alle Ersternennungen von Vollzeitprofessoren zu einem der folgenden Ränge erfolgen:

1. Professor titulaire (ständige Professur)
2. Professor agrégé (Associate-Professur)
3. Professor adjoint (Assistant-Professur)
4. Chargé de cours (Lektor)

Ferner wird in Artikel 11.03 Catégories de nomination (Ernennungskategorien) erwähnt, dass alle Ersternennungen von Vollzeitprofessoren zu einer der folgenden Kategorien erfolgen:

1. Permanence (ständige Anstellung)
2. Nomination à l'essai (Prüfungsstelle mit Aussicht auf ständige Anstellung)
3. Nomination à durée limitée (Befristete Stelle)

Außerdem ist in Artikel 16.05 zu lesen, dass Beförderungen, es sei denn sie werden an anderer Stelle im Vertrag ausdrücklich anders geregelt, am 1. Juli des folgenden akademischen Jahres wirksam sind, in dem das Antragsjahr endete und genehmigt wurde.

question: Wie definiert oder beschreibt die Vereinbarung die Auswahl von Vorsitzenden/Direktoren?
answer:
Gemäß Artikel 9.15 der Konvention Collective 2017-2020 werden die Direktoren/Dekane (Directeurs) wie folgt ausgewählt:

* Der Direktor/Dean wird vom Vice-Rector aux études und Provost ernannt, vgl. Artikel 9.15.1.
* Die Auswahlverfahren beginnen mindestens sechs Monate vor dem Ende eines Mandats oder unmittelbar, wenn ein Posten frei wird, vgl. Artikel 9.15.2.
* Ein Comité der Auswahl mit folgender Zusammensetzung wird eingesetzt:
 + Ein Drittel (1/3) der Vollzeit-Mitglieder des Departements/Schule (auf die nächste ganze Zahl gerundet), vgl. Artikel 9.15.3(a)(i).
 + Der Dekan/Bibliotheksdirektor als Mitglied ohne Stimmrecht, vgl. Artikel 9.15.3(a)(ii).
 + Ein Direktor eines anderen Departements/Schule, ernannt durch den Dekan/Bibliotheksdirektor in Absprache mit dem Departement/Schule, das einen neuen Direktor benötigt, vgl. Artikel 9.15.3(a)(iii).
 + Mindestens eine Frau muss dem Comité angehören, vgl. Artikel 9.15.3(a)(iv).
* Das Comité wählt einen Präsidenten unter seinen Mitgliedern, vgl. Artikel 9.15.3(b).

Der Präsident des Auswahlcomités macht alle Anstrengungen, um alle Vollzeit-Mitglieder des Departements/Schule (einschließlich derer, die beurlaubt sind) einzuladen, in einer bestimmten Frist und im Vertrauen, die Namen möglicher Kandidaten sowie die Gründe für ihre Kandidatur zu übermitteln.

question: What does the collective agreement provide regarding pregnancy, parental and adoption?
answer:
The collective agreement provides for three types of leaves:

1. **Pregnancy Leave**: Article 7.60 - Pregnancy, Parental and Adoption Leaves
	* A pregnant full-time Member or pregnant Master Lecturer Member is entitled to 17 weeks of pregnancy leave (Article 7.60.1(a), Collective Agreement 2017-2020).
	* During the period of pregnancy leave, the Member shall receive from the Employer:
		+ For the first week, 100% of her nominal salary (Article 7.60(b)(i), Collective Agreement 2017-2020).
		+ For up to a maximum of 16 additional weeks, a benefit (Article 7.60(b)(ii), Collective Agreement 2017-2020).
2. **Parental Leave**: Article 14.06 Congé d'adoption
	* A Member who is the parent and has chosen to take parental leave under the Employment Insurance Act and any other applicable law will have a maximum of 35 weeks of parental leave (Article 14.06, Collective Agreement).
	* During the period of parental leave, the Member shall receive from the Employer 100% of their nominal salary for 5 days after they have worked a minimum of 12 consecutive months.
3. **Adoption Leave**: Article 14.06 Congé d'adoption
	* A Member who is the parent and has chosen to take parental leave under the Employment Insurance Act and any other applicable law will have a maximum of 35 weeks of parental leave (Article 7.60.1, Collective Agreement).
	* The provision for adoption leave appears to be similar to that for parental leave.

Note: The collective agreement also provides for leaves related to a newborn child being hospitalized and the postponement or interruption of pregnancy leave in such cases.

question: What is stated about vacation?
answer:
According to Article 7.15 of the collective agreement, here are the key points stated about vacation:

1. **Definition**: Vacation is the period during which a Member is not accountable to the University (Article 7.15.1).
2. **Eligibility and duration**: Each Member is entitled to a vacation of twenty-five (25) working days after eleven (11) months of service, annually thereafter (Article 7.15.2). Members on contracts of less than one year's duration are entitled to a pro-rated period of vacation.
3. **Accrual**: Vacation may not be accumulated from year to year (Article 7.15.4).
4. **Payment during vacation**: The Members will be paid during vacation periods, but there shall be no remuneration in lieu of vacation if they choose not to take their vacation allowance (Article 7.15.3 and 17.04).
5. **Required time off**: Members are required to take the vacation to which they are entitled between Spring Convocation and Labour Day, unless prior permission has been granted by the Dean/University Librarian (Article 7.15.4).
6. **Notification**: Members must indicate their vacation dates to the Dean/University Librarian through their Chair/Director at least one month in advance (Article 7.15.4).
7. **Payment upon termination**: In the event of retirement, resignation, or expiration of a limited-term appointment, the value of any unused vacation entitlement will be paid to the Member's beneficiary (Article 7.15.5 and 7.15.6).

According to Article 10 — Academic Activity of the Collective Agreement 2015-2018 (page 11), "The domains of activity identified in this article carry different sorts of implications for the workload of members and may vary according to a member’s discipline, from member to member and from year to year for each member."

This suggests that the collective agreement recognizes that academic workload can vary significantly depending on individual circumstances, disciplines, and years.

question: How does the agreement define or describe selection of chairs/directors?
answer:
According to Article 9.15 - Selection of Chairs/Directors, the selection process for chairs/directors is as follows:

* The ballots shall be opened and counted in the presence of the Selection Committee (Clause 9.15.1).
* The Chair of the Selection Committee shall report the results of the selection process and its recommendation to the Dean/University Librarian (Clause 9.15.9).
* If the Dean/University Librarian is prepared to accept the Selection Committee's recommendation, they will forward this recommendation together with their own to the Vice-President, Academic who will make the appointment (Clause 9.15.10).
* If the Dean/University Librarian and the Selection Committee are unable to agree on an appointment, the selection procedure shall be reinstituted (Clause 9.15.11).

Additionally, Article 9.20 - Term of Office of Chairs/Directors outlines the term of office for chairs/directors, which is normally three years renewable by Department/School selection.

It's also worth noting that there are provisions for abbreviated selection process in clause 9.15.14, and for acting chairs/directors in clauses 9.15.13 and 9.20.2.

question: What are the rules concerning moving expenses?
answer:
According to Article 6.50 of the 2014-2017 Thorneloe-LUFA Collective Agreement, page 66, moving expenses include:

* Moving, packing, crating and unpacking of household goods and personal effects (6.50.1.a)
* Transfer of family by the most economical means of transportation (6.50.1.b)
* Reasonable living expenses for the duration of the trip to the new location (6.50.1.c)
* One (1) advance visit for the purpose of securing suitable housing (6.50.1.d)

No additional rules or restrictions are mentioned regarding moving expenses in this article, other than those explicitly listed above.

question: What conditions apply to academic freedom?
answer:
According to Article 2.01, the proper academic tradition of reasonable discussion must be maintained.

Additionally, according to Section 0.02 (d), members must exercise their academic freedom in a manner consistent with their scholarly obligations as professors, including:

* Basing research and teaching on an honest and responsible search for knowledge
* Upholding the norms of civil discourse, especially with regard to criticism
* Ensuring that criticism is respectful, constructive, ad rem, reasonable, balanced, and fair in the use of evidence. (Source: LUFA-H Collective Agreement 2016-2020, page 4)

question: How does the agreement define or describe discipline?
answer:
According to Article 5.75 of the collective agreement, discipline is defined as "just and reasonable" (source document name: Collective Agreement, page number: not specified) and based on the principle of progressive discipline, except in egregious cases.

Additionally, according to Clause 5.75.2 of the collective agreement, just cause for discipline includes:

* Gross misconduct including serious unprofessional behaviour and/or misconduct constituting a grave and direct violation of the personal safety of another Member; Members of the University community and/or students of the University community (source document name: Collective Agreement, page number: not specified)
* Persistent failure to discharge academic responsibility as defined in this Collective Agreement (source document name: Collective Agreement, page number: not specified)

question: How is political leaves addressed in the collective agreement?
answer:
According to Article 7.50 - POLITICAL LEAVES (page numbers vary depending on source document), political leaves are addressed as follows:

* The Employer recognizes that all Members of the Bargaining Unit are free to enter public life and to seek any political office, as a Member of the provincial or federal government, or any full-time political office. (7.50.1)
* If Members of the Bargaining Unit wish to allow their names to stand either before a party convention or for actual nomination for an election, the Members shall notify the Dean/University Librarian concerned within a reasonable time so that the Dean/University Librarian may make whatever arrangements may be deemed necessary in order to ensure that the resulting added workload can be properly performed by others from the date of the issuance of the writ up to and including the date of the election. (7.50.2)
* The Employer may grant such a Member leave without pay for a period from the issuance of the writ up to and including election day. (7.50.3)

Similarly, in Article 5.40 - POLITICAL LEAVES (page numbers vary depending on source document), it is stated:

* The Employer recognizes that all Members are free to enter public life and to seek any political office, as a Member of the provincial or federal government, or any full-time political office. (5.40.1)
* If Members wish to allow their names to stand either before a party convention or for actual nomination for an election, the Members shall notify the President within a reasonable time so that the President may make whatever arrangements may be deemed necessary in order to ensure that the resulting added workload can be properly performed by others from the date of the issuance of the writ up to and including the date of the election. (5.40.2)
* The Employer may grant such a Member leave without pay for a period from the issuance of the writ up to and including election day. (5.40.3)

In Article 3.34 - POLITICAL LEAVES (page numbers vary depending on source document), it is stated:

* The Board recognises that all Members of the bargaining unit are free to enter public life and to seek any political office, as a member of the provincial or federal government, or any full-time political office. (3.34.1)
* If Members of the bargaining unit wish to allow their names to stand either before a party convention or for actual nomination for an election, the Members shall notify the Dean/Director of the Library concerned within a reasonable time so that the Dean/Director of the Library may make whatever arrangements may be deemed necessary in order to ensure that the resulting added workload can be properly performed by others from the date of the issuance of the writ up to and including the date of the election. (3.34.2)
* The Board may grant such a Member leave without pay for a period from the issuance of the writ up to and including election day. Such leave shall not be unreasonably withheld. (3.34.3)

Finally, in Article 14.02 - Public Service Leave (page 35 of 59), it is stated:

* Members who are candidates for election are entitled to paid leave for the duration of the writ, or in the cases of regional, municipal, or school board elections, from Nomination Day until the end of the election.

question: According to the agreement, what applies to voluntary reduced workload?
answer:

* The request is made by the Member.
* Time spent on study leave does not count towards sabbatical credit (Note: This is actually from Article 7.30.6 Appointments while on Leave, page 77, but related to study leave).

question: What does the agreement say about laurentian university research fund (lurf)?
answer:
According to the collective agreement:

* The Employer shall provide a research fund to enhance scholarly productivity through an open competition among Members, known as Research Support (LURF), in the amount of $160,000 per year for each of the years of the Collective Agreement. (Source: Article 6.25.1, page 106-107 of 243)
* In the event that faculty from federated or affiliated universities wish to apply, their applications shall only be considered if their home institution has contributed to the LURF fund an amount per full-time Member equivalent to that provided by the Employer. (Source: Article 6.25.1, page 106-107 of 243)
* The Employer will also provide an additional $20,000 per year to support both research activities and attendance at academic and professional conferences by retired Members, Sessional Members and Master Lecturers, through an open competition. (Source: Article 6.25.2, page 106-107 of 243)
* A LURF Committee of eight (8) full-time Members will evaluate the proposals submitted to the Office of Research Services once a year. The composition of the committee is specified in article 6.25.3, with variations across different collective agreements.
* The LURF Committee shall establish its own procedures and develop criteria for the administration of the funds, which must be just, equitable and consistent with the objective of nurturing and stimulating research at Laurentian University. (Source: Article 6.25.4, page 108-109 of 243)
* The total LURF funding shall be allocated by Faculty/Library, proportionate to the numbers of full-time Members in each Faculty/Library.
* The amount of funding per application cannot exceed $5,000.

question: What conditions apply to personnel files?
answer:
According to the collective agreement, there are several conditions that apply to personnel files:

1. Accuracy: The documents comprising the file must be accurate paper copies (Article 18.01).
2. Ownership: Official personnel files of a member shall be kept by the Office of the President and are the property of the Employer (Article 21.01).
3. Examination: Members have the right to examine all of their personnel files, upon making prior arrangements to do so (Article 21.02).
4. Confidential material: Material in the files which is to be held confidential according to the provisions of this Agreement will be removed from the files prior to their inspection by the member, and an inventory of this confidential material will be provided to the member (Article 21.02).

Source:
Collective Agreement 2015-2018, Articles 18.01 and 21.01-02.

question: What conditions apply to professional development expenditures?
answer:
According to Article 6.45 of the Collective Agreement 2011-14 (page 115), the following conditions apply to professional development expenditures:

* Expenditures must be approved in advance by the Dean/University Librarian (Article 6.45.3).
* Reimbursements will be made on verification of receipts (Article 6.45.3).
* In the event that expenditures are incurred in relatively small amounts, reimbursements should be accumulated but receipts must be submitted not later than January 1 or July 1 following the date the expenditures have been made (Article 6.45.3).
* Any equipment purchased with funds provided under this Article remains the property of the University, but a Member shall have the right to buy back such equipment at fair market value (Article 6.45.5).
* Any unused portion of the maximum allowed for professional development can be carried forward for two years only (Article 6.45.6).

Additionally, according to Article 30.05, full-time academic staff who are on sabbatical leave or study leave or voluntary reduced workload are eligible for professional development expenditures on a prorated basis.

It's also worth noting that the Collective Agreement 2017-2020 (Article 4.70 and 4.85) has slightly different provisions for Sessional Members, including Clinical Instructors and Educators.

question: What conditions apply to redundancy?
answer:
According to Article 11.10.3 and Article 11.10.4 of the Collective Agreement:

A declaration of redundancy by the Employer may be initiated in one of two ways:
(a) Senate may resolve to terminate a Faculty, Department/School or program for reasons other than Financial Exigency.
(b) The Vice-President, Academic and Provost may make a submission to the Employer that a particular Department(s)/School(s) has (have) a larger number of Members than necessary to fulfil its (their) program and service teaching requirements in the light of student demand.

Redundancies may be justified only for bona fide academic reasons and/or on the grounds of insufficient student demand. When insufficient student demand is used as a justification, such lack of demand must be demonstrable over a period of at least three (3) years and projections into the future must not indicate any appreciable increase in this student demand.

Source document: Collective Agreement between Laurentian University Faculty Association and Laurentian University (2017-2020), pages 111-115.

question: How is patents addressed in the collective agreement?
answer:
According to Article 6.40.3 of the Collective Agreement, any grievance by a Member pertaining to Article 6.30 – Patents and/or Article 6.35 – Copyright shall be handled in accordance with the following procedure:

* The Member presents a grievance to the Vice-President, Academic and Provost within three (3) weeks of the event giving rise to the grievance (Source: Collective Agreement 2017-2020, page 1)
* The Vice-President, Academic and Provost refers the matter to the continuing Committee on Patents and Copyright and informs the Union within two (2) weeks of receipt of the grievance. If they fail to do so, the Members shall be deemed to have succeeded in their grievance and the results thereof shall be binding on the university (Source: Collective Agreement 2017-2020, page 1)
* The continuing Committee on Patents and Copyright makes a recommendation for the resolution of the grievance within one (1) month of receipt. If they fail to do so, the Vice-President, Academic and Provost may act as in Article 6.40.3 (d) below (Source: Collective Agreement 2017-2020, page 1)
* The Vice-President, Academic and Provost renders the Committee's proposal in writing within one (1) week of receipt of the recommendations or within one (1) week of the end of the time limits for action by the Committee (Source: Collective Agreement 2017-2020, page 1)

If the proposal does not resolve the grievance, the matter may be submitted to binding arbitration by one (1) arbitrator in accordance with the grievance and arbitration procedures of this Collective Agreement (Source: Collective Agreement 2017-2020, page 1).

question: What does the agreement say about arbitration procedure?
answer:
According to Schedule "S" - Expedited Mediation and Arbitration Processes (page not specified), the parties agree on the following terms for mediation and arbitration:

1. The parties may be represented by legal counsel for the expedited med-arbitration dates.
2. The parties will agree to up to four (4) dates for expedited med-arbitration for each year of the term of the Collective Agreement.
3. At least sixty (60) days prior to each expedited med-arbitration date, the parties will agree on the grievances to be dealt with on that day.
4. The parties will schedule up to three (3) grievances to be heard on each expedited med-arbitration date.

In terms of arbitration procedure, Article 11.15 - Arbitration Procedure states:

(a) Failing settlement and/or timely response under the foregoing grievance procedure, any grievance may then be submitted to arbitration as hereinafter provided under its own distinct arbitral procedure.
(b) When either Party requests that any matter be submitted to Arbitration as provided in this Article, it shall make such request in writing addressed to the other Party of this Collective Agreement, and at the same time appoint a nominee. Within fifteen (15) working days thereafter, the other Party shall appoint its nominee.

Additionally, Article 36 - Arbitrator states:

question: What are the rules concerning sabbatical leaves?
answer:
According to Article 22.07 of the Collective Agreement, here are the rules concerning sabbatical leaves:

* A sabbatical leave is for a period of 12 months, commencing on July 1, or for 6 months commencing on July 1 or January 1 [Source: Collective Agreement, page not specified (assuming it's Article 22.07)].
* No portion of the academic year in which a sabbatical leave is taken shall count toward the years of eligibility entitlement [Source: Collective Agreement, page not specified (assuming it's Article 22.07)].
* A sabbatical leave includes the appropriate vacation entitlement proportional to the length of the leave [Source: Collective Agreement, page not specified (assuming it's Article 22.07)].

Additionally, according to other articles in the Collective Agreement:

* When a Member takes a sabbatical leave after three years, all accumulated years of eligibility are exhausted except as otherwise provided for by this Collective Agreement [Source: Collective Agreement, page not specified (assuming it's Article 5.20)].
* Members with tenure can be granted a sabbatical after three years, but only if they have met the eligibility criteria [Source: Collective Agreement, page not specified (assuming it's Article 5.20)].

Finally, according to Article 12.20:

* Immediately following the completion of a sabbatical leave, the member is required to return to the University for a period equal to the length of the leave taken, or to satisfy some other arrangement that is mutually acceptable to the member and the Employer [Source: Collective Agreement, page not specified (assuming it's Article 12.20)].

question: What is stated about sabbatical leave?
answer:
Here are some key points about sabbatical leave as per the provided collective agreements:

1. **Compensation for Sabbatical Leaves** (Article 22.09, page 33 of LUFA-H Collective Agreement 2016-2020): Compensation for sabbatical leaves coincides with the Collective Agreement in place. Salary, benefits, and other provisions will be adjusted according to any new agreement between the Board and the Association.
2. **Eligibility** (Article 7.25.2, page [not specified] of Collective Agreement 2017-2020): Members must have been full-time faculty members of the University for the past six consecutive years, holding a tenure-track position at the time of application. They must be tenured at the start of their sabbatical leave.
3. **Purpose and Use** (Article [not specified] of Collective Agreement 2017-2020): Sabbaticals can be used for upgrading, but the University will give special consideration to employment equity goals in such cases.
4. **Scheduling** (Article 7.25.2, page [not specified] of Collective Agreement 2017-2020): Sabbatical leave is not automatic and must be granted following an approved application procedure. The Vice-President, Academic and Provost may grant credit towards a sabbatical leave for full-time faculty service at another University.
5. **Leave Conditions** (Article 7.25.10, page [not specified] of Collective Agreement 2017-2020): If a Member becomes unable to fulfill their sabbatical obligations due to disability, they must advise the Dean/University Librarian and provide a physician's report outlining the extent of the disability.
6. **Disability Leave** (Article 7.25.10, page [not specified] of Collective Agreement 2017-2020): If a Member is disabled from performing their tasks for less than 50% of the sabbatical leave, they are deemed to have taken their sabbatical leave. If they are disabled for more than 50% of the leave, they are not deemed to have taken a sabbatical leave.
7. **Study Leave** (Article [not specified] of Collective Agreement 2016-2020 and Article 7.25.9, page [not specified] of Collective Agreement 2017-2020): Members can be granted up to one year of study leave immediately following their sabbatical leave if they were studying for a Doctorate during the sabbatical.
8. **Sabbaticant Activities** (Article 7.25.10, page [not specified] of Collective Agreement 2017-2020): Members must submit a report on their sabbatical activities on completion of the sabbatical leave or at the end of the sick leave, whichever occurs later.
9. **Office Space and Workload** (Article 7.25.1, page [not specified] of Collective Agreement 2017-2020): Members on sabbatical leave are not normally assigned formal workload or participate in formal activities, except as required by the collective agreement. They may be entitled to suitable office space on campus.
10. **Reimbursement** (Article 7.25.9, page [not specified] of Collective Agreement 2017-2020): Members who do not fulfill their sabbatical obligations due to disability or other reasons may be required to reimburse the University for stipend and benefits received during the leave.

Please note that these points are based on the provided collective agreements and might not be an exhaustive list.

question: How is employer's retirement addressed in the collective agreement?
answer:
According to Article 1.20 (page not specified) and Articles 16-19 of Collective Agreement 2011-14 (pages 212-213), employer's retirement, specifically Special Voluntary Early Retirement, is addressed as follows:

* Members who go on Special Voluntary Early Retirement will retain participation in certain benefit plans, including Group Life Insurance, Dependant Group Life, Accidental Death and Dismemberment, Hospital Care, Extended Medical (including ManuAssist), the dental plan, and the Retirees Health Benefit Plan.
* The Employer's cost of those benefit plans in which the Member does not retain participation will be added to the early retirement incentive.
* Members who go on Special Voluntary Early Retirement will not be eligible for sick leave.
* If a Member dies during the Special Voluntary Early Retirement Period, the payment will cease at the end of the month the death occurred. Benefits and Pension contributions will also terminate as of the end of the month of the Member's death.
* Members taking Special Voluntary Early Retirement would enjoy all retiree privileges as well as tuition fee waiver.

question: According to the agreement, what applies to selection of chairs/directors?
answer:
According to Article 9.15 and 9.20 of the collective agreement:

* The term of office for Chairs/Directors is normally three (3) years, renewable by Department/School selection per Article 9.15 – Selection of Chairs/Directors (Article 9.20.1).
* If a Chair/Director is unable to carry out their duties for six (6) months or less, they shall make provision for the take-over of their duties in consultation with the Department/School and Dean/University Librarian (Article 9.20.2).
* If the absence is for a period of longer than four (4) months, the Chairs/Directors shall relinquish her/his title and a new Chair/Director shall be selected according to the procedures set out in Article 9.15 – Selection of Chairs/Directors.

The selection process involves:

* The ballots shall be opened and counted in the presence of the Selection Committee (Article 9.15.8).
* The Chair of the Selection Committee shall report the results of the selection process and its recommendation to the Dean/University Librarian (Article 9.15.9).
* If the Dean/University Librarian is prepared to accept the Selection Committee's recommendation, they will forward this recommendation together with their own to the Vice-President, Academic who will make the appointment (Article 9.15.10).
* In exceptional circumstances, the Vice-President, Academic and Provost and the Dean/University Librarian may appoint an acting Chair/Director for a period of up to four (4) months (Article 9.15.13).

The agreement also mentions an Abbreviated Selection Process, where if there is a strong consensus for one candidate, the Selection Committee may proceed directly to step 8 of the procedure (Article 9.15.14).

question: What is stated about loan reimbursement?
answer:
According to Article 31 — MOVING EXPENSES and A.09 MOVING EXPENSES in the Collective Agreement 2015-2018 (page 56, 57), if a Member leaves the University before completing three years of continuous service, they must reimburse the University for the remaining unretired portion of the loan.

Specifically:

* Article 31: "Should the beneficiary of such a loan leave the University before completing three (3) years of continuous service for personal or disciplinary reasons, they must reimburse the University for a pro-rated portion of the loan." (page 56)
* A.09 MOVING EXPENSES: "Moving expenses paid to a new member will constitute a loan made by the Employer. This loan will be retired when the member has completed three years of continuous service to the University, each year being equivalent to one-third of the reimbursement of the loan. Should the member leave the University before completing three years of continuous service, the member must reimburse the Employer for the remaining unretired portion of the loan." (page 57)

answer:
According to the collective agreement, a sabbatical leave is described in Article 12. The relevant sections are:

* 12.12: A sabbatical leave includes the accumulation of vacation entitlement proportional to the length of the leave (Source: LUFA-H Collective Agreement 2016-2020, page 23)

These sections indicate that a sabbatical leave is defined as including accumulated vacation entitlements based on the length of the leave, and that benefits coverage continues during the leave.

question: What is stated about academic workload?
answer:
According to Article 5.40 of the collective agreement, the academic workload shall be assigned in a fair and equitable manner (Source document name: Collective Agreement, page number: not specified). 

Specifically, it states that each Member of a Department/School shall receive a copy of the Chair's/Director’s recommendations on their own workload and a summary of the recommendations on all other Members in the Department/School prior to the Dean/University Librarian making a decision (Source document name: Collective Agreement, page number: 40).

The normal guideline for the distribution of workload among three main components is: 40% teaching/professional librarianship/archives management, including supervision; 40% scholarly activity, including commitments to external granting agencies; and 20% University governance, administrative duties, and other contributions to the University (Source document name: Collective Agreement, page number: not specified).

The academic workload of a full-time Member during the academic year includes teaching/professional librarianship/archives management, including supervision of graduate and undergraduate students; scholarly activity, including commitments to external granting agencies; and University governance, administrative duties, and other contributions to the University (Source document name: Collective Agreement, page number: not specified).

The only formal "Disciplinary Measures" that may be taken by the Employer against a Member are:

* A letter of reprimand, specifying the grounds and adding this reprimand to the personnel file (5.75.3(a))
 
Additionally, there is also another section mentioning:
When an alleged breach of discipline is made against a member, the parties shall attempt to resolve the matter through a discussion between the Dean/University Librarian, the member, and their union representative (Source: Collective Agreement, page not specified).

According to Article 8.55 - MOVING EXPENSES in the Collective Agreement 2011-14 (page 163 of 243), moving expenses are defined as follows:

c) Reasonable living expenses for the duration of the trip to the new location.
d) One (1) advance visit for the purpose of securing suitable housing. The newly appointed Members may be accompanied by their spouse in this instance."

Additionally, Article 32.02 - Moving Expenses Include in the LUFA-H Collective Agreement 2012-2016 (page 45) also defines moving expenses as:

"Moving Expenses Include:
a) moving, packing, crating, and unpacking of household goods and personal effects;
b) transfer of family by the most economical means of transportation;
c) reasonable living expenses while travelling to Sudbury;
d) one advance visit for the purpose of securing suitable housing. The newly appointed Members may be accompanied by their spouse in this instance."

question: What are the rules concerning sabbatical leaves?
answer:
According to Article 22.07 of the Collective Agreement, the rules concerning sabbatical leaves are as follows:

* A sabbatical leave is for a period of either 12 months commencing on July 1 or 6 months commencing on either July 1 or January 1 (source: "Collective Agreement" page 22.07).
* No portion of the academic year in which a sabbatical leave is taken shall count toward the years of eligibility entitlement (source: same as above).
* A sabbatical leave includes the appropriate vacation entitlement proportional to the length of the leave (source: same as above).

Additionally, Article 5.20 provides further rules and guidelines for sabbatical leaves:

* When Members take a sabbatical leave after three years, all accumulated years of eligibility are exhausted except as otherwise provided for by this Collective Agreement (source: "SABBATICAL LEAVE" page 5.20.01).
* When the sabbatical leave is postponed, the Member shall receive one year's sabbatical credit for the year postponed so that their next sabbatical leave will occur according to their original sabbatical rotation (source: same as above).
* Sabbaticals after three years can be granted provided that Members have tenure when the leave is taken (source: "SABBATICAL LEAVE" page 5.20.01).

Finally, Article 12.20 states that immediately following the completion of a sabbatical leave, the Member is required to return to the University for a period equal to the length of the leave taken, or to satisfy some other arrangement that is mutually acceptable to the member and the Employer (source: "Collective Agreement" page 12.20).

question: What does the collective agreement provide regarding deadlines and time limits?
answer:
According to Article 1.30 - Deadlines and Time Limits of the collective agreement, it states:

"Deadlines and time limits expressed throughout this agreement are binding on the parties, except as expressly referred to herein." (Source: 2017-2020 Thorneloe-LUFA Collective Agreement, page 6)

This means that deadlines and time limits in the collective agreement are enforceable unless specifically mentioned otherwise.

Additionally, it mentions two specific scenarios regarding deadlines:

* If the Thorneloe Steward is absent for 2 or more consecutive days, the Association may appoint another Member as steward during the absence. (Source: 2017-2020 Thorneloe-LUFA Collective Agreement, page 6)
* If the President is absent for 2 or more consecutive days, the deadlines for the Employer's responses or actions throughout this agreement shall be deemed to be extended by the length of such absence. (Source: 2017-2020 Thorneloe-LUFA Collective Agreement, page 6)

It also references Article 1.30 in Article 7.20.5 - Extension of Time Limits, which states that all time limits in this Article shall be automatically extended by the number of Recognized and Other Holidays occurring within the time limit period. (Source: LUFA-H Collective Agreement 2012-2016, page 49)

question: What does the agreement say about removal from office of?
answer:
According to the Collective Agreement, the process for removal from office of a Chair/Director is outlined in Article 9.30.3 and Articles 5.2 - REMOVAL FROM OFFICE and 10.10 - REDUNDANCY.

Specifically:

* If there are complaints against the Chair/Director, the Vice-President, Academic may request them to relinquish their office (Article 9.30.3).
* If the Chair/Director does not voluntarily resign as Chair/Director:
	+ The Vice-President, Academic is empowered to suspend that individual as Chair/Director (Article 9.30.3(a)).
	+ The Vice-President, Academic shall instruct the Dean/University Librarian to appoint an Acting-Chair/Director in consultation with the Department/School (Article 9.30.3(b)).
	+ The President shall create an ad hoc committee to investigate the complaint and shall conduct its investigation in accordance with statutory requirements (Article 9.30.3(c)).
* The decision of the President shall be final, non-grievable and binding on all parties (Article 9.30.3(d)).

Additionally, Article 5.2 outlines the procedures for removal from office, which include:

* Proceedings may be initiated by a written complaint to the Dean/Director of the Library or a written complaint by the Dean/Director of the Library to the Vice-President, Academic.
* The Vice-President, Academic shall invite the Chairperson/Directors and the unit to discuss the complaint. Following an adequate investigation, the Vice-President, Academic may request the Chairperson/Directors to relinquish their office.

It's worth noting that redundancy and financial exigency are also outlined in Article 10.10, but they do not appear to be directly related to removal from office of a Chair/Director.

question: What is stated about redundancy?
answer:
According to Article 11.10 of the collective agreement, here are some key points stated about redundancy:

* No procedures other than those specified in this article will be used to deal with redundancies (Article 11.10).
* The term redundancy does not apply to limited-term appointments that carry no implication of renewal or continuation beyond the stated term in accordance with Article 5.20 (Article 11.10).
* Redundancy is defined in Article 11.10.3, but the specific definition is not provided in the text snippet.
* The Employer must declare a state of redundancy by sending a written notice to the Union and the Vice-President (Article 11.10.2).

question: What conditions apply to patents?
answer:
According to the Collective Agreement 2017-2020, specifically Article 6.30 – PATENTS, the following conditions apply to patents:

* If an invention was made with the use of the Employer's funds, personnel or equipment (Article 6.30.2 and 6.30.4), the Members must sign an agreement with the University before filing a patent application.
* In this case, the Employer assigns all rights, title, and interest in the invention to the Members, subject to sharing equally in the "net proceeds" after deduction of expenses (Article 6.30.4).

Note that unless otherwise provided for in Article 6.30, any invention or patent arising therefrom is considered the sole property of the inventor (Article 6.30.2).

question: How is professional development addressed in the collective agreement?
answer:
According to Article 10.40 – Professional Development Expenditure, the collective agreement addresses professional development as follows:

* The University and the Association agree that staff should have opportunities for personal development and career advancement (Source: Collective Agreement 2002-2005, p. 29).
* Each full-time Counsellor is entitled to $500 in expenditures per contractual year to support their activities in furthering the objectives of the University (Source: Article 10.40.2, Collective Agreement 2002-2005, p. 29).
* Sessional Members are eligible for professional development money of $250 per each three credit course they teach, up to a limit of $2,000 (Source: LUFA-H Collective Agreement 2016-2020, p. 47).

Additionally, the collective agreement provides guidelines for requesting sabbatical leave in Article 12.05:

* A member must provide their Chair with a dossier by 30 September of the year prior to the leave.
* The dossier should include:
	+ A report of the previous sabbatical
	+ An outline of proposed plans explaining how they will contribute to the member's scholarly, pedagogical, or professional development
	+ An updated curriculum vitae (Source: Collective Agreement 2002-2005, p. 31).

question: What does the collective agreement provide regarding physical and mental illness?
answer:
According to Article 5.80.3, when a member's inability to perform reasonable duties is due to physical or mental illness, the case shall be treated separately from cases of dismissal for just cause (page 106 of 246).

Additionally, if sickness or disability is proven, leave shall be granted and the case dealt with within the sickness and disability provisions of this Agreement (Article 5.80.3, page 106 of 246).

In exceptional cases, when behaviour providing grounds for disciplinary measures is judged to be due to illness and the member refuses to be placed under the sickness and disability provisions, disciplinary procedures may be initiated (page 106 of 246).

Furthermore, if a member's non-culpable behaviour results from a physical or mental illness, confirmed by an independent physician agreed upon by LUFA and the Employer, the case shall be dealt with in accordance with the Ontario Human Rights Code (Article 37.08, page 55).

question: What is stated about personnel files?
answer:
According to Article 21 - Faculty Personnel Files, the following is stated about personnel files:

* Official personnel files of a member are kept by the President and are the property of the Employer (Collective Agreement 2015-2018, p. 42).
* Members have the right to examine all of their personnel files upon making prior arrangements to do so (Article 21.02, Collective Agreement 2015-2018, p. 43).
* Material in the files that is to be held confidential will be removed from the files prior to inspection by the member, and an inventory of this material will be provided to the member (Article 21.02, Collective Agreement 2015-2018, p. 43).

Additionally, according to Article 5.70.2 - Personnel Files:

* Members have the right to examine all of their personnel files during normal business hours, after notice in writing, in the presence of the Dean/University Librarian or a person authorized by them (Article 5.70.2, Collective Agreement 2017-2020, p. 12).
* Material in the files that is to be held confidential will be removed from the files prior to inspection by the member, and an inventory of this material will be provided to the member, certified by the Office of the Vice-President, Academic and Provost (Article 5.70.2, Collective Agreement 2017-2020, p. 12).

It is also stated that Members have the right to request the removal from their personnel file of any false, irrelevant or unsubstantiated material (Article 5.70.5, Collective Agreement 2017-2020, p. 13).

question: How is selection of chairs/directors addressed in the collective agreement?
answer:
The selection of Chairs/Directors is addressed in Article 9.15 of the Collective Agreement. Here are some key points regarding chair/director selection:

5.  The Selection Committee may proceed directly to step 8 of the procedure if a strong consensus emerges for the selection of one candidate at step 4, but only if no more than two Members object to the abbreviated selection process (Source: Article 9.15.14).

question: According to the agreement, what applies to sabbatical leave?
answer:
According to Article 7.25 and Section 5.20 of the Thorneloe-LUFA Collective Agreement:

1. A sabbatical leave is not automatic and must be applied for through an approved application procedure (Section 7.25).
2. Applications for sabbatical leave must be submitted by September 30 of the academic year preceding the leave (Article 7.25.3(b)).
3. The Dean/University Librarian must make a recommendation to the Vice-President, Academic and Provost no later than November 15 (Article 7.25.3(c)).
4. The Vice-President, Academic and Provost shall reach a decision and transmit it to the Member no later than December 15 of the academic year preceding the leave (Article 7.25.3(d)).
5. Members are entitled to a stipend equivalent to 85% of their salary during a twelve-month sabbatical leave (Section 5.20.11(b)).
6. Members taking a six-month sabbatical leave, after six years of accumulated sabbatical credit, are entitled to full salary (Section 5.20.11(a)).
7. A sabbatical leave includes the appropriate vacation entitlement proportional to the length of the leave (Article 22.07).

These provisions outline the procedures and terms for applying for and taking a sabbatical leave, as well as the remuneration and benefits associated with it.

question: According to the agreement, what applies to voluntary reduced?
answer:
According to Article 7.35 - VOLUNTARY REDUCED WORKLOAD, a number of provisions apply to voluntary reduced workloads. Specifically:

* Any full-time member with at least 2 years of continuous service can request up to 50% reduction in workload (p. 133)
* The temporary reduction is effective for a 12-month period (p. 139 and p. 133)
* The request must be made 3 months in advance to the Department/School and Dean/University Librarian (p. 139 and p. 133)
* The Dean/University Librarian's approval is required, but such approval should not be unreasonably withheld (p. 139 and p. 133)

These provisions apply to voluntary reduced workloads for periods of up to 12 months, although the University may grant longer or renewed reductions subject to the Dean's/University Librarian's approval.

Additionally, Faculty Members on Voluntary Reduced Workload have the right to benefits and contribute to the benefits plan in accordance with the Collective Agreement (p. 133-140).

answer:

- Must include in their annual report a full written account of their scholastic and professional activities and accomplishments as per the approved sabbatical plan during the leave.

question: What is stated about faculty appointments?
answer:
According to Article 13 — Faculty Appointments, the process of developing recommendations on faculty appointments is a peer-review process (LUFA-H Collective Agreement 2016-2020, p. 22). The University recognizes that input from Members of the same discipline as the contemplated appointment is important, but ultimately, final decisions are the responsibility of the Board and President.

Additionally, Article 13 outlines specific procedures for appointments to Sessional Members (Article 13.09) and Full Time Members (Article 13.07).

For Sessional Members:

* Appointments are first offered to Members with establishment in the course.
* If an appointment cannot be filled by a Member with establishment, Sessional appointments shall be made from rosters of names of potential instructors maintained by the Employer.

For Full Time Members:

* All new appointments must be advertised within and outside the University through suitable national publications.
* A search committee consisting of at least three persons, including the department Chair, representative of another department, and Member designated by the President, shall review applications, conduct interviews, consult with the President, and recommend candidates.

question: What does the collective agreement provide regarding academic freedom?
answer:
According to the Collective Agreement 2017-2020 (page 2) and the Collective Agreement 2018-2021 (pages 1 and e), the relevant provisions regarding academic freedom are:

* Academic freedom is essential to the teaching and research activities of the University, and its pursuit is a fundamental objective of the institution. (Collective Agreement 2017-2020, page 2)
* Academic freedom allows members to search for truth, knowledge, and understanding; to express their opinions freely; and to teach, discuss, and criticize without restriction. (Collective Agreement 2018-2021, Article 0.02(a))
* However, academic freedom does not confer legal immunity, and members are still obligated to perform their duties and responsibilities satisfactorily. (Collective Agreement 2018-2021, page 1)
* Academic freedom also carries the responsibility to respect the rights of other members of the academic community to express their opinions. (Collective Agreement 2018-2021, Article e)

Overall, the collective agreement emphasizes the importance of academic freedom in the pursuit of truth and knowledge, while also acknowledging its limitations and responsibilities.

answer:
According to the Collective Agreement 2011-14 (page 191 of 243), a formal grievance procedure requires that the grievor present a notice of grievance in writing within thirty (30) working days of the date upon which the matter arose. Additionally, it is also stated in Collective Agreement 2015-2018 (pages 45 and 59) that:

* The time limits set out in Article 23 are mandatory (page 59).
* Grievances shall not be filed arbitrarily or in bad faith (pages 45 and 59).

It is also noted in the Collective Agreement 2011-14 that, however, this does not preclude making the Vice-President, Academic and Provost aware of such a grievance, nor does it preclude a grievance from being addressed to the Vice-President, Academic and Provost initially or early on in the process (page 191).

question: What does the agreement say about pregnancy, parental and adoption?
answer:
According to Article 25.06 of the LUFA-H Collective Agreement 2012-2016 (page not specified), there are provisions related to pregnancy leave, parental leave, and adoption.

**Pregnancy Leave:**

* A Member may postpone or interrupt her pregnancy leave by the number of weeks the newborn child is hospitalized but it must be taken within the fifty-two (52) weeks from the date of the birth of the child. (Page not specified)
* The pregnancy leave of a Member who is not entitled to take parental leave shall end on the later of either the day that is seventeen (17) weeks after the pregnancy leave began or the day that is six (6) weeks after the birth, stillbirth or miscarriage.

**Parental Leave:**

* On the occasion of the adoption of a child coming into the care or custody of a parent for the first time, a Member who is a parent shall be entitled to a parental leave of up to thirty-seven (37) weeks. The parental leave must be commenced within the fifty-two (52) weeks from the date the child comes into care or custody of the parent for the first time.

**Adoption:**

* The agreement also allows for parental leave on the occasion of the adoption of a child, with up to thirty-seven (37) weeks available.

question: What are the rules concerning voluntary reduced workload?
answer:
According to Article 7.35 in the Collective Agreement, here are the rules concerning voluntary reduced workload:

1. Any full-time Member of the Bargaining Unit who has at least two (2) years of continuous full-time service at the University can request a temporary reduction in workload with a proportionate reduction in salary and annual vacation entitlement.
	* The temporary reduction is effective for a twelve (12) month period (7.35.1(a)).
	* The request must be made to the Department/School and Dean/University Librarian three (3) months in advance (7.35.1(b)).
	* The Dean/University Librarian's approval is required, and it should not be unreasonably withheld (7.35.1(c)).
2. The University may grant voluntary reduced workloads for periods longer than twelve (12) months and/or renewals of twelve (12) month reduction periods, subject to the Dean's/University Librarian's approval (7.35.2).
3. Faculty Members on Voluntary Reduced Workload have the right to benefits and to contribute to the benefits plan of the University in accordance with the provisions of the Collective Agreement for sharing contributions (7.35.3).
	* Sick leave: Members are covered for periods of sick leave to the extent of the actual salary paid during that period as per Article 7.55 – Physical and Mental Illness (7.35.3(a)).
	* Long-Term Disability: Members who plan to take a voluntary reduced workload must be provided with specific information concerning coverage for Long-Term Disability during and after the period of voluntary reduced workload (7.35.3(b)).
	* Pension Plan: Members on voluntary reduced workload may contribute to the pension plan on the basis of their normal full salary, subject to Revenue Canada regulations (7.35.3(c)).
	* Life Insurance: Life insurance may be carried based on the Member's normal salary and normal maximum (7.35.3(d)).
	* Sabbatical Leave: Sabbatical leave entitlements for Members on voluntary reduced workload will be pro-rated in accordance with the reduced workload (7.35.3(e)).
4. Members who use this option remain Members of the Bargaining Unit, notwithstanding the definition of Membership as defined in Article 2.15 – Recognition of the Bargaining Unit (7.35.4).
5. For the application of tenure and promotion policies, periods of reduced workload are pro-rated in accordance with the reduction in workload (7.35.5). Full-time research and teaching activities at another institution while a Member is on voluntary reduced workload at Laurentian will be counted for purposes of the minimum time requirement for promotion.
6. Members on voluntary reduced workload retain both the right and the obligation to contribute to the administrative work of the University, and evaluations of such activity should recognize the reduced workload (7.35.6).
7. During the period of voluntary reduced workload, Members are expected to submit annual reports as per Article 5.45 – Annual Report for Members in order to qualify for Progress-Through-The-Ranks increments.

Note that these rules may have been modified or updated since the last collective agreement was signed (Collective Agreement 2017-2020). It's always best to check with the University or the Union for the most up-to-date information.

question: What are the rules concerning faculty personnel files?
answer:
According to Article 21 of the Collective Agreement 2015-2018 (pages 42 of 59), there are specific rules concerning faculty personnel files:

* The official personnel files of a member shall be kept by the President and are the property of the Employer (Article 21.01).
* Members have the right to examine all their personnel files, upon making prior arrangements to do so (Article 21.02).
* Material in the files that is to be held confidential according to the provisions of this Agreement will be removed from the files prior to their inspection by the member.
* There are two types of files: active files and archival files. Active files shall contain only information allowed under Article 5, while archival files shall contain material banned for use in subsequent proceedings (Collective Agreement 2015-2018, page not specified).

Additionally, there are specific rules regarding confidential information:

* All letters or assessments solicited by the Faculty Personnel Committee and any summaries thereof shall be kept confidential and used only for the purposes for which they were solicited in any subsequent proceedings against that Member (Article 5.70.8).
* Student evaluations, in numerical or written form, shall not be admissible as evidence in any process involving a Member's tenure, promotion or dismissal if such evaluations are more than five years old (Article 5.70.9).
* The Employer agrees not to use any unofficial personnel information that is not maintained in accordance with this Article for any official purposes including disciplinary measures (Collective Agreement 2015-2018, page not specified).

Please note that these rules may have changed since the agreement was last updated. It's always a good idea to verify the information through more recent sources or by contacting the relevant authorities directly.

question: What does the collective agreement provide regarding annual report for members?
answer:
According to Article 10.08 of the Collective Agreement 2018-2021, all full-time members of the Bargaining Unit shall submit a written Report on their activities for the preceding twelve months (from May 1 to April 30) to the President by June 22nd, with a copy to their department chairs. The report will cover all components of members' activities as described in Article 10, Academic Activity.

In preparing their Annual Report, members shall use the standardized form approved by the University of Sudbury Senate and provided by the President's Office (page 22 of 66). It is also the responsibility of the members to provide annually an up-to-date C.V. with their Annual Report (page 22 of 66).

Additionally, Article 8.20 provides further information regarding annual reports for the award/denial of a Progress-Through-The-Ranks Increment (PTR increment), stating that decisions to award the annual increment or notification of a review shall be communicated to the Members by June 30, provided that the Member submitted her/his annual report by May 15 (page 151 of 243).

question: What are the rules concerning research and development?
answer:
According to Article 6 of the collective agreement:

* The work of the RCD Office shall be done in a constructive manner to promote research activities and creativity at Laurentian University, giving better access to funding and research collaboration at the national and international level (Source document: [not specified], page not mentioned).
* Internally or externally-funded grant applications requesting pre-selection or evaluation require the Employer to communicate the composition of the selection committee on the RCD Office website (Article 6.15.2, source document: "Collective Agreement" but specific name not specified, page number not provided).
* The University is a place without obstacles for scholarly work, and the Employer undertakes to make reasonable efforts to support research and creativity in a fair and equitable manner (Article 6.10.2, source document: [not specified], page not mentioned).

Additionally, regarding the administration of funds for research, Article 6.25.4 states that:

* The LURF Committee shall establish its own procedures and develop criteria for the administration of the funds, which must be just, equitable, and consistent with the objective of nurturing and stimulating research at Laurentian University (Source document: "Collective Agreement" but specific name not specified, page number not provided).

question: What is stated about academic freedom?
answer:
According to Article 3.10 of the Collective Agreement, Academic Freedom includes:

* Freedom in teaching (without restriction by prescribed doctrine)
* Freedom in research and scholarship including the right to disseminate and publish results
* Freedom to produce and perform creative works
* Freedom to acquire, preserve, and provide access to documentary material in all formats
* Freedom to participate in professional and representative academic bodies
* Freedom to engage in service to the institution and community
* Freedom to express one's opinion about the University, its administration, and the system

Source: Collective Agreement, page 11.

Additionally, Academic Freedom requires the acknowledgement of the work of others and acceptance of responsibility for one's own beliefs and utterances. It does not confer legal immunity.

Source: Collective Agreement, page 12.

Academic freedom also entails the right to exercise civil liberties as individuals, including the right to contribute to social change through free expression on matters of public interest, without being censored, impeded or hindered by the Employer.

Source: Collective Agreement, page 13.

	+ Members have tenure when the leave commences (Eligibility (a)).

question: What does the agreement say about parking?

question: What does the collective agreement provide regarding discipline?
answer:
According to the collective agreement, the following are key points regarding discipline:

* Discipline must be "just and reasonable" (Source: Collective Agreement, page 1).
* The principle of progressive discipline is applied, except in egregious cases (Source: Collective Agreement, page 1).
* Just cause for disciplinary measures includes:
	+ Gross misconduct, including serious unprofessional behavior and/or misconduct that violates the personal safety of another Member or student (Source: Collective Agreement, 5.75.2(a)).
	+ Persistent failure to discharge academic responsibility (Source: Collective Agreement, 5.75.2(b)).
	+ Serious unprofessional behavior (Source: Collective Agreement, 5.75.2(a)).
