question: Quelles conditions s’appliquent à charge de travail universitaire?
answer:
Selon la Convention collective de l'Association des professeur(e)s de l'Université Laurentienne, voici les conditions qui s'appliquent à la charge de travail universitaire :

* La distribution normale de la charge de travail parmi les trois composantes principales est la suivante :
 + Quarante pour cent (40 %) à l'enseignement ou aux fonctions de bibliothécaire ou d'archiviste [Source : 5.40.3, page inconnue].
 + Quarante pour cent (40%) aux travaux d’érudition, y compris les engagements envers les organismes subventionnaires externes [Source : 5.40.3, page inconnue].
 + Vingt pour cent (20 %) à la régie de l’Université, aux tâches administratives et aux autres contributions à l’Université [Source : 5.40.3, page inconnue].
* L'emploi du temps relatif à l'enseignement/au travail de bibliothèque est communiqué par écrit au Membre par le Doyen/Bibliothécaire en chef avant le 15 juillet après consultation du Secrétaire général [Source : 5.40.3, page inconnue].
* Le Secrétaire général prend la décision finale concernant l’horaire de tous les cours pendant la durée de la présente Convention collective [Source : 5.40.3, page inconnue].
* La composition de la charge de travail d'un Membre peut varier selon sa discipline et elle tient compte des aptitudes du Membre, de la nécessité d'aide à l'enseignement ou au développement de programmes [Source : 5.40.4, page inconnue].

Ces conditions sont présentées dans le document intitulé "Convention collective de l'Association des professeur(e)s de l'Université Laurentienne", mais les numéros de pages ne sont pas fournis.

Référence : Convention collective de l'Association des professeur(e)s de l'Université Laurentienne, Chapitre 5, Articles 5.40.3 et 5.40.4.

question: Selon la convention, qu’est-ce qui s’applique à équité en matière d’emploi?
answer:
Selon l'article 5.25 de la convention collective, les parties appuient le principe d'équité en matière d'emploi tel que défini par les lois provinciales et fédérales et par la politique du Sénat/Conseil des gouverneurs en matière d'équité (Source : "Convention Collective de l'Association des professeur(e)s de l'Université Laurentienne", page non spécifiée).

De plus, les parties s'engagent à s'efforcer d'augmenter dans une mesure équitable la proportion de membres du corps professoral qui appartiennent aux quatre (4) groupes désignés pour l’équité en matière d’emploi : femmes, autochtone, personne handicapée et minorités visibles (Source : "Convention Collective de l'Association des professeur(e)s de l'Université Laurentienne", page non spécifiée).

La convention ne fournit pas plus d'informations sur la mise en œuvre de ces mesures pour promouvoir l'équité en matière d'emploi.

question: Que dit la convention collective au sujet de congés?
answer:
Selon la Convention collective 2015-2018, les membres qui se portent candidats à une élection ont droit à un congé rémunéré (Article 14.02) et l'Employeur ne peut pas refuser son autorisation sans raison valable (7.40.1).

La Convention collective mentionne également que des congés non rémunérés peuvent être accordés, mais il faut suivre les conditions spécifiées dans un document écrit envoyé au Syndicat avant la date du congé (Article 7.40.1).

Source : Convention collective 2015-2018, pages 35 et 136.

Il est important de noter que la Convention collective 2011-14 mentionne également le droit des membres de prendre part à la vie publique ou d'accepter une charge officielle (Article 7.50), mais cela ne concerne pas spécifiquement les congés rémunérés pour les élections.

question: Quelles sont les règles concernant révocation des directeurs?
answer:
La convention collective 2017-2020 de l'Association des professeur(e)s de l'Université Laurentienne précise la procédure de révocation d'un Directeur à l'article 9.30.

Selon cet article, une procédure visant la révocation d'un Directeur peut être entamée de deux manières :

*   En déposant une plainte sous forme écrite auprès du Doyen/Bibliothécaire en chef en spécifiant les motifs (Article 9.30.1 (a)).
*   Le Doyen/Bibliothécaire en chef peut également déposer une plainte auprès du Vice-recteur aux études et Provost en spécifiant ses raisons, qui se rapportent généralement aux critères établis à l’Article 9.10 – Obligations des Directeurs et l’Article 5.15 – Droits, obligations et responsabilités du personnel enseignant et des bibliothécaires professionnels (Article 9.30.1 (b)).

Si le Directeur ne démissionne pas de son propre gré, la procédure continue comme suit :

*   Le Vice-recteur aux études et Provost a la possibilité de suspendre le Directeur de ses fonctions en tant que Directeur. Une fois suspendu, le Membre jouit toujours de tous les autres droits et obligations définis dans la présente Convention collective (Article 9.30.3 (a)).
*   Le Vice-recteur aux études et Provost prie le Doyen/Bibliothécaire en chef, après consultation des Membres du Département/de l’École, d'installer un Directeur intérimaire, ainsi que prévu à l'Article 9.15 – Sélection des Directeurs, et il transmet la plainte, sous forme d'appel, au Recteur (Article 9.30.3 (b)).
*   Le Recteur constitue un comité spécial qui examine la plainte selon les exigences statutaires. À la suite de cet examen, le Recteur rend sa décision sur la question de la révocation (Article 9.30.3 (c)).
*   La décision du Recteur est sans appel, elle ne peut pas faire l'objet d'un grief et lie toutes les parties intéressées (Article 9.30.3 (d)).

Il convient de noter que la procédure de révocation d'un Directeur doit être suivie avec soin pour respecter les droits et obligations des membres de l'équipe universitaire.

question: Que prévoit la convention collective concernant congé sabbatique?
answer:
Selon la Convention collective 2008-11 (page 131 de 246), le congé sabbatique est défini comme une période durant laquelle le Membre est déchargé de ses fonctions habituelles pour lui permettre de :

* Continuer sa formation, poursuivre ses études à un niveau plus avancé dans un centre de recherches ou d'études supérieures, ou suivre des cours de langue (a)
* Consacrer plus de temps aux travaux d’érudition ou de création (b)
* Renforcer les liens entre l'Université et d'autres universités ou d'autres pays, en tant que professeur ou biologiste (c)

En outre, habituellement, toute rémunération supplémentaire acquise au cours du congé sabbatique ne peut excéder une somme qui porterait le total à cent pour cent (100 %) du traitement usuel du Membre en plus des frais de voyage et des frais de déplacement pour lui, son épouse et leurs enfants à charge. Si cette limite est dépassée, l'Université se réserve le droit de réduire le traitement proportionnellement.

Source : Convention collective 2008-11 (page 131 de 246)

question: Quelles conditions s’appliquent à discipline?
answer:
Selon l'article 37 de la Convention collective de l'Association des professeur(e)s de l'Université Laurentienne, les conditions suivantes s'appliquent à la discipline :

* La discipline doit être imposée uniquement pour cause (37.01).
* La discipline doit être juste et raisonnable (37.01).
* La discipline doit être basée sur le principe de la discipline progressive, sauf dans les cas graves (37.01).
* La discipline doit être imposée en conformité avec les principes de justice naturelle et de procédure régulière (37.02).
* Le membre a droit à connaître, en temps utile, la nature des accusations contre lui(e) et à y répondre (37.02).

Source : Convention collective, article 37, page non spécifiée.

question: Selon la convention, qu’est-ce qui s’applique à procédure d’arbitrage?
answer:
Selon la convention collective de l'Association des professeur(e)s de l'Université Laurentienne, les dispositions suivantes s'appliquent à la procédure d'arbitrage :

* Les procédures d'arbitrage se feront de façon accélérée par les parties (page 12).
* La décision de l'arbitre sera définitive et liera les parties et l'employé ou les employés visés (page 12).
* Les parties partagent également les honoraires et les frais de l'arbitre, le cas échéant (page 12).

Ces dispositions sont présentées dans les articles 12.15.4, 12.15.5.

Il est également précisé que la procédure d'arbitrage doit se faire sur la base des critères suivants :

* Chaque partie fait tous les efforts possibles pour résoudre le problème (article 24).
* Aucune position prise ni aucune information présentée à l’occasion de la médiation ne sont admissibles dans le cas où la cause est menée à l’arbitrage (article 24).

Source : Convention collective 2018-2021, pages 12 et 53.

question: Quelles sont les règles concernant mécanisme d'évaluation en vue d'une?
answer:
D'après l'article 5.65 – Mécanisme d'évaluation en vue d'une promotion de la Convention collective 2017-2020, voici les règles concernant le mécanisme d'évaluation en vue d'une promotion :

* Une demande de promotion peut être faite par un membre pendant qu'il est en congé, mais il doit maintenir le contact avec l'université et assumer toutes les dépenses nécessaires lorsqu'on lui demande de se présenter. (Article 5.65.2)
* Le candidat doit présenter sa demande sur le formulaire prescrit et la transmettre au Bureau du Doyen/Bibliothécaire en chef, accompagnée d'une copie papier de toute la documentation nécessaire et pertinente. (Article 5.65.4)
* Pour qu'une décision soit prise au cours de la même année universitaire, la demande de promotion doit parvenir au doyen ou à la bibliothécaire en chef au plus tard le 2 juillet. Les membres sont priés de consulter le doyen ou la bibliothécaire en chef bien avant cette date. (Article 5.65.5)
* Si la demande est faite avant le 1er juin, le doyen ou la bibliothécaire en chef rédigera une évaluation écrite préliminaire qui tient compte des dispositions pertinentes de l'article 5.10 – Lignes directrices touchant les titres universitaires. (Article 5.65.5)
* Les recommandations touchant une demande de promotion sont assujetties à la procédure d'évaluation indiquée à l'article 5.50 – Évaluation du rendement du Membre. (Article 5.65.7)

Il est important de noter que ces règles sont spécifiques au mécanisme d'évaluation en vue d'une promotion et ne concernent pas les autres types d'évaluations prévues par la convention collective.

answer:
La convention collective de l'Association des professeur(e)s de l'Université Laurentienne prévoit plusieurs choses :

1. Concernant les travaux de recherche (15.04) : Lorsque un membre réalise une étude originale pour développer des matériaux commandés par l'Employeur, le membre peut utiliser la recherche pour produire d'autres matériaux universitaires, à condition que le credit soit donné à l'Employeur pour la commission originale et qu'une reconnaissance soit faite que le droit d'auteur du matériel commandé reste avec l'Employeur.

3. Concernant les dossiers personnelles (18.03) : Les membres ont le droit de faire compléter ou corriger leurs dossiers en cas d'erreur ou d'inadéquation et ils ont également le droit de fournir des documents supplémentaires pour y inclure.

question: Comment la convention définit-elle ou décrit-elle révocation des directeurs?
answer:

Cependant, il est important de noter que le document ne spécifie pas clairement les étapes suivantes après l'envoi de la plainte ou les conditions pour révoquer un Directeur. Seule une mention est faite selon laquelle le Doyen/Bibliothécaire en chef examine la situation et offre ses services comme médiateur.

La source document name est "Convention collective de l'Association des professeurs de l'Université Laurentienne" (page inconnue).

question: Que prévoit la convention collective concernant conges sabbatioues?
answer:
Selon l'article 12 de la Convention collective 2018-2021, les membres à temps plein sont admissibles à des congés sabbatiques après six ans d'emploi depuis le dernier congé sabbatique. Un congé sabbatique peut être de une année entière ou de demi-année, selon les cas.

La Convention collective précise que :

* Tous les membres à temps plein sont admissibles à des congés sabbatiques consistant en un congé d’une année entière après six ans d’emploi depuis le dernier congé sabbatique, ou d’une demi-année après trois ans d’emploi depuis le dernier congé sabbatique. (Article 12.02)
* Un membre n’est admissible à un premier congé sabbatique qu'après six ans d'emploi à temps plein à l’Université de Sudbury dans un poste permanent ou à Pessai. (Article 12.02)

La Convention collective souligne également que le but d’un congé sabbatique est de favoriser la poursuite de la connaissance et d'aider l'Université à atteindre ses objectifs de recherche en accordant aux membres de manière régulière une occasion de consacrer toute leur énergie à la recherche et à l’étude. (Article 12.01)

En outre, si le directeur élu est éligible à un congé sabbatique au cours de son mandat, le Département veillera à ce qu’un directeur intérimaire soit choisi six (6) mois avant son départ en congé sabbatique. (Article 12.02)

Source : Convention collective 2018-2021, Article 12.

question: Comment la convention collective traite-t-elle de situation financière critique?
answer:
Selon l'article 10.15 de la Convention collective 2015-2018 (page non spécifiée), une « situation financière critique » est définie comme un déficit substantiel qui dure plus de deux ans fiscaux, suivant les méthodes de comptabilité généralement acceptées.

La convention colle également les critères suivants pour déterminer si une situation est considérée comme financièrement critique :

(a) La situation financière de l'Université (c'est-à-dire le budget global et non seulement les éléments se rapportant à l'enseignement et aux traitements) présente des déficits qui semblent se prolonger plus de deux années fiscales.

(b) L'impact sur la priorité pédagogique de l'Université dans un contexte où le budget doit être ajusté.

Il convient de noter que les normes énoncées pour évaluer le rendement d'un membre sont exposées dans l'article 8.04 (page 11). Ces normes incluent l'évaluation du rendement en enseignement, en travaux d'érudition et au service à l'Université, à la profession et à la collectivité.

Source : Convention collective 2015-2018, article 10.15

question: What are the rules concerning absence: general?
answer:
According to Article 7.20 - ABSENCE - GENERAL, the following rules apply:

1. The University requires its Members to be available on a regular and ongoing basis to ensure that scheduled and unscheduled activities can be carried out in an orderly manner (Article 7.20.1).
2. Any absence should not normally interfere with assigned and/or scheduled activities and the harmonious functioning of the Department/School (Article 7.20.2).
3. Absences from campus affecting teaching/professional librarian duties should be reported to the President and the Thorneloe Steward for adjustment prior to the grievance process commencing, as stated in Article 7.20.3.

Note: There is no general rule stating a specific number of days of absence that would automatically trigger a paid leave or other benefits, except for the mention of replacement costs for absences (Article 3.20.5).

question: What does the collective agreement provide regarding pregnancy, parental and adoption?
answer:
The Collective Agreement 2017-2020 provides the following information regarding pregnancy, parental, and adoption leaves:

1. For pregnant full-time Members or pregnant Master Lecturer Members, they are entitled to 17 weeks of pregnancy leave (Article 7.60.1(a)).
2. During this period, they shall receive:
   - 100% of their nominal salary for the first week.
   - Up to a maximum of 16 additional weeks at 75% of their nominal salary.
3. The collective agreement also mentions that in the case where a newborn child is hospitalized, a Member may postpone or interrupt her pregnancy leave by the number of weeks the newborn child is hospitalized, but it must be taken within 52 weeks from the date of birth (Article 7.60).
4. For adoption leaves, Members who are parents and choose to take parental leave under the Employment Insurance Act and other applicable laws have the right to a parental leave of up to 35 weeks (14.06). During this period, they will receive 100% of their nominal salary for five days after working for at least 12 consecutive months consecutively.

question: What does the collective agreement provide regarding academic workload?
answer:
The collective agreement provides several details regarding academic workload:

1. The President must ensure that the annual academic workload is determined, distributed, and scheduled as equitably as possible (10.07 Annual Academic Workload).
2. The member's assigned annual academic workload must take into account factors such as student enrolments, preparation, grading, administration, counselling, and research (10.07 Annual Academic Workload).
3. Full-time faculty are expected to have a normal teaching load of 15 credits per academic year, with a minimum of 12 credits taught live (3.38 Teaching Workload).
4. The workload includes three components: teaching/professional librarianship/archives management, scholarly activity, and university governance/administrative duties (5.40 Academic Workload).
5. The distribution of the workload among these components is typically: 40% teaching/professional librarianship/archives management, 40% scholarly activity, and 20% university governance/administrative duties (5.40 Academic Workload).
6. The academic workload is assigned in a fair and equitable manner, with each member receiving a copy of the chair's recommendations on their own workload by April 1, and a summary of recommendations for other members in the department/school by April 1 (5.40 Academic Workload).
7. The Dean/University Librarian must communicate the assignment of the workload to each member in writing by July 15, after consulting with the Registrar (5.40 Academic Workload).

However, if the Dean/University Librarian and the Selection Committee are unable to agree on an appointment, the selection procedure shall be reinstated as in Article 9.15.3 above. (9.15.11)

question: What are the rules concerning moving expenses?
answer:
There are two sets of rules regarding moving expenses in the provided document:

1. Article 8.55 - MOVING EXPENSES (from the 2012-2016 Collective Agreement):

* On initial appointment to the University, each regular full-time Member is entitled to reimbursement for moving expenses subject to certain conditions.
* The University shall reimburse claims at a rate of 100% to a maximum of $5,000. In exceptional circumstances, the University may exceed this amount.
* Moving expenses include:
 + Moving, packing, crating, and unpacking of household goods and personal effects
 + Transfer of family by the most economical means of transportation
 + Reasonable living expenses for the duration of the trip to the new location
 + One (1) advance visit for the purpose of securing suitable housing. The newly appointed Members may be accompanied by their spouse in this instance.
* Employees appointed on a contract of twelve (12) month's duration or less shall not normally be eligible to claim moving expenses, except with special approval from the Vice-President, Academic and Provost.

2. Article 4.55 - MOVING EXPENSES (from the 2002-2005 Collective Agreement):

* On initial appointment to the University, each regular full-time Member is entitled to reimbursement for moving expenses subject to certain conditions.
* The University shall reimburse claims at a rate of 100% to a maximum of $2,500. In exceptional circumstances, the University may exceed this amount.
* Moving expenses include:
 + Moving, packing, crating, and unpacking of household goods and personal effects
 + Transfer of family by the most economical means of transportation
 + Reasonable living expenses for the duration of the trip to the new location
 + One (1) advance visit for the purpose of securing suitable housing. The newly appointed Members may be accompanied by their spouse in this instance.
* Employees appointed on a contract of twelve (12) month's duration or less shall not normally be eligible to claim moving expenses, except with special approval from the Vice-President, Academic.

Note that there are some differences between the two sets of rules regarding moving expenses.

* Non-renewal of term appointments shall not be subject to grievance.

question: How does the agreement define or describe discipline?
answer:
According to Article 5 of the Collective Agreement, discipline is defined as just and reasonable, based on the principle of progressive discipline, except in egregious cases (5.75.2). Just cause for discipline includes:

* Gross misconduct including serious unprofessional behavior and/or misconduct constituting a grave and direct violation of the personal safety of another Member; Members of the University community and/or students of the University community (5.75.2(a)).
* Persistent failure to discharge academic responsibility as defined in this Collective Agreement.

In other words, discipline is only justified in cases where there is gross misconduct or a serious breach of academic responsibility.

question: What are the rules concerning copyright?
answer:
According to Article 6.35 of the Collective Agreement 2017-2020, the rules concerning copyright are as follows:

* The Member who is the creator of any work retains the copyright unless otherwise stated in this Article (Section 6.35.1).
* The University holds copyright to any work, including creative works, printed material, computer programs, on-line course material, films, slides, tapes, or similar materials produced by Members as part of their normal workload for the University for use in its distance education courses (Section 6.35.2). However, if a Member and the University enter into a special contract for such work, the copyright shall be vested in the University (Section 6.35.3).
* All special contracts for distance education courses must contain an Article allowing contributors to use parts of any course they have created for their own classroom purposes, provided they do not use such material in another distance education course without permission from the University (Section 6.35.4).
* The master copy of any work whose copyright is vested in the University under the terms of this Article shall be the property of the University, and it shall be responsible for the custody and control of such works and copies thereof (Section 6.35.5).
* In cases where consent, fees, or licenses are required for the use of incorporated materials in works in which the University has copyright under the terms of this Article, the contributor must notify the University by provision of a list of works that require such clearance (Section 6.35.6).

question: According to the agreement, what applies to voluntary reduced workload?
answer:
According to Article 7.35 - VOLUNTARY REDUCED WORKLOAD of the Collective Agreement 2008-11, a full-time Member of the Bargaining Unit who currently occupies a regular full-time position and has at least two (2) years of continuous full-time service can be granted up to 50% temporary reduction in workload.

Specifically:

* The request for voluntary reduced workload must meet certain conditions, including:
 + Having at least two (2) years of continuous full-time service
 + Occupying a regular full-time position
* The terms of the agreement include:
 + A proportionate reduction in salary
 + Annual vacation entitlement
* The temporary reduction is effective for a 12-month period.
* The report shall become part of their personnel file.

Note: There is no mention of study leave, sabbatical credit, or paid activity while on leave in relation to the voluntary reduced workload. Those provisions are found in other articles (7.30.6).

question: According to the agreement, what applies to promotion procedures?
answer:
According to the Laurentian University Faculty Association collective agreement, promotion procedures are as follows:

* A Member is eligible to apply for promotion while on leave (Article 16.02).
* Assessments from additional colleagues with relevant qualifications and experience may be introduced at the discretion of the Member (Article 16.04(iii)).
* The Dean/Director of the Library will officially request assessments from nominated assessors, and the FPC/FFPC/LPC will decide what weight to give these assessments.
* Promotions are effective on July 1st of the academic year following the year in which the application was made and approved (Article 16.05).
* The promotion is not necessarily tied to a specific date, but rather follows the university receiving confirmation of the Member's doctoral degree (Article 16.05).

Additionally, the agreement states that:

* A Lecturer who obtains a doctoral degree shall have an approved promotion to Assistant Professor.
* Promotions are subject to breakpoints, and increments are awarded according to Article 8.15- Progress-Through-The-Ranks-Increment and Article 8.25 - Merit Increments.

No specific information is provided in the context about promotion procedures beyond what has been stated above.

According to Section 11.16 of the LUFA-H Collective Agreement 2016-2020, a "recommendation" by the Department is defined as:

In other words, the President is required to consider the recommendation made by the Department where the appointment is taking place.

Additionally, Section 11.06(c) also mentions that the Department will provide the President with recommendations on the content of the Sessional appointment contracts.

It's worth noting that the agreement requires that the recommendation be "reasoned", implying that it should be based on a careful and informed evaluation of the individual's qualifications and suitability for the position.

question: What conditions apply to selection of chairs/directors?
answer:
According to Article 9.15.12, the Chair/Director shall be a tenured or probationary Member of faculty. Any outside appointment shall be made in accordance with Article 5.20 – Appointment and Renewal.

* A six (6) credit teaching load reduction during each calendar year served as Chair/Director.

* An overload payment (or proportion thereof) in lieu of a full teaching load, if assigned by the Dean or University Librarian.

question: What are the rules concerning vacation?
answer:
According to the Collective Agreement, there are two main rules concerning vacation:

1. Members are required to take their vacation entitlement, and it cannot be accumulated from year to year (17.03).
2. If a member chooses not to take their vacation entitlement, they will continue to receive their normal earnings during that time period, but will not receive any remuneration in lieu of vacation (17.04).

Additionally, the Collective Agreement outlines the duration of sick leave and long-term disability benefits, but these are separate from the rules regarding vacation.

question: What conditions apply to rights and privileges of the union?
answer:
According to Article 2.40, the following conditions apply to the rights and privileges of the Union:

1. The Employer must provide the Union with access to a private serviced office in an academic area of the University, with a floor area no less than what was allocated as at July 1st, 2017 (Source: Article 2.40.1).
2. The Employer must also provide the Union with access to the University Club for use by Members and their guests (Source: Article 2.40.1).
3. Additionally, the Employer must provide a common room for use by Members and their guests (Source: Article 2.40.1).
4. Payment of regular salary and benefits is not considered as use of the Employer's funds for purposes of interpreting clauses related to the Union's rights and privileges (Source: Article 6.30.6).
5. The Union grants the Employer a non-exclusive, royalty-free, irrevocable, indivisible, and non-transferable right to use solely for the University certain rights and privileges of the Union (Source: Article 6.30.7).

question: What conditions apply to professional development expenditures?
answer:
According to Article 6.45 and Article 4.70 of the Collective Agreement, the following conditions apply to professional development expenditures:

* Membership fees for professional and/or learned societies related to the Member's discipline (Article 6.45 - Professional Development Expenditures)
* Subscriptions to professional and/or learned journals (Article 6.45 - Professional Development Expenditures)
* Books, materials, equipment, and services directly related to research and teaching/professional Library work (Article 6.45 - Professional Development Expenditures)
* Registration fees for the Member to attend a scholarly conference (Article 6.45 - Professional Development Expenditures)
* Travel including transportation, food and accommodation (subject to University travel policies) for the Member to attend relevant scholarly conferences or seminars, or to visit other universities or research sites to conduct research and scholarly work which cannot be done at Huntington University (Article 6.45 - Professional Development Expenditures)
* Page and reprint charges or costs incurred in the preparation and completion of scholarly manuscripts (Article 6.45 - Professional Development Expenditures)
* Professional/academic development or upgrading (Article 6.45 - Professional Development Expenditures)
* Hiring part-time assistants in support of research and teaching, excluding marking (Article 6.45 - Professional Development Expenditures)
* Tuition fees (Article 4.70 - Professional Development Expenditures for Sessional Members)

Additionally, full-time academic staff who are on study leave or have a voluntary reduced workload are eligible for professional development expenditures on a prorated basis (Article 30.05).

question: According to the agreement, what applies to academic?
answer:
Based on the provided context, here are the answers to your question:

1. What applies to academic staff regarding their time allocation?

According to 11.03 Rights and Responsibilities of Full-Time Scholars/Researchers (a) and (b), full-time academic staff have the right and responsibility to devote a "reasonable proportion" of their time to scholarly activity.

2. How is 'scholarly activity' defined for academic staff?

For the purpose of this Collective Agreement, "scholarly activity" means:
i) Research directed towards a contribution to knowledge, and the dissemination of its results;
ii) Participation in those academic activities that contribute to the enhancement, creation, interpretation, preservation, and dissemination of knowledge.

3. What is the process for assessing probationers or new hires with disabilities?

According to 11.03 Rights and Responsibilities of Full-Time Scholars/Researchers (iv), The FPC/FFPC/LPC will be responsible for deciding what weight to give assessments from additional colleagues with relevant qualifications and experience, after a member requests such assessments.

answer:

* Race
* Creed
* Colour
* Age (as defined in the Ontario Human Rights Code)
* Sex
* Nationality
* Language
* Ancestry
* Place of origin
* Sexual orientation
* Physical handicap
* Marital or family status (except where such status places the individual in a conflict of interest)
4. This provision does not apply where discrimination is permissible or mandated under any statute.

Additionally, Article 3.02 states that there will be no:

question: How does the agreement define or describe retirement?
answer:
The Collective Agreement 2017-2020, specifically Article 2 and Article 4.15, describes retirement as follows:

* Retirement is defined as a participant's irrevocable exit from employment with Laurentian University.
* For phased retirement, the cumulative appointment over the two (2) year phased retirement period will be at least one hundred percent (100%) but not more than one hundred and twenty-five percent (125%) of a full-time appointment.
* A participant who is eligible and qualifies for Long-Term Disability benefits during the phased retirement program may opt out of the phased retirement program and retire instead of receiving Long-Term Disability benefits.

Additionally, Article 4.15.7 states that Retirees shall be deemed to have Establishment with respect to a particular course either at the time they are appointed to teach a course for the third (3rd) academic year on sessional contracts or at the time they are appointed to teach it on a first sessional contract after having taught the course twice as part of their full-time workload.

It's also worth noting that the agreement mentions the "Normal Retirement Date" in Article 2, which is likely the date when a participant is considered fully retired and no longer eligible for phased retirement benefits.

question: What is stated about selection of chairs/directors?
answer:
According to Article 9.20 – Term of Office of Chairs/Directors:

* The term of office for Chairs/Directors normally lasts three (3) years, renewable by Department/School selection per Article 9.15 – Selection of Chairs/Directors.
* If a Chair/Director is unable to carry out their duties for four (4) months or less, they should make provision for the takeover of their duties in consultation with the Department/School and Dean/University Librarian.
* If the absence is for a period longer than four (4) months, the Chair/Director shall relinquish their title and a new Chair/Director shall be selected according to the procedures set out in Article 9.15 – Selection of Chairs/Directors.

Additionally, the Abbreviated Selection Process (Article 9.15.14) states that if there is a strong consensus for the selection of one candidate at step 4, the Selection Committee may proceed directly to step 8 of the procedure. However, if at least two Members object to the abbreviated process, the Committee shall follow the full procedure.

It's also worth noting that the Chair/Director must be a tenured or probationary Member of faculty (Article 9.15.12).

question: What conditions apply to redundancy?
answer:
According to Article 11.10 of the Collective Agreement, a redundancy (also known as a workload redundancy) shall occur under the following conditions:

1. The Employer must declare a state of redundancy by sending a written notice to the Union and the Vice-President, Academic and Provost.
2. Such an action will not result in insufficient academic personnel for the Department(s)/School(s) to continue offering a viable program(s).
3. The proposed reductions must be consistent with normal workloads as defined in Article 5.40 – Academic Workload.
4. The proposed reductions must not create an inequitable workload for the remaining employees.

question: According to the agreement, what applies to grievance procedure?
answer:
According to the Collective Agreement 2015-2018, Article 23:

* A grievance is a claim, dispute, or complaint involving the interpretation, application, administration, or alleged violation of this collective agreement. (Article 23.01, page 45)
* Grievances shall not be filed arbitrarily or in bad faith. (Article 23.01, page 45)
* Any Member's complaint which is not settled by the President within ten (10) working days of initially discussing the complaint shall commence at stage one (1) of the grievance procedure. (Article 34.02)

Additionally, there are specific provisions for individuals who accept recall offers and sessional members regarding their rights in relation to roster, seniority, and establishment rights.

question: What does the agreement say about dismissal procedures?
answer:
The 2017-2020 Thomeloe-LUFA Collective Agreement states that "Dismissal" means the termination for just cause of a term appointment or a probationary appointment before the end of the stated contractual period, or the termination of a tenure appointment for cause at any time other than normal retirement.

According to Article 4.65, just cause for dismissal is defined as:

a. gross misconduct;
b. persistent failure to discharge academic responsibilities as defined in this Agreement either through incompetence or neglect of duties.

However, cases involving the inability of a Member to perform reasonable duties by reason of physical or emotional illness shall be treated separately from cases for disciplinary measures (Article 4.60.6). If sickness or disability is proven, leave shall be granted and the case dealt with within the University's sickness and disability provisions.

In exceptional cases when behavior providing grounds for disciplinary measures is judged to be due to illness and the Member refuses to be placed under the sickness and disability provisions of this Agreement, disciplinary procedures may be initiated (Article 4.60.6).

Additionally, if a Member is on sickness or disability leave and considers that they have recovered and are capable of undertaking normal academic activities, they must present medical evidence from a medical practitioner to the President (Article 4.60.6).

question: What are the rules concerning sabbatical leaves?
answer:
According to the Collective Agreement, here are the key rules concerning sabbatical leaves:

1. A sabbatical leave can be taken for a period of 12 months (Article 22.07(01)), or 6 months (either July 1st or January 1st).
2. The academic year in which a sabbatical leave is taken shall not count towards the years of eligibility entitlement (Article 22.07(02)).
3. A sabbatical leave includes proportional vacation entitlement (Article 22.07(01)).
4. Members must return to work for a period equal to the length of the leave taken immediately following the completion of a sabbatical leave (Article 12.20).
5. Sabbaticals can be granted after three years of service, provided that the member has tenure at the time of the leave.
6. If a sabbatical leave is postponed, the member receives one year's sabbatical credit to keep their original rotation schedule intact.
7. Members who terminate employment between June 1 and Labour Day with no formal teaching duties during part or all of that period shall take as much vacation entitlement as possible (Article 22.07(02)).

question: How does the agreement define or describe compassionate leave?
answer:
According to the Collective Agreement 2015-2018, Section 14.07 Compassionate Leave, a full-time Member who holds a tenured or probationary appointment within the University is eligible for a paid leave of absence for a period of up to 3 days per calendar year to fulfill responsibilities relating to the special needs of a member of their family.

The agreement specifies that "special needs" may include, but are not restricted to:

* Resettlement of aged or disabled parents (Section 14.07 Compassionate Leave, page 37 of 59)
* Serious illness of parents, partner, or child
* Medical treatment of partner or child (Section 14.07 Compassionate Leave, page 37 of 59)

Additionally, Section 39.02 lists some of the responsibilities that may be covered under compassionate leave, but it does not provide a comprehensive definition of what constitutes "special needs".

question: What does the collective agreement provide regarding discipline?
answer:
According to the Collective Agreement 2017-2020, discipline shall be just and reasonable, based on the principle of progressive discipline, except in egregious cases (5.75.2).

Just cause for disciplinary action is defined as:

(a) Gross misconduct including serious unprofessional behaviour and/or misconduct constituting a grave and direct violation of the personal safety of another Member; Members of the University community and/or students of the University community.

(b) Persistent failure to discharge academic responsibility as defined in this Collective Agreement.

Note that there is no page number provided for this specific claim, but it can be found in Section 5.75 of the Collective Agreement document.

question: According to the agreement, what applies to selection of chairs/directors?
answer:
According to the agreement, the following apply to the selection of Chairs/Directors:

* The Chair/Director shall be a tenured or probationary Member of faculty. (Article 9.15.12)
* Any outside appointment shall be made in accordance with Article 5.20 – Appointment and Renewal. (Article 9.15.12)
* In exceptional circumstances, the Vice-President, Academic and Provost and the Dean/University Librarian may appoint an acting Chair/Director for a period of up to four months, consistent with Article 9.20 – Term of Office of Chairs/Directors and Article 9.30 – Removal from Office of Chairs/Directors. (Article 9.15.13)
* The selection process may follow an abbreviated procedure if at least two Members object to it. In such cases, the full procedure shall be followed. (Article 9.15.14)
* The term of office for Chairs/Directors shall normally be for three years, renewable by Department/School selection per Article 9.15 – Selection of Chairs/Directors. (Article 9.20.1)
* Chairs/Directors are entitled to a six credit teaching load reduction during each calendar year served as Chair/Director, with an additional three credit course reduction for Departments/Schools with twenty-five or more full-time Members and employees. (Article 9.25.1(a))
* Chairs/Directors are also entitled to an annual stipend, pro-rated based on the number of full-time teaching/librarian Members in the Department/School and other full-time equivalent employees who report to the Chair/Director. (Article 9.25.2)

answer:
Moving expenses paid to a new Member will constitute a loan made by the University. This loan will be retired when the Member has completed three (3) years of continuous service with the University, each year being equivalent to one-third of the reimbursement of the loan.

question: What is stated about academic workload?

* The President will assign academic workload in a fair and equitable manner (Article 12.01).

question: What does the collective agreement provide regarding disciplinary measures?
answer:
According to Section 5.75 of the collective agreement, the only formal "Disciplinary Measures" that may be taken by the Employer against a Member are:

* A letter of reprimand, specifying the grounds and adding this reprimand to the personnel file (5.75.3(a))

Additionally, the collective agreement outlines the process for disciplinary actions, including:

* The Member and their union representative shall receive 5 working days' notice of the meeting where the allegation will be discussed (5.75.4)
* The Dean/University Librarian must review the particulars of the allegation with the Member and provide an opportunity for the Member to respond (5.75.4)
* The parties shall attempt to resolve the matter in a manner acceptable to all concerned (5.75.5)

It's also worth noting that disciplinary actions are subject to the principle of progressive discipline, except in egregious cases (5.75.2).

These conditions are outlined in the collective agreement document, which was last updated for the years 2011-12, 2012-13, and 2013-14, as referenced in Article 8.10 - Salary Structure and other relevant sections.

question: What are the rules concerning professional development?
answer:
The rules concerning professional development for sessional Members at Laurentian University are outlined in Article 30.07 of the LUFA-H Collective Agreement 2016-2020.

Sessional Members are eligible for a professional development allowance of $250 per each three credit course they teach, up to a maximum limit of $2,000 per academic year. This allowance is intended to be used in both the current and subsequent academic years.

There is no specific rule regarding the types of courses or areas of focus that qualify for this allowance, although it implies that teaching any course may potentially qualify (as long as it's within the three-credit limit).

question: How is study leaves addressed in the collective agreement?
answer:
Study leaves are addressed in Article 7.30 of the LUFA-H Collective Agreement 2016-2020, specifically stating that:

* A leave for upgrading academic qualifications shall be known as a Study Leave.
* Such leave must be in the best interests of the University.
* The maximum length of study leave granted during a Member's academic career shall not exceed two (2) years.
* A study leave may be granted to a tenured or probationary Member.

Additionally, Section 23.02 of the collective agreement outlines the conditions under which a Member on study leave is entitled to receive a salary, stating that:

* The Member shall receive 30% of their salary, up to a maximum of $40,000.
* Time spent on other types of leave (e.g. LTD leave) with a period exceeding six (6) months shall not count towards the eligibility requirements for three (3) years of uninterrupted service or towards years of service for determining salary while on study leave.

question: How is laurentian university research addressed in the collective agreement?
answer:
The Collective Agreement 2017-2020 addresses Laurentian University Research through several articles:

	+ Providing funding for start-up grants for new full-time Members ($8,000 minimum)
	+ Offering a Research Support Fund (LURF) of $160,000 per year to enhance scholarly productivity
	+ Providing additional funding of $20,000 per year to support research activities and conferences for retired Members, Sessional Members, and Master Lecturers
* Article 6.25 – LAURENTIAN UNIVERSITY RESEARCH FUND (LURF) details the LURF program, including:
	+ An open competition among Members for LURF funding
	+ A LURF Committee that evaluates proposals submitted to the ORS Office once a year

These articles demonstrate the Employer's commitment to supporting research and creativity at Laurentian University.

question: How does the agreement define or describe rights?
answer:
The agreement defines rights as follows:

* In Section 6.30.9, it states that the Employer agrees not to use the name of the University without its interest in inventions (i.e., the Employer has no interest).
* In Section 4.72.2, it states that the University shall hold copyright to any work including any creative work, printed material, computer programme, on-line course material, films, slides, tapes or similar materials produced by Members as part of their normal workload for the University.
* In Section 6.35.1 and 4.72.2, it states that the Member retains the copyright to their own work (unless otherwise stated), while the University holds the copyright to any work created as part of their normal workload.

Overall, the agreement distinguishes between the rights held by the Employer (University) and those held by the Members (individual academics). The Employer's rights are limited to cases where it has an interest in the invention, while the Members' rights are retained unless they have assigned them to the University.

question: What conditions apply to retirement?
answer:
According to Article 19 – RETIREMENT AND RESIGNATION, the following conditions apply to retirement:

1. The possible retirement dates of a member and the provisions for early retirement under the University pension plan are governed by the terms of the plan to which the University belongs (Article 19.01).
2. A member must be five (5) years or less from the attainment of their Normal Retirement Date to be eligible for Special Voluntary Early Retirement (SVER), as outlined in clauses (a) and (b) of Article 19.04.
3. A member must have completed at least fifteen (15) years of full-time service at Laurentian University as of the proposed date of commencement of SVER, as stated in clause (b) of Article 19.04.
4. A member who meets the eligibility criteria may choose to take SVER on any July 1 (January 1), and must apply in writing to the Dean/University Librarian by no later than October 1 (April 1) (Article 19.05).

These conditions outline the requirements for retirement, including the timeframe from Normal Retirement Date and the minimum service period.

question: What are the rules concerning sabbatical leaves?
answer:
The rules concerning sabbatical leaves are as follows:

1. A sabbatical leave can be for a period of 12 months, starting on July 1st, or 6 months, starting on either July 1st or January 1st.
2. No portion of the academic year during which a sabbatical leave is taken counts towards the years of eligibility entitlement (Article 22.02).
3. A sabbatical leave includes vacation entitlement proportional to the length of the leave.
4. Members who terminate their employment between June 1st and Labour Day with no formal teaching duties must take as much of their vacation entitlement as possible during that period (Article 5.20 - Sabbatical Leave).
5. In the event of a Member's death, unused vacation entitlement will be paid to their estate (Article 5.20).
6. When Members take a sabbatical leave after three years, all accumulated years of eligibility are exhausted except as otherwise provided for by this Collective Agreement.
7. If a sabbatical leave is postponed, the Member receives one year's sabbatical credit towards their next sabbatical leave.
8. Sabbaticals can be granted after three years, provided that the member has tenure (Article 22.07).
9. Following the completion of a sabbatical leave, the member must return to the University for a period equal to the length of the leave taken, or satisfy some other mutually acceptable arrangement.

It's worth noting that the rules regarding sabbatical leaves are outlined in Article 5.20 - Sabbatical Leave and Article 22.07 in the Collective Agreement.

question: How is professional development addressed in the collective agreement?
answer:
Professional development is addressed in two main ways:

1. Article 10.40 of the Collective Agreement states that the University values staff personal development and career advancement, and provides $500 in expenditures for each full-time Counsellor to support their activities.
2. Sessional Members are eligible for professional development money of up to $2,000 per year, with a maximum of $250 per three credit course they teach.

Both articles aim to encourage staff members to develop their abilities and leadership potential, but the specifics of the benefits differ between full-time and sessional staff.

question: What does the collective agreement provide regarding physical and mental illness?
answer:
The Collective Agreement provides several provisions regarding physical and mental illness:

* Cases involving non-culpable behaviour by a Member as a result of physical or mental illness, which has been confirmed by an independent physician agreed to by LUFA and the Employer, shall be treated separately from cases for disciplinary conduct and shall be dealt with in accordance with the Ontario Human Rights Code. (Article 37.08, page 55)

* The inability of a Member to perform reasonable duties by reason of physical or mental illness shall be treated separately from cases of dismissal for just cause. (Article 5.80.3, page 106)

* Where such inability has been established, leave shall be granted and the case dealt with within the University's sickness and disability provisions set out in Article 7.55 – Physical and Mental Illness. (Article 5.80.3, page 106)

* If a Member is on sickness or disability leave and considers that they have recovered and are capable of undertaking normal academic activities, they shall present medical evidence from a medical practitioner to their Dean/University Librarian. If the Dean/University Librarian agrees, the Member shall be reinstated with full rights and benefits forthwith. (Article 7.55.2, page 246)

* The majority opinion of three medical practitioners shall prevail in cases where there is disagreement about the Member's ability to return to work. (Article 7.55.2, page 247)

question: According to the agreement, what applies to academic activity?
answer:
According to Article 10 - ACADEMIC ACTIVITY of the Collective Agreement, academics are entitled and expected to engage in various activities in a reasonable proportion, varying from individual to individual. These activities include:

* Performance of teaching duties as assigned according to this Collective Agreement (Article 10.01)
* Research, scholarly, and creative activities (Article 10.01)
* University service (Article 10.01)
* Professional and community service (Article 10.01)

Additionally, the agreement states that the domains of activity carry different sorts of implications for the workload of members, which may vary according to a member's discipline, from member to member, and from year to year for each member.

question: What is stated about personnel files?
answer:
According to Article 21 – Faculty Personnel Files, official personnel files of a member are kept by the President and are the property of the Employer (Section 21.01). Members have the right to examine their personnel files upon making prior arrangements, and material that is confidential will be removed from the files before inspection (Section 21.02).

Additionally, members have the right to:

* Have their files supplemented or corrected in case of error or inadequacy (Section 21.03)
* Provide additional material for inclusion in their personnel files (Section 21.03 and Section 46 of 66)

It's also mentioned that no anonymous material will be kept by the Employer, and certain types of assessments and evaluations may not be admissible as evidence in proceedings involving a member's tenure, promotion, or dismissal (Sections 21.05, 21.06, and 21.07).

Lastly, members can request one copy of their personnel file from the President, excluding confidential material, within five working days at no charge to the member.

(b) Persistent failure to discharge academic responsibility as defined in this Collective Agreement.

"The Employer normally issues contracts by July 1st for courses starting in September, November 1st for courses starting in January, and February 1st for courses starting in May."

This indicates that the normal process for issuing contracts is to do so at these specific dates before the start of each academic term.

Additionally, the collective agreement outlines an abbreviated selection process in case the Dean/University Librarian and the Selection Committee are unable to agree on an appointment (Article 9.15.14).

question: According to the agreement, what applies to sabbatical leave?
answer:
According to the Laurentian University Faculty Association collective agreement:

1. Compensation for sabbatical leaves coincides with the Collective Agreement in place (Clause 22.09). Salary, benefits, and other provisions will be adjusted according to any new agreement between the Board and the Association.
2. During a sabbatical leave, pension calculations are based on the Member's salary that would have been in effect if the Member had not been on sabbatical (Clause 5.20.12).
3. Members granted sabbatical leave must return to the University to resume their responsibilities as a full-time Member for at least one year (Clause 5.20.13).
4. During the period of sabbatical leave, the Member continues to be eligible to receive all fringe benefits as a regular full-time Member (Clause 22.09).

question: What does the agreement say about moving expenses?
answer:
According to Article 31 — MOVING EXPENSES, full-time Members who move from a distance of 100 kilometres or more are entitled to reimbursement for moving expenses. The conditions for reimbursement are:

* All claims must be substantiated by official receipts or reasonable facsimiles (Article 31.01).
* The Employer will reimburse claims at the rate of 100% up to a maximum of $3,000.00. In exceptional circumstances, the Employer may exceed this amount (Article 31.01).

Additionally, Article 7 of the agreement requires Members to register a second mortgage on their property in favor of the University as security for any loan guaranteed under the agreement.

question: What does the agreement say about disciplinary measures?
answer:
The Collective Agreement outlines the following formal disciplinary measures that can be taken by the Employer against a Member:

1. A letter of reprimand, specifying the grounds and adding this reprimand to the personnel file of the Member concerned.
2. The withholding of an annual increment.
3. Suspension without pay for a period of one to five, ten, fifteen, or twenty working days. (The reduction in pay shall be computed as 1/365 of normal salary per day of suspension.)
4. Suspension with pay, which is only applicable if the Vice-President, Academic cites it as a disciplinary measure.

It's worth noting that there are also exceptions and special provisions for certain types of cases, such as:

* Cases involving physical or mental illness being treated separately from disciplinary measures.
* Sessional Members having their grievances dealt with by a separate procedure (Article 4.40.7).
* The requirement for the Member to be given notice and an opportunity to respond before discipline is imposed.

Additionally, the agreement emphasizes that disciplinary measures must be "just and reasonable" and commensurate with the offense, and that the employer shall not release individually identifiable information without the member's consent, except in certain circumstances.

question: According to the agreement, what applies to voluntary reduced?
answer:
According to the Collective Agreement 2008-11 (Article 7.35), Members on Voluntary Reduced Workload:

* May contribute to the pension plan on the basis of their normal full salary with appropriate contributions from the Employee and Employer as outlined in the Collective Agreement, to the extent possible under Revenue Canada regulations.
* Are covered for periods of sick leave to the extent of the actual salary paid during that period (Article 7.55 – Physical and Mental Illness).
* May carry life insurance based on their normal salary and normal maximum.
* Retain both the right and the obligation to contribute to the administrative work of the University, with evaluations of such activity by the Dean/University Librarian recognizing the reduced workload.

It's also mentioned that contributions based on normal salary rather than reduced salary may not be possible under Revenue Canada regulations for a cumulative total of more than five (5) years.

answer:
According to Article 10.07 of the Collective Agreement 2017-2020, the President must ensure that the annual academic workload is determined, distributed, and scheduled as equitably as possible.

Specifically, the member's assigned annual academic workload must take into account the four domains of activity indicated in 10.01 and factors such as:

* The needs of the member's program, including student enrolments
* The necessity of offering required courses

Additionally, Article 5.35 states that new hires (appointments effective July 1 or before the signing of a new Collective Agreement) shall receive all increases in salary for that year that become effective July 1, except for certain increments explicitly excluded by the new Collective Agreement.

question: What are the rules concerning annual report for members?
answer:
According to Article 10.08 of the Collective Agreement, all full-time members of the Bargaining Unit shall submit a written Report on their activities for the preceding twelve months, from May 1st to April 30th, to the President by June 22nd, with a copy to their department chairs. The report is expected to cover all components of members' activities as described in Article 10, Academic Activity.

In preparing their Annual Report, members are required to:

* Use the standardized form approved by the University of Sudbury Senate and provided by the Registrar (in the case of previous agreements).
* Provide an up-to-date C.V. with their Annual Report.

It is also mentioned that department chairs are not expected to evaluate the report.

question: What does the collective agreement provide regarding workload?
answer:
According to Article 5.40 of the Collective Agreement 2017-2020:

1. The academic workload shall be assigned in a fair and equitable manner.
2. Each member of a Department/School shall receive a copy of the Chair's/Director's recommendations to the Dean/University Librarian on their own workload and a summary of the recommendations on all other Members in the Department/School, including any recommendations for overloads, prior to the recommendations being forwarded to the Dean/University Librarian.    * teaching/professional librarianship/archives management, including the supervision of graduate and undergraduate students (40%)

Additionally, the collective agreement also considers factors such as the capabilities of the Members, the need to maximize their potential, and any obligations placed on them within the University's operations when assigning workload.

question: What does the collective agreement provide regarding academic freedom?
answer:
According to the Collective Agreement 2017-2020, Academic Freedom is a fundamental objective of the University, and it is essential to its teaching and research activities (0.02(a)). The Parties acknowledge their commitment to the pursuit of truth, the advancement of learning, and the creation, interpretation, preservation, and dissemination of knowledge.

In addition, the Collective Agreement provides that academic freedom includes:

* The freedom to carry out research and to publish its results
* The freedom to teach
* The freedom to discuss and criticize

However, it also makes clear that academic freedom does not confer legal immunity (1 of 66). Members have obligations to perform satisfactorily their duties and responsibilities in their capacity as professors of the University.

Furthermore, academic freedom carries the responsibility to respect the right of other members of the academic community - faculty, staff, and students - to express their opinions (e).

Lastly, the Employer shall not supervise or restrain, nor will it assume responsibility for restricting the expression of any member's opinions under the guise of protecting academic freedom.

question: What does the agreement say about pregnancy, parental and adoption?
answer:
The Collective Agreement 2011-14 mentions the following regarding pregnancy, parental, and adoption leaves:

* Pregnancy Leave:
	+ A pregnant full-time Member or pregnant Master Lecturer Member is entitled to 17 weeks of pregnancy leave (Article 7.60.1).
	+ During this period, the member receives from the Employer: 
		- 100% of their nominal salary for the first week.
		- An amount equal to the difference between EI benefits and 100% of their nominal salary for up to 16 additional weeks (Article 7.60.1(ii)).
	+ If the member is disentitled or disqualified from receiving EI benefits, the Employer maintains them at 100% of their nominal earnings.
* Parental Leave:
	+ A Member who is a parent and has opted to take parental leave under the Employment Insurance Act and applicable legislation is entitled to up to 35 weeks of parental leave (Article 7.60.5).
	+ During this period, the member receives from the Employer: 
		- 100% of their nominal salary for the first two weeks.
		- An amount equal to the difference between EI benefits and 100% of their nominal salary for up to seven additional weeks (Article 7.60.5(ii)).
	+ If the member is disentitled or disqualified from receiving EI benefits, the Employer maintains them at 100% of their nominal earnings.
* Adoption Leave:
	+ A Member who is a parent and has opted to take parental leave under the Employment Insurance Act and applicable legislation is entitled to up to 37 weeks of adoption leave (Article 7.60.6).
	+ The terms and conditions for adoption leave are similar to those for parental leave, with some minor differences.

Please note that Article 7.60 does not specifically mention "pregnancy, parental, and adoption" together in the same section. Instead, it has separate sections for each type of leave.

question: What are the rules concerning voluntary reduced workload?
answer:
Here are the main rules concerning Voluntary Reduced Workload:

1. Any full-time Member of the Bargaining Unit who has a minimum of two (2) years of continuous full-time service at the University may be granted up to 50% temporary reduction in workload with a proportionate reduction in salary and annual vacation entitlement, as outlined in Article 7.35.

2. The request for voluntary reduced workload must normally be made three (3) months in advance to the Department/School and the Dean/University Librarian.

3. The Dean/University Librarian approves the request, and approval shall not be unreasonably withheld.

4. Voluntary reduced workloads may be granted for periods longer than twelve (12) months and/or renewals of twelve (12) month reduction periods, subject to the Dean's/University Librarian's approval.

5. Faculty Members on voluntary reduced workload have the right to benefits and contribute to the benefits plan, as outlined in Article 7.35.

6. The temporary reduction is effective for a twelve (12) month period, but can be extended or renewed with the approval of the Dean/University Librarian.

7. For the application of tenure and promotion policies, periods of reduced workload are pro-rated in accordance with the reduction in workload.

8. Members on voluntary reduced workload retain both the right and obligation to contribute to administrative work at the University.

9. Evaluations of such activity by the Dean/University Librarian must recognize the reduced workload of the Member.

10. During the period of voluntary reduced workload, Members are expected to submit annual reports as per Article 5.45 – Annual Report for Members in order to qualify for Progress-Through-The-Ranks increments.

question: What are the rules concerning faculty personnel files?
answer:
According to Article 21 of the Collective Agreement, there are specific rules regarding faculty personnel files:

1. Official personnel files of a member shall be kept by the President and are the property of the Employer (Article 21.01).
2. Members have the right to examine all of their personnel files upon making prior arrangements to do so (Article 21.02). Material in the files that is to be held confidential will be removed from the files prior to inspection, but an inventory of this confidential material will be provided to the member.
3. There are two types of files for Members: active files and archival files. Active files contain only information allowed under the Article, while archival files contain material that has been banned for use in subsequent proceedings (Article 5.70.1).
4. Members have the right to examine their personnel files during normal business hours, after notice in writing, in the presence of the Dean/University Librarian or a person authorized by the Dean/University Librarian (Article 5.70.2).
5. Confidential material will be removed from the files prior to inspection, but an inventory of this confidential material will be provided to the member.
6. Members have the right to request the Vice-President, Academic and Provost to provide one (1) copy of their personnel file, excluding confidential material, within five (5) working days at no charge to the Member (Article 5.70.3).
7. No anonymous material concerning any Member shall be kept by the Employer for inclusion in the Member's personnel file (Article 5.70.4).
8. Members have the right to have all of their files supplemented or corrected in the event of error, or inadequacy (Article 5.70.5).

It is also worth noting that there are specific limitations on the use of faculty personnel files, including:

* Letters of assessments received in relation to the appointment of a Member shall be confidential and not used as evidence in any subsequent proceedings (Article 4.55.1).
* Student evaluations shall not be admissible as evidence in any process involving a Member's tenure, promotion, or dismissal if such evaluations are more than five (5) years old (Article 4.55.6).

Overall, the rules regarding faculty personnel files aim to balance the employer's need for information with the employee's right to privacy and control over their personal records.

question: What is stated about academic freedom?
answer:
According to the provided text, academic freedom is defined as the right to:

* Search for truth, knowledge, and understanding
* Express freely what one believes
* Carry out research and disseminate its results
* Teach without deference to prescribed doctrine
* State professional views on matters relating to their discipline
* Discuss and criticize both the University and the wider society
* Engage in service to the institution and the community
* Express one's opinion about the University, its administration, and the system in which one works

Academic freedom also entails:

* The right to exercise civil liberties as individuals, including contributing to social change through free expression on matters of public interest
* The protection of privacy, consistent with the traditions of Academic Freedom and the provisions of this Article

However, academic freedom does not confer legal immunity and requires the acknowledgement of the work of others and the acceptance of responsibility for one's own beliefs and utterances.

question: What does the collective agreement provide regarding beneficiary procedures?
answer:
The Collective Agreement 2017-2020 (page 8.80) provides the following regarding beneficiary procedures:

* The beneficiary is required to contact the Pension and Benefits Officer in the Personnel Office within seven days of the University's death.
* If the University has not been contacted by the beneficiary within this timeframe, the University will make every reasonable effort to contact the beneficiary.
* To request payment of life insurance proceeds, the beneficiary must provide:
  * A completed Statement required by the insurance carrier
  * The beneficiary's Social Insurance Number
  * Notice of the Employee's death from Obituary Notices
  * A Death Certificate
  * The last insurance certificate issued to the faculty member

Additionally, if the Member dies prior to receiving a pension, the following procedures must be followed:

* The University contacts the Beneficiary and outlines the procedures to be followed.
* The Beneficiary completes an "Application for Death Benefit".
* Provides a Death Certificate.
* Provides a "notarial copy" of the Employee's Last Will and Testament.

It is also stated that all Members should have a current Last Will and Testament, and beneficiaries without one may need to settle disputes between potential beneficiaries in court before receiving funds from the Pension Plan.

question: What does the collective agreement provide regarding discipline?
answer:
The Collective Agreement provides detailed guidelines for discipline in Article 5.60 - DISCIPLINARY MEASURES. According to the agreement, discipline shall be just and reasonable, based on the principle of progressive discipline, except in egregious cases (Article 5.75.2).

The forms of discipline that may be taken by the Employer against a Member are specified as follows:

* A formal reprimand in writing to the Member, specifying the grounds and adding this reprimand to the personnel file of the Member concerned (Article 4.60.1(a))
* The suspension without pay of a Member for a period of one to five, ten, fifteen or twenty working days (Article 4.60.3(b))

It is also mentioned that certain forms of disciplinary measures are not permissible, such as withholding an annual increment (Article 4.60.2), and that the annual increment should not be used as a form of disciplinary measure (Article 4.60.2).

Additionally, the Collective Agreement specifies the types of behavior that constitute just cause for disciplinary measures, including:

* Serious unprofessional behaviour
* Failure to comply with any of the provisions of this Agreement

The agreement also emphasizes the importance of principles of natural justice and due process in imposing discipline, and guarantees a Member's right to know the nature of allegations against them and to respond (Article 5.75.4).

question: What does the collective agreement provide regarding retirement?
answer:
Based on the provided context, I can answer that the collective agreement provides for several aspects of retirement:

1. Phased retirement: The collective agreement outlines a program for phased retirement over three years, which was instituted on July 1, 2006 ( Appendix D, Section 1).
2. Pension portability: The agreement states that proposed members hired after September 24, 2017, will not have the option to commute the value of their pension benefit upon retirement or resignation (Section 5.90.5).
3. Special Voluntary Early Retirement Plan: This plan is available for a four-year period from July 1, 2008 to June 30, 2012, and provides benefits such as life insurance, dental plan, hospital care, extended medical, and retiree privileges (Sections 16-18 of the Collective Agreement 2008-11).
4. Eligibility for CPP benefits: Members who are at least 60 years old may be eligible for full or partial CPP benefits, provided they have contributed to the plan (Section 16 of the Collective Agreement 2011-14).

Please note that these provisions may have been modified or updated in subsequent collective agreements.

question: What are the rules concerning redundancy?
answer:
According to Article 10.10 of the Collective Agreement, redundancies may be justified only for bona fide academic reasons and/or on the grounds of insufficient student demand.

The rules governing redundancies are as follows:

1. A declaration of redundancy by the Employer must be made in writing, specifying the reasons why the redundancy is justified and the magnitude of the reduction believed to be necessary.
2. The declaration must be approved by the Senate (Article 10.10.3(a)) or a submission by the Vice-President, Academic and Provost that a Department or School has an excessive number of members relative to its workload (Article 10.10.3(b)).
3. The onus is on the Employer to show that the proposed reductions are consistent with normal workloads as defined in Article 5.40-Academic Workload.
4. Redundancies may not be justified if they would create an inequitable workload for the Department or School affected by the redundancies.
5. If insufficient student demand is used as a justification, the lack of demand must be demonstrable over a period of at least three (3) years and projections into the future must not indicate any appreciable increase in this student demand (Article 10.10.4).
6. A Redundancy Committee will be formed to make recommendations on the redundancies. The committee will consist of three members chosen by the Union, three individuals named by the Employer, and the Vice-President, Academic and Provost as non-voting Chair (Article 10.10.6).

question: What does the collective agreement provide regarding academic workload?
answer:
According to Article 10.07 of the Collective Agreement 2017-2020, the President must ensure that the annual academic workload is determined, distributed, and scheduled as equitably as possible. The member's assigned annual academic workload must take into account the four domains of activity indicated in 10.01 and the factors mentioned in the Preamble, such as the needs of the member's program (including student enrolments) and the necessity of offering required courses.

Additionally, Article 5.35 states that newly hired members will receive all increases in salary for the year, except for PTR increment, merit increment, or other explicitly excluded increases, regardless of the actual date of commencement of employment.

Source: Collective Agreement 2017-2020, Articles 10.07 and 5.35.

question: How is health, safety and security addressed in the collective agreement?

* Charging $15 per card for replacement of computer equipment (3.20.5)
* Providing a standard computer in members' offices every 4 years, without charge to the member and department/school (3.20.5)

These provisions demonstrate the collective agreement's commitment to addressing health, safety, and security concerns in the workplace.

question: How does the agreement define or describe arbitration procedure?
answer:
According to the Collective Agreement 2008-11, the arbitration procedure is defined in Article 12.15 and Article 11.15. The key points are:

* If no written request for arbitration is received within 30 working days after the decision of the Vice-President, Academic and Provost or the Union President under Step 2 – Formal Grievance Procedure, the grievance shall be deemed to have been abandoned (Article 12.15.1(a)).
* When either Party requests that any matter be submitted to Arbitration as provided in this Article, it shall make such request in writing addressed to the other Party of this Collective Agreement, and at the same time propose an Abritrator (Article 11.15.1(b)).
* The other Party shall appoint its nominee within 15 working days thereafter, or the Minister of Labour for Ontario shall have the power to make such appointment upon application thereto by the Party invoking the arbitration procedure.
* If the two nominees are unable to agree on a chairperson of the Arbitration Board, they shall attempt to do so (Article 11.15.1(b)).
* The grievance may be submitted to arbitration as provided in Article 24 if no written notice of referral to arbitration is received within 35 working days after the decision under Step 2 has been communicated to the Association (Article 12.15.3).

Additionally, Article 11.15.1(a) states that failing settlement and/or timely response under the foregoing grievance procedure, any grievance may then be submitted to arbitration as hereinafter provided under its own distinct arbitral procedure.

It's worth noting that there are two separate articles (12.15 and 11.15) describing the arbitration procedure in different contexts.
